HubSpot help: automation, data and reporting

This guide holds HubSpot’s own help for automating work and understanding data, gathered from knowledge.hubspot.com in November 2026: workflows and sequences, importing, cleaning and syncing data, and reports, dashboards and analytics.

HubSpot’s knowledge base is too large for one guide, so this collection splits it by HubSpot’s own top categories into four: HubSpotAccount.md for account setup, getting started, its AI tools and partners; HubSpotCrm.md for the CRM, sales, service and revenue tools; HubSpotData.md for automation, data and reporting; and HubSpotMarketing.md for marketing and content. The categories are HubSpot’s own, from the trail above each article. Android-only articles are left out, as this collection covers Windows, the web, iPhone and iPad, and Alexa. HubSpot’s developer documentation is a separate site and is not here.

The help text belongs to its publisher and is gathered here unchanged for accessible reading. This guide’s own arrangement and wording are available under CC BY-SA 4.0.

Automation: Workflows

Add and update contacts in marketing events with workflows

Use the Add participant to marketing event workflow action to add contacts to and update the participant state of these contacts in manually created marketing events.

Please note: this action only works for marketing events created directly in HubSpot, including manually created events, and events created in other tools or by Breeze. It cannot be used for events synced via integrations.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow, or create a new workflow.
  • Click the + add icon to add a workflow action.
  • In the left panel, click to expand the Marketing section. Then, select Add participant to marketing event.
  • Configure your workflow action:
    • Contact: this will be set to the enrolled contact by default.
    • Marketing event: select your marketing event. This will only apply to marketing events created directly in HubSpot. Marketing events created from third-party integrations will not appear.
    • Mark contact as: the contact participant stage. You can select from Registered, Attended, or Cancelled.
    • Started attending at: the date and time the contact attended the event. This is an optional field.
    • Finished attending at: the date and time the contact completed the event. This is an optional field.
  • After setting up your workflow action, at the top, click Save.
  • Continue setting up your workflow.

Add comments to a workflow

Add comments to your workflow, enrollment triggers, and actions to collaborate with your team and ask for feedback. For example, you can comment on a delay to ask a colleague to confirm a workflow’s timing.

Comments can be added to workflow triggers and all workflow actions, including if/then branches. You can edit or delete a comment after adding it.

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to use the workflows tool.

Add a comment to a workflow action

To add a comment to an action in a workflow:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.

  • Click the name of the workflow.

  • Hover over the enrollment trigger box or action that you want to comment on. Then, click the comments comment icon.

  • In the comment field, type your comment. Use the rich text toolbar to format your text.

  • To notify a specific user or team of your comment, type the @ symbol, then enter the user or team name.

  • To save your comment, click Save or hit enter. Once a comment has been added to the enrollment trigger or action, the comment icon will display so that others know it has been commented on.

  • To edit or delete your comment, click the comments CCComment icon, then click Actions and select Edit or Delete. You can only edit or delete your own comments.

Add comments with the drag and drop collaboration sidebar

Use the drag and drop version of the collaboration sidebar in your workflows tool to add comments and work with your team. Learn more about adding comments to your HubSpot assets.

To use the drag and drop collaboration sidebar:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of the workflow.
  • Click and drag the collaboration sidebar along the edges of your editor to reposition it.
  • To comment on the collaboration sidebar, click the comments comment icon. By default, comment mode will be enabled. In this mode, you can add comments to your workflow actions.
  • To exit comment mode, in the top right, click the X icon.
  • To re-enter comment mode, in the right panel, click Comment mode.
  • To hide your comments, click More > Hide comments on screen. This will hide comments on workflow actions.
  • To add a general comment:
    • In the comment field, type your comment. Use the rich text toolbar to format your text.
    • To notify a specific user or team of your comment, type the @ symbol, then enter the user or team name.
    • To save your comment, click Comment.
    • To edit or delete a comment:
      • Hover over the comment you want to edit or delete.
      • In the top right of the comment, click Actions and select Edit or Delete. You can only edit or delete your own comments.
  • To exit the drag and drop collaboration sidebar, at the top of the right panel, click the X icon.

Add data to Airtable with workflows

Use the Add data to Airtable workflow action to automate sending your HubSpot data to Airtable. This workflow action enables you to create new rows of data in a new or existing Airtable database.

Permissions required Super Admin or Edit permissions for workflows are required to create and edit workflows.

Add data to Airtable with workflows

Before you can add data to Airtable with workflows, you’ll need to connect Airtable to your HubSpot account. Learn more about connecting apps within a workflow.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • To edit an existing workflow, hover over the workflow, then click Edit. Or create a new workflow.
  • In the workflow editor, click the + plus icon to add a workflow action.
  • In the left panel, select the Create Airtable row action.

.

  • Enter your Airtable row details:
    • Base: click the dropdown menu to select the Airtable base to add data to.
    • Table: select the table that you want to add rows to.
    • Header: select the row header.
    • Property: select the HubSpot property that you’ll be pulling information from. If there are previous actions in the workflow, you can also select from the outcomes of those actions.
  • To add multiple rows, select multiple Header and Property values.
  • To add the action to the workflow, at the top, click Save.

Add data to Google Sheets with workflows

Use the Create Google Sheet row action or Update data in a Google Sheet action to send data from HubSpot properties to your spreadsheet. For example, you can use this action to send contact data from new leads to a spreadsheet for your sales outreach team.

Before you can add data to Google Sheets with workflows, you’ll need to connect Google Sheets to your HubSpot account. You can connect the app from the App Marketplace or from within a workflow.

Before you get started

Permissions required Super Admin or Edit Workflows permissions are required to create and edit workflows.

Keep the following in mind when sending data to Google Sheets from HubSpot:

  • By default, HubSpot sends internal property values to Google Sheets. For dates, HubSpot sends unix timestamps in milliseconds.

    • If you have an Data Hub Professional subscription, you can format the date property into your desired format by adding a Format data action before the Create Google Sheets row action. Then, in the Property dropdown menu of the Google Sheets action, select the date output from the Format data action.
    • You can also convert dates from milliseconds in Google Sheets by adding the following formula to a separate column in the spreadsheet: =A1/1000/60/60/24 + DATE(1970,1,1). Replace A1 with the column that the unix timestamp is in.

  • When using the Create Google Sheet row action, data is not added to existing rows. Instead, the action inserts a new row into the sheet. This can affect referenced cells and any formulas used. To avoid this, ensure that only populated, existing rows are referenced. To add data to existing rows use the Update existing Google Sheet rows action.

  • Avoid manually adding data to the sheet that HubSpot is sending data to. If you need to manually add data to the spreadsheet, you should create a new sheet and reference existing data from the first sheet.

  • It is generally not recommended to use formulas in the Google Sheets that you’re updating. Updating cells in formula-heavy Google Sheets can result in slower action execution times or errors in the workflow.

    • Google Sheets automatically recalculates all dependent formulas whenever cells are modified. The larger and more formula-heavy the spreadsheet becomes, the longer each update operation will take to complete.
    • Instead, it’s recommended to use as few formulas as possible or to apply your formulas only after all updates to the spreadsheet.

  • It is not recommended to update the same sheet in multiple workflows as doing so can result in data duplication. Instead, it’s recommended to only use a single workflow for each sheet.

  • When selecting a spreadsheet in the workflow editor, the sheets available are tied to the sheets that the connecting user has access to. For a sheet to appear as an option, it must meet at least one of the following requirements:

    • Belong to the connecting user’s drive.
    • Previously shared with the connecting user.
    • Belong to a shared drive that the connecting user has access to.

  • If you disconnect the Google sheets integration and reconnect with another user, the sheets available may be different. It’s recommended that you check any dependent workflows before disconnecting and reconnecting.

Please note: at times, when adding data a request can time out and a duplicate row may be created. To resolve, the duplicate data can be deleted in your account.

Set up your spreadsheet

When setting up your spreadsheet, do take note of the following:

  • The header row must start in the first column of the first row.
  • Each column header should be labeled so that HubSpot can identify and send data to it. HubSpot cannot send data to unlabeled columns.
  • Ensure all columns in your table range have column headers. Avoid having blank column headers between columns as this can cause issues and prevent the spreadsheet from updating as expected. For example, if your spreadsheet uses columns A to C, do not leave the column B header blank.
  • The spreadsheet cannot exceed 5,000,000 cells.

Connect Google sheets to HubSpot

Before you can add data to Google Sheets with workflows, you’ll need to connect Google Sheets to your HubSpot account.

You can connect the app from the App Marketplace.

Add new Google Sheet rows

When using the Create Google Sheet row action to add data your Google sheet, ensure your spreadsheet has been correctly formatted. Aside from the header row, do not include any other data in the sheet you’re sending data to.

This action does not add data to existing rows. Instead, the action inserts a new row into the sheet. This can affect referenced cells and any formulas used. To avoid this, ensure that only populated, existing rows are referenced.

To add new Google Sheet rows:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • To edit an existing workflow, hover over the workflow, then click Edit. Or, create a new workflow.
  • In the workflow editor, click the + plus icon to add an action.
  • In the left panel, under Google Sheets, select Create Google Sheet row.
  • Click the Spreadsheet dropdown menu and select the spreadsheet you want to send data to. You can select from the spreadsheets that are owned by or have been shared with the user who connected Google Sheets to HubSpot.
  • Click the Sheet dropdown menu and select the sheet you want to send data to. The Sheet field refers to the tabs at the bottom of your spreadsheet.
  • Set up your Google sheet column header and corresponding HubSpot property. HubSpot will add data to empty rows below any existing data in the sheet. Each action can add up to 20 cells of data per row.
    • Click the Header dropdown menu and select the Google sheet column header to send the data to.
    • Click the Property dropdown menu and select the corresponding HubSpot property you’ll send data from.
  • After setting up your workflow action, click Save.

Update existing Google Sheet rows

When using the Update existing Google Sheet rows action, ensure your spreadsheet has been correctly formatted.

This action will update data that is in your Google Sheet. By default, no additional rows will be added to your Google Sheet, only existing rows will be updated.

To update your existing Google Sheet rows:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • To edit an existing workflow, hover over the workflow, then click Edit. Or, create a new workflow.
  • In the workflow editor, click the + plus icon to add an action.
  • In the left panel, select Update data in a Google Sheet.
  • Click the Spreadsheet dropdown menu and select the spreadsheet you want to send data to. You can select from the spreadsheets that are owned by or have been shared with the user who connected Google Sheets to HubSpot.
  • Click the Sheet dropdown menu and select the sheet you want to send data to. The Sheet field refers to the tabs at the bottom of your spreadsheet.
  • Set up unique identifiers to match the data in Google Sheets to the data in HubSpot. When the value of a cell in the selected Lookup column header matches the value of the selected HubSpot property for the enrolled record, the row containing the matching cell will be updated. If there are multiple rows with matching values, only the first row containing the matching cell will be updated.
    • Click the Lookup column header dropdown menu and select a column header in the spreadsheet. This should correspond to a HubSpot property to use as a unique identifier for the update. For example, a unique identifier could be a contact’s email address because it is unique to them.
    • Click the Lookup column property dropdown menu and select a property corresponding to the Lookup column header to use as an identifier for the update.
  • In the create a new row if none match dropdown menu:
    • If you want to create a new row if there is no matching Lookup column header and Lookup column property, click Yes. This will create a new row containing only properties set in the Select columns to update section.
    • If you do not want to create a new row if there is no matching Lookup column header and Lookup column property, click No.
  • Set up the columns in the spreadsheet that you want to update:
    • Click the Select columns to update dropdown menu, a list of column headers from the selected spreadsheet will display. Then, select the column that you want to update.
    • Click the dropdown menu under the column header and select an option. You can either choose to update the data with an existing property value from the enrolled record or with the outcome of an earlier workflow action.
    • To add another column to update, click Add a column.
    • To delete a column, click the delete detedelete icon next to the column header.
  • Click Save.

Troubleshoot errors when using Google Sheets with HubSpot

If you’re unable to locate a specific sheet or encountering an error when setting up your workflow actions, it is recommendeded to check the following:

  • Confirm that the spreadsheet has not been updated. It is recommended to check for the following:
    • The spreadsheet still exists and has not been deleted.
    • The correct sheet tab is selected.
    • The mapped headers are present.
    • The header row starts in cell A1.
    • There are no blank column headers in the table range.
  • If the sheet is large or formula-heavy, test with a simpler sheet or reduce formulas before retrying the action.
  • If the user account used to connect to Google Sheets is still valid. For example, if the user has been deactivated in the HubSpot, you may encounter the following error: “Spreadsheet” options could not load due to 3rd-party API failure.

Generally, to resolve Google Sheet workflow action issues, it is recommended to disconnect your Google sheets integration and reconnect the integration using an active HubSpot user and a Google account that has access to the sheets that you’d like to update.

Add data variables to workflow actions

Depending on the selected workflow action, you can use the data panel to insert data variables from various object sources.

For example, you can use data from a contact record and its associated deal to send an internal notification email that contains personalization tokens from both records.

Before you get started

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to use the workflows tool.

  • By default, additional data sources will be automatically added to contact, company, deal, and ticket-based workflows.
  • You can add up to 50 data sources per workflow.
  • Custom event properties can be used for actions that are supported by the data panel. The available custom event properties will be displayed under the name of the custom event in the data panel.

Add data variables to workflow actions

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.

  • Click the name of a workflow. Or, create a new workflow.

  • In the workflow editor, click the + Add icon to add a new action.

  • After selecting your action, in the left panel, click on the field that you’d like to use the data with.

  • In the Choose data variable section, click Edit available data.

  • To create a new data source, in the right panel, click + Add records.

  • In the Name your data source field, enter a name for your data source.

  • Click the Choose a record type dropdown menu and select a data source.

  • Click the Choose a condition to filter [data source record type] dropdown menu and select from the following:

    • If associated to the enrolled record: use data from associated records. For example, in a contact-based workflow, you can use data from an associated company record.
      • Association label: select the association label you’d like to refine the associated records by, especially if you have more than one associated record of the same record type. Learn more about association labels.

  • .

    • If property values match: use data from records with matching property values. For example, in a deal-based workflow, you can refine only companies where the domain property’s value matches the domain property’s value of an enrolled contact.
      • All records in your CRM are reviewed to find a matching property: choose a property from the selected record type to match with the enrolled record.
      • Has the same value as: choose a property from your enrolled record.
    • If a property value is equal to: use data from records with specific property values. It is generally recommended to use this option if you’re using a custom property to store unique identifiers. For example, you can choose only custom objects where the Listing ID role property has a value of ABC12345.
      • All records in your CRM are reviewed to find a matching property: choose a property from your selected record type to refine by.
      • Is equal to: select or enter a property value, only records with the specific property value will be selected.

  • Click the Choose a condition to filter [record type] down to one dropdown menu and select from Most recently updated, Most recently created, or First created.

  • Configure the data source details, then click Add at the bottom.

  • After adding a data source, to review or delete an existing data sources:

    • In the Choose data variable section, click Edit available data. In the right panel, review all added data sources.
    • To review more details about an existing data source, click the eye icon.
    • To delete an existing data source, click the delete icon.

  • After adding your data sources, use data from a specific source:

    • In the Insert data panel, click the View properties or action output from dropdown menu and select a data source.
    • After selecting your source, click to expand the data type that you’d like to use, then click on the property to use in the field. The property will be automatically inserted into the field.

Add line items to deals using workflows

Use the Add line item to deal workflow action to associate specific products with deals in workflows. For example, you may want to automatically add a line item to a deal whenever the deal reaches a specific stage in your deal pipeline, or if a specific form has been submitted.

Before you get started

When using the Add line item to deal workflow action, do note the following:

  • This action is only available in deal-based workflows.
  • The action can only be used to add existing products to deals. It cannot edit or replace currently associated products.

Add line items to deals using workflows

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of an existing deal-based workflow or create a new deal-based workflow.
  • Set your enrollment triggers.
  • Click the + plus icon to add an action.
  • In the left panel, click to expand the CRM section. Then, click Add line item to deal.
  • Configure the Add line item to deal action:
    • Deal: choose to associate the line items with the enrolled deal or a different associated deal.
    • Product: select the line item that you’d like to associate with the deal. Learn more about creating and managing products.
    • Quantity: select the number of products that you’d like to associate with the deal.
  • After setting up your action, at the top, click Save.
  • Continue setting up your workflow.

Add re-enrollment triggers to a workflow

Use re-enrollment in your workflow to enroll records in a workflow again. By default, records are only enrolled in workflows the first time they meet the workflow enrollment triggers or are enrolled manually. Re-enrollment triggers allow records to be re-enrolled in your workflows.

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to use the workflows tool.

How re-enrollment triggers work

When setting up your re-enrollment triggers, take note of the following:

  • Whether you can use an enrollment trigger for re-enrollment depends on the type of trigger and operator. The following rules apply to all workflow types:
    • In general, properties can only be used for re-enrollment when they’re the same type as the workflow. For example, in company-based workflows, you can only re-enroll using company properties.
    • Activities and activity properties cannot be used for re-enrollment in any type of workflow.
    • Not all enrollment triggers can be used for re-enrollment. Learn more about the available re-enrollment triggers.
  • When re-enrollment is turned on, records can re-enroll in workflows either by manual re-enrollment or by meeting at least one selected re-enrollment trigger.

    • Records that have already completed the workflow will only re-enroll if they meet the initial enrollment criteria and meet a selected re-enrollment trigger again after re-enrollment is turned on.

    • It is not possible to use AND criteria when setting up re-enrollment. Records that meet at least one re-enrollment trigger will automatically re-enroll.

    • Records that are manually re-enrolled do not have to meet the initial enrollment triggers or re-enrollment triggers to enroll.

    • If re-enrollment is turned off, records that were previously enrolled cannot be enrolled again, including through manual or automatic enrollment.

    • Turning on re-enrollment will not retroactively enroll new records. To enroll records that have not previously enrolled in the workflow, learn how to manually enroll records instead.

  • A record won’t re-enroll in a workflow while it’s already enrolled. Re-enrollment can only happen after the record is manually unenrolled from or has exited the workflow.
  • When using the property filter is known for re-enrollment, in addition to meeting the criteria above, records can re-enroll in two ways:
    • The property gains a value after not previously having one.
    • The property is updated from one value to another. For example, a contact’s lifecycle stage changing from Lead to Subscriber would qualify for Lifecycle stage is known. Each time this contact’s lifecycle stage is updated, they would re-enroll in the workflow, provided the contact also meets the workflow’s initial enrollment triggers.
  • Records will re-enroll each time they are updated from not matching to matching a re-enrollment trigger. For example, if a re-enrollment trigger is based on segment membership, a contact will re-enroll when they join the segment:
    • If the contact stays in the segment, they will not re-enroll each time they finish the workflow.
    • If the contact leaves the segment, they will re-enroll in the workflow once they join that segment again.
  • When a record is re-enrolled in a workflow, they will start the workflow again from the beginning and complete all workflow actions again (e.g., receiving any automated emails).
  • While enrollment triggers can be refined by date or number, refinement won’t apply to re-enrollment. For example:
    • Date: your workflow has the enrollment trigger Contact has filled out Any form submission on Homepage between 1/1/2019 and 2/1/2019. The date range will not be taken into account for re-enrollment. Instead, contacts will re-enroll any time they submit that form, even if it’s outside the date range.
    • Number: your workflow has the enrollment trigger Contact has filled out any form on Any page at most 5 times. The number of times a contact has filled out your forms will not be taken into account for re-enrollment. Instead, contacts will re-enroll any time they submit that form.
  • If a workflow contains an action of Enroll in another workflow, records will still re-enroll if they meet re-enrollment criteria.
  • For a re-enrollment to occur based on a relative-date-based criteria (e.g., is today), the relative-date-based criteria must be true at the time the property associated with that criteria changes. For example, if a re-enrollment criteria is set to is today for a relative-date-based-property and the property was changed on a record on July 27th and set to Aug. 1st, the record won’t be re-enrolled.

Add re-enrollment triggers to contact-based workflows

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of a contact-based workflow.
  • Click the Contact enrollment trigger box.

.

  • In the left panel, click the Re-enrollment tab.
  • Click to toggle the Allow contacts to re-enroll after completing the workflow switch on.
  • Under Re-enroll contacts if they meet the trigger criteria and any of the following occurs to, select the checkboxes next to the triggers you want to use for re-enrollment. For example, for form submissions, you must select the checkbox for the specific form-submission condition. If not, automatic re-enrollment for the form submission will not occur, even when re-enrollment is turned on. Learn more about which triggers can be used for re-enrollment.
  • When you’re done, click Save. If you’re updating a published workflow, in the dialog box, select from the following options:
    • Save and enroll existing [object]: select this option to enroll all existing records that meet the updated trigger criteria, If re-enrollment is turned on, any records that may have previously enrolled in this workflow will be enrolled again.
    • Save and don’t enroll existing [object]: select this option to only enroll records that meet the trigger criteria moving forward. If this workflow has been turned on for some time, this is recommended to avoid unexpected re-enrollments. For example, if the workflow sends SMS messages, this can help avoid sending repeated messages.

Add re-enrollment triggers to other workflow types

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.

  • Click the name of the non-cantact-based workflow, such as a company or deal-based workflow.

  • Click the enrollment trigger box.

  • In the left panel, click the Settings tab.

  • Click to toggle the Re-enroll switch on.

  • Select the checkboxes next to the triggers you want to use for re-enrollment.

  • At the top, click Save.

If your workflow is currently turned on, a dialog box will appear with the message Do you want to enroll existing [object-type]. If the workflow has been turned on for some time, you may want to select the option Save and don’t enroll existing [object-type] to avoid re-enrollments. For example, if the workflow sends SMS messages to associated contacts, this can help avoid sending repeated messages.

Re-enrollment will only apply with the specific trigger checkboxes selected in your enrollment settings. When a record that has previously completed in the workflow meets the selected triggers again, they will enroll in the workflow again.

Available re-enrollment triggers

The following rules will apply to all workflow types:

  • Generally, properties can only be used for re-enrollment when they’re the same type as the workflow. For example, in deal-based workflows, you can only re-enroll using deal properties.
  • Activities and activity properties cannot be used for re-enrollment in any type of workflow.
  • It’s not recommended to use today’s date as a re-enrollment trigger. In general, this will not re-enroll the record, unless the property has been updated and the value is met again after not having been met. Instead, it is recommended to set up the workflow using recurring Based on a schedule enrollment triggers instead.

Below are enrollment triggers that can be used for re-enrollment. The listed triggers may not be exhaustive. To check whether or not a current enrollment trigger can be used for re-enrollment:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of the workflow.
  • Click the Enrollment triggers box.
  • In the right panel, click the Re-enrollment tab.

Any enrollment conditions that can’t be used for re-enrollment will be listed in the The following enrollment conditions can’t be used for re-enrollment section.

.

Please note:

  • Re-enrollment based on Last modified date is known is not supported.
  • From September 10, 2024, re-enrollment based on Now in workflow property is no longer supported. Existing workflows that use the Now in workflow property for re-enrollment will not be affected.
Contact-based workflows

The following cannot be used as re-enrollment triggers in contact-based workflows:

  • Privacy consent events cannot be used for re-enrollment.
  • Calculation properties, including default calculated properties such as Recent Conversion and Number of unique forms submitted cannot be used for re-enrollment.
  • Re-enrollment triggers cannot be refined by date or number. Learn more about how refinement filters apply to re-enrollment.
  • The is any of, is equal to all of, and is equal to any of operators cannot be used for re-enrollment if they have multiple values. For example, a single trigger of Field of study is equal to any of Neurosurgery or Catsitting cannot be used for re-enrollment. Instead, you can split it into two triggers of Field of study is equal to any of Neurosurgery OR Field of study is equal to any of Catsitting.
  • Activities and activity properties cannot be used for re-enrollment.

In contact-based workflows, the following triggers can be used for re-enrollment:

  • Contact properties can be used for re-enrollment when paired with certain operators:

    • Any contact properties using is known.

    • Single-line text, multi-line text properties using is equal to any of.

    • Text, number, and date properties using is equal to.

    • Single checkbox, dropdown select, and radio select properties using is any of.

    • Multiple checkbox properties using is equal to all of.

  • Contact is a member of segment

  • Contact has filled out form

  • Contact has viewed as least one URL equal to

  • Contact has viewed at least one URL containing

  • Contact has completed event

  • Any integration triggers, including Mailchimp and Zoom

Other workflow types

In other non-contact-based workflow types:

  • You can only trigger re-enrollment using properties specific to the workflow object. For example, in a company-based workflow, you can only re-enroll based on company properties.
  • Activities and segments cannot be used for re-enrollment.

Only the following property operators can be used for re-enrollment:

  • is any of
  • is none of
  • is equal to
  • is not equal to
  • has ever contained exactly
  • is greater than
  • is greater than or equal to
  • is less than
  • Is less than x days ago
  • is less than x days from now
  • is more than x days ago
  • is more than x days from now
  • updated in the last x days
  • not updated in the last x days
  • is before date
  • is after date
  • is between
  • is not between
  • is known
  • contains exactly
  • doesn’t contain exactly
  • starts with
  • ends with

When using any of the following filters for re-enrollment, special rules apply:

  • Is less than x days ago
  • is less than x days from now
  • is more than x days ago
  • is more than x days from now
  • updated in the last x days
  • not updated in the last x days

If a record is enrolled in a workflow within the specified timeframe, they will not re-enroll if they are updated again within the specified timeframe. Once the specified amount of time has passed after enrollment, the record is eligible for re-enrollment.

For example:

  • Your workflow is set to re-enroll companies when they meet the criteria Lifecycle stage has been updated in the last 5 days.
  • A company enrolls in the workflow after their lifecycle stage updates to Customer.
  • Three days later, the company’s lifecycle stage is updated again.
  • The company will not re-enroll in the workflow, because 3 days is still within the original 5-day window from when it enrolled.
  • A week later, the company’s lifecycle stage is updated to Evangelist.
  • The company will then re-enroll in the workflow, because the original 5 days have passed since enrollment.

Analyze workflow performance and opportunities

You can review and analyze the overall enrollment data and any additional opportunities for automating more processes on the Analyze tab of the workflows tool. This data can help you drill down on chances to use automation and streamline your team’s critical processes. To review the overall health of your workflows, learn how to use the workflows health page.

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to use the workflows tool.

Analyze workflow performance and opportunities

To review and analyze workflow performance data:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the Analyze tab.
  • At the top of the page, you can filter reports by:
    • Compare: click the dropdown menu to switch between comparison views:
      • Compare groups of workflows: compare workflows by type (e.g., Deleted, Needs review, Unused, or All workflows).
      • Compare workflows: compare specific workflows by click the Choose the individual Workflows dropdown menu and selecting the checkbox next to a workflow you want to be included in the data you’re analyzing.
    • For the date range: filter by this week, this month, the last 30 days, last month, this quarter, this year, or a custom time period.
    • Comparing the past two: click the dropdown menu to select the time period to compare different workflows against. For example, you can compare between Weeks, Months, or Quarters.
  • You can click Clear filters at the top of the page to reset all filters to their defaults.
  • Review your reports:

    • The top two reports that outline enrollment data across your workflows.

    • The next two reports that chart enrollment data over time, you can click the filter icon to edit the report and change the Data frequency.

    • The last two reports document opportunities to automate or create more workflows.

Assign and rotate record owners using workflows

Use the Rotate record to owner workflow action to assign records to your paid sales and service users. You can use this action to assign users on the record owner property or any custom HubSpot user property.

If you’re using the Rotate record to owner workflow action to assign ticket or lead (BETA) records, you can use additional distribution options, such as load balanced, round robin, and random.

Understand requirements and considersations

When using the Rotate record to owner workflow action, the following requirements and limitations will apply.

Understand requirements

Seats required When assigning users with this action, users must have paid sales or service seats. Learn more about managing paid seats.

  • When assigning records to specific users:
    • Users must be active with an assigned Sales or Service Hub Professional or Enterprise seat.
    • Users with core and view-only seats, or who have not accepted the invite to join the HubSpot account, will be greyed out.
  • When assigning records to a team:
    • The team must have at least one user with an assigned Sales or Service Hub Professional or Enterprise seat. If not, the team will be greyed out when setting up the workflow action.
    • Only main team members with an assigned Sales or Service Hub Professional or Enterprise seat will be eligible for assignment. Extra team members will not be included.
    • If an account is opted into the Support Multiple Main Teams for Full Functionality beta, all team members will be eligible for assignment.
  • Deactivated users or users who no longer have a paid seat will show in routing rules with a red border and will not be included in assignments.
Understand considerations
  • If the HubSpot owner property syncs to Salesforce, the action may not work as expected. Salesforce may try to update HubSpot with the previous owner even after HubSpot clears ownership.
  • When assigning leads using this action, you’ll need to turn off the Sync lead owner with contact or company owner setting.

Workflow assignment distribution

When using the Rotate record to owner workflow action, the following workflow assignment distribution rules will apply to most record types. These do not not apply to lead or ticket-based workflows.

  • By default, when distributing enrolled records, records will be assigned to users equally within a selected team or between specified users.
  • If there is no eligible user to rotate to, or if no team is selected for team-based assignment, no owner will be assigned.
  • If you add or remove owners from the action after your workflow has been turned on:
    • The assignment counts for that action will reset and the random assignments will start again.
    • Newly enrolled records will be rotated to all the selected owners or team members evenly, regardless of the rotation assignment counts for previously enrolled records.
  • HubSpot will only allow one object to be rotated at a time to ensure fairness in distribution.
    • If multiple objects are in the rotate object action at the same time, only one will be allowed through while the others retry.
    • This can result in objects taking longer to move through this action.
Assign records using workflows

To assign records using the Rotate record to owner action in a workflow:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow or create a new workflow.
  • Set your enrollment triggers.
  • Click the + plus icon to add an action.
  • In the left panel, click to expand the CRM section. Then, click Rotate record to owner.
  • Configure your Rotate record to owner action:
    • HubSpot user property: select the user property that you’d like to use with the action. By default, the [object] owner property will be selected. You can also use any other custom user properties.
    • Overwrite if [object] has an existing owner: choose whether to overwrite existing user property values.
    • Rotate between: select whether to rotate between specific users or teams.
      • Specific users: select the specific users for assigning records to.
      • Teams: select the specific team for assigning records to.
  • After setting up your workflow, at the top, click Save.
  • Continue setting up your workflow.

Additional distribution options

When assigning leads (BETA), deals (BETA), or tickets to specific users and teams using the Rotate record to owner action, you can use the following distribution options:

  • Load Balanced: automatically evaluate and assign the record to the user with the least amount of open, assigned tickets.
  • Round Robin: assign records in a rotating, sequential order.
  • Random: assign records randomly to eligible users in the assignment pool.
Assign leads or deals (BETA) using workflows

Subscription required A Sales Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to assign and rotate leads or deals using workflows.

To assign leads or deals (BETA) using the Rotate record to owner action in a workflow:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of an existing lead-based workflow or create a new workflow.
  • Set your enrollment triggers.
  • Click the + plus icon to add an action.
  • In the left panel, click to expand the CRM section. Then, click Rotate record to owner.
  • Configure your Rotate record to owner workflow action for tickets:
    • Owner property: this will be set to Lead Owner by default. You can also select any other lead user properties.
    • [Object] assignment: select from the following:
      • Specific users and teams: assign incoming records to specified users or teams. You can select from load balanced, round robin, or random distribution types.
      • Contact owner: assign incoming records to a contact’s owner.
        • The contact must have an owner assigned to their record and be tracked with a cookie.
        • If there’s no contact owner or if the assignment fails, the fallback option will be used. It is strongly recommended to add a user for the fallback option to prevent unassigned tasks or unaddressed internal notifications.
        • No one: incoming records will not be assigned to any team members.
  • After setting your assignment type, set your assignment configurations:
    • Overwrite any existing [object] owner: overwrite any existing record owners with a new record owner based on the assignment rules.
    • Assign to available users only: users that are set to Away will not be assigned records, even if they are configured in the assignment rules. Only available users will be assigned tickets. If all users in the assignment pool are away, the [object] Owner or Custom user property will be set to unassigned or (No owner).
  • At the top, click Save.
  • Continue setting up your workflow.

.

Assign tickets using workflows

Subscription required A Service Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to assign and rotate tickets using workflows.

To assign tickets using the Rotate record to owner action in a workflow:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of an existing ticket-based workflow or create a new workflow.
  • Set your enrollment triggers.
  • Click the + plus icon to add an action.
  • In the left panel, click to expand the CRM section. Then, click Rotate record to owner.
  • Configure your Rotate record to owner workflow action for tickets:
    • Owner property: this will be set to Ticket owner by default. You can also select any other ticket user properties.
    • Ticket assignment: select from the following:
      • Customer agent: incoming tickets will be routed to the customer agent. Learn more about setting up a customer agent.
      • Specific users and teams: assign incoming tickets to specified users or teams. You can select from load balanced, round robin, or random distribution types.
      • Team only: route incoming tickets to teams without assigning a ticket owner.
        • Tickets will appear in team-based views in help desk, including My Team’s Unassigned and My Team’s Open.
        • Only teams with at least one user with a Service Hub seat can be selected for team routing.
      • Contact owner: assign incoming tickets to a contact’s owner.
        • The contact must have an owner assigned to their record and be tracked with a cookie.
        • If there’s no contact owner or if the assignment fails, the fallback option will be used.
      • No one: incoming tickets will not be assigned to any team members.
  • After setting your assignment type, set your assignment configurations:
    • Overwrite any existing ticket owner: overwrite any existing ticket owners with a new ticket owner based on the assignment rules.
    • Assign to available users only: users that are set to Away will not be assigned tickets, even if they are configured in the assignment rules. Only available users will be assigned tickets. If all users in the assignment pool are away:
      • The Ticket Owner or Custom user property will be set to unassigned or (No owner).
      • The Assigned Teams ticket property will be set to all of the target teams from the routing options.
  • At the top, click Save.
  • Continue setting up your workflow.

Associate records based on existing associations with workflows

Create associations between records based on an intermediary record. When a record is already associated to two other records that aren’t connected to each other, you can use the Copy associations workflow action to associate these two other records. These records do not need to have a matching property, such as when using the Create associations action.

Understand the Copy associations action

The Copy associations action creates new associations, based on existing shared associations. For example, you have the following records:

  • Deal A associated to Contact A.
  • Deal A associated to a Company A.
  • Contact A and Company A are not associated.

When using Deal A as an intermediary record in the action, Contact A and Company A will be associated.

When using this action, associations will be set up for all associated records. For example, you have the following records:

  • Deal A associated to Contact A, Contact B, and Contact C.
  • Deal A associated to Company A and Company B.
  • None of the contacts or companies are associated.

When using Deal A as an intermediary record in the action, the following associations will be created:

  • Company A will be associated with Contact A, Contact B, and Contact C.
  • Company B will also be associated with Contact A, Contact B, and Contact C.

Use the Copy association action

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow or create a new workflow.
  • Set your enrollment triggers.
  • Click the + plus icon to add an action.
  • In the left panel, click to expand the CRM section. Then, click Copy associations.
  • Configure your Copy associations action details:
    • Intermediary record: the intermediary record, connecting the records to be associated. by default, this will be set to the [object] from trigger. You can also select other associated objects as the intermediary record, such as an associated contract.
    • Associate these records: the first object type to be associated.
    • With these records: the second object type to be associated.
    • Label to apply: the association label to be appled to the newly associated records. By default, no association labels will be applied, and the field will be set to Default (no label). Learn more about association labels.
  • After setting up your Copy associations action, at the top, click Save.
  • Continue setting up your workflow.

Automate A/B email testing with workflows

You can automate your A/B email tests by creating and saving an A/B email for automation. Once saved, you can include the A/B email in a workflow.

Over time, HubSpot will send the email variations across enrolled records. The 50/50 split may not occur immediately. This split is gradual and will occur over time as the number of recipients increase.

You can also test different automation strategies with enrolled records using Random distribution by percentage branches in workflows.

Before you get started

Permissions required Super Admin or Edit permissions for workflows are required to create or edit workflows.

Permissions required Super Admin or Publish permissions for marketing emails are required to create and save automated emails.

When setting up an automated email for A/B testing, the following restrictions will apply.

  • You must configure the A/B test in the email editor before publishing. If you’ve published an automated email without setting up an A/B test, it cannot be used for A/B email testing after. Even if the email is subsequently edited or unpublished.
  • Each A/B email can only be used once. After an email action has been saved to a workflow, you cannot use the same email in any other workflows. To use the same email in another workflow, clone the email instead.

Use an A/B email in a workflow

Use workflows to automate your A/B testing. You can send multiple A/B emails in a single workflow. After turning the workflow on, HubSpot will begin to evenly distribute the email variations to your enrolled records.

  • Create your A/B test automated email:
    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
    • In the upper right, click Create email to create a new automated email or clone an existing email. Only new, unpublished automated emails or cloned automated emails can be used when setting up an automated email for A/B testing.
    • In the email editor, enable A/B testing and configure your testing options. Automated A/B emails will be distributed in a 50/50 split.
    • After saving setting up your email, in the top right, click Review and Publish.
    • In the right panel, click Publish. The email will then be available for use in a workflow.

Please note: when using A/B testing and the Delay until an event happens functionality in workflows, HubSpot cannot check which version an interaction (opens clicks etc.) occurred.

  • Add your published A/B automated email to a workflow
    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
    • Click the name of an existing workflow, or create a new workflow.
    • In the workflow timeline, click the + plus icon to add a new action.
    • In the right panel, select Send email. Then select your A/B email.
    • Continue setting up your workflow.

Choose a winning A/B test variant

Metrics for your A/B test will be available on the email details screen. As you gather data, you can choose a winner between the two variants.

After choosing a winner, the workflow will only send out the winning variation. Once you pick the winning version, it will be sent to all future contacts in the workflow who meet the enrollment criteria, and the losing version will be archived.

Build workflows using Breeze Assistant

If you have a Data Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription, when creating or updating your workflow with Breeze Assistant, if no appropriate actions are identified, a custom code action may be automatically generated with corresponding code.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Understand limitations and requirements

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to use the workflows tool.

When building workflows with Breeze Assistant, do note the following:
