Categorize records in Agent Hub workflows

Add the Categorize record action to your Agent Hub workflow to classify CRM records based on their properties using AI. When using the action, set up different categories. Records will be automatically assigned to different categories based on the category name and description.

After setting up your action, use outputs from the action, such as the record’s Category and Confidence with other workflow actions.

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to use the workflows tool.

Use the Categorize records workflow action in Agent Hub workflows

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub.
  • At the top, click the Workflows tab.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow built in the agent builder.
  • In the top left or within the action workflow editor, click the + add icon.
  • In the left panel, search for and select the Categorize record action. Then, configure your action:
    • Record to categorize: the object type to be categorized. For example, contact records enrolled by the workflow trigger.
    • Categories: the categories for the CRM records to be categorized by. For example, categorize your records by different industries, urgencies, or sales potential. You can manually create categories or use existing properties.
      • Enter manually: manually create and define your own categories to sort records by.
        • To add a new category, click Add category. In the dialog box, configure your category.
          • Category: the name of the category.
          • Description a description of the category. This field is optional.
        • To remove a category, click the deletedelete icon next to the category name.
      • Use record property: use and existing property and corresponding property values to categorize your records. The categories will match the options of a dropdown select or multiple checkboxes property.

Example use cases

  • Branch records based on category: use the Category output from this action to branch records based on their category. Learn more about using branches in workflows.
  • Update record properties based on category: use the Category output with an Edit record action to update CRM records based on their category. For example, you can use it to update a ticket record’s urgency or a company record’s industry property. Learn more about using the Edit record workflow action.

Please note: when using outputs from the Categorize record action, it is recommended to include the Confidence output as an additional AND filter. For example, you may want to only update records when the Confidence for the output is at least 0.85.

Choose your workflow actions

Review the workflow actions available for automation when creating workflows in HubSpot. Actions are functions that the workflow will execute for enrolled records. Select appropriate workflow actions to ensure your workflows run as intended. Before selecting your workflow actions, review common workflow goals and workflow action and template recommendations.

Workflow actions are grouped by action type, such as delays, branches, CRM actions, AI actions, and more. Within a workflow, add actions to send an email, create a new record, and manage your contacts’ subscription. You can also use workflow actions from connected apps.

Workflow actions such as Create task and Send email can be saved without setting details. Add your actions first as placeholders. Then, fill out your placeholder actions before turning the workflow on. Learn more about placeholder actions.

Certain actions can be used with all workflow types. When using these actions, you may need to add the target record as a data source. For example, in a company workflow, you could add the enrolled company’s associated contact to an ads audience.

Please note: the actions available to you depend on your subscription. Locked actions locked require an account upgrade to use.

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to create and edit workflows.

Delay actions

Use delays to add a pause between actions in your workflow. Learn more about using delays with your workflows.

Action

What the action does

Calendar date

Delay enrolled records until a specific date. Use this delay when you want an action to execute only on a specific date.

Date property

Delay enrolled records until a specific date or date and time in a date or datetime property. Use this delay when you want an action to execute only on the date based on a specific date or datetime property. This delay option can be used with all workflow types.

Event occurrence

Delay enrolled records until a specified event occurs. For example, you can delay a contact until they visit a page or fill out a form.

Set amount of time

Delay enrolled records for a specific amount of days, hours, and minutes. Enrolled records will wait in the delay before they move to the next action. For example, when a contact submits a form, you can set a one-day delay before sending an automated marketing email.

If you have a Center on a date or Center on a date property contact-based workflow, delays are relative to the selected date or date property instead. Learn how to schedule actions in a contact-based workflow to execute at a specific date and time.

Days of week

Delay enrolled records until a specific day of the week.

Time of day

Delay enrolled records until a specific time of day. For example, if you’re using a workflow to send a series of promotional emails, you might want certain emails to only go out on Tuesdays. You can add a delay just before the Send email action to pause delayed contacts until Tuesday.

Branches

Use branches to direct your enrolled record down specific workflow paths based on set criteria. Learn more about using branches in your workflows.

Action

What the action does

Based on one property or action output

Use this type of branch to send enrolled records down paths based on properties and the outcomes of previous actions in the workflow.

This type of branch cannot be configured with AND and OR criteria. Each branch can create up to 250 unique branches for a single property.

Based on AND/OR logic

Direct enrolled records down a certain path based on filter criteria. You can use AND and OR criteria when setting up this type of branch.

Based on random distribution by percentage (Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise only)

Randomly split enrolled records into evenly sized groups for workflow experimentation.

Go to workflow action

Enroll the record in the current workflow into a new selected workflow, while remaining in the original workflow.

When a record reaches the Go to workflow action:

  • The record will be enrolled in the selected workflow, bypassing any enrollment triggers set.
  • The record will also remain enrolled in the original workflow and proceed to the next action.

You can only enroll a record in a workflow of the same type. For example, deals can only be enrolled in deal-based workflows. The record will not be enrolled in the selected workflow if:

  • The record is on a suppression list for the selected workflow.
  • The record is already enrolled and active in the selected workflow.

Go to action

Connect if/then branches with this action. This streamlines your workflow building process by connecting if/then branches.

Go to other action actions can only be added within if/then branches, and you can only select actions in other if/then branches. This prevents workflow loops. Actions that are not available for selection will be greyed out.

Learn more about using the Go to other action action.

Communication actions

Action

What the action does

Enroll in a sequence (Sales Hub and Service Hub Enterprise only)

Automatically enroll contacts in a sequence. You can select a specific sequence, along with the sender and sender’s email address. Only users with a paid Sales Hub or Service Hub Enterprise seat can be selected as the sequence sender.

Learn more about automating sequence enrollment using workflows.

Please note: when you select an option from the Sender dropdown menu, your choice applies to all emails in the sequence. If you select Contact owner, the From address for all emails in the sequence will be the contact owner at the time of enrollment, even if the contact owner changes after enrollment.

Send Email (Marketing Hub and Service Hub Professional and Enterprise only)

Send marketing emails that have been saved for automation to contacts associated with the enrolled record. You can select from existing automated marketing emails, or create a new automated marketing email by clicking + Create new email.

When using this action, please note the following:

  • Marketing emails will be sent only to a contact’s primary email address.
  • Other automated emails, such as member registration emails for private content, cannot be used with this action.
  • In contact-based workflows, you can send an email to an enrolled contact, or any associated contacts of the enrolled contact.

Service Hub Professional and Enterprise users can use this action to send automated emails when a ticket is received or closed. Learn how to send an email when a ticket is received or closed.

Please note: if you have access to Service Hub Starter and Sales Hub Professional+ or Marketing Hub Starter+ you will see emails in the Send email action section in the Workflows tool. However, these emails are not available to use and the action can only be used to send automated emails when a ticket is received or closed.

Send in-app notification

Send an in-app notification to specified teams or users. The notification will appear in both the HubSpot notification center and in the HubSpot app as a notification. This action can be used with all workflow types.

When specifying a team, only primary members of that team will receive notifications. Extra team members will not receive any team notifications. If an account is opted into the Support Multiple Main Teams for Full Functionality beta, all team members will receive notifications.

Send an internal email notification

Send an internal email to specific users, teams, or owners. This action can be used with all workflow types.

This type of email notification has similar formatting options to other rich text editors across HubSpot. You can set and format text, insert images, and use tokens based on the type of workflow (i.e., contact-based workflows can use contact tokens).

  • In contact-based workflows, this action is different from the Send internal marketing email action, because you cannot select from existing automated emails. The internal email notification must be created from within the workflow editor.
  • When specifying a team, only primary members of that team will receive notifications. Extra team members will not receive any team notifications. If an account is opted into the Support Multiple Main Teams for Full Functionality beta, all team members will receive notifications.
Send internal marketing emails (Marketing Hub Professional
and Enterprise only)

Send an automated email to specified email addresses, or a contact property that stores an email address, including any custom properties.

  • This action differs from the Send internal email action because you can select existing automated emails.
  • This action is only available in contact-based workflows.
Send survey (Service Hub Professional and Enterprise only) (BETA)

If you’ve created a custom survey with the delivery method Workflow, you can automatically send the survey to enrolled contacts. Learn how to create a workflow survey.

Send WhatsApp message
(Marketing Hub and Service Hub Professional and Enterprise only)

Automatically send WhatsApp messages to a contact’s Whatsapp phone number. Contacts must have a valid number in the default property and be opted in to receive WhatsApp messages.

You can use this action in both contact-based workflows and all other workflow types. Learn more about connecting a WhatsApp channel to the conversations inbox.

Send SMS message (Marketing SMS Add-On only)

Automatically send an SMS to the enrolled contact or a specific type of contact associated to the enrolled record. Learn more about sending sms messages using workflows.

You can use this action in both contact-based workflows and other workflow types. Learn more about using contact-based workflow actions in other workflow types.

Unenroll from sequence (Sales Hub and Service Hub Enterprise only)

Automatically unenroll contacts from the sequence they’re currently enrolled in. This action can be used with all workflow types.

Learn more about automating sequence unenrollment using workflows.

Assign conversation owner in a workflow (Service Hub and Data Hub Professional or
Enterprise only)

Automatically change the inbox and ownership assignment for a conversation.

Learn more about automatically assigning a conversation owner in a workflow.

CRM actions

Use these actions to create, update, and manage the properties of enrolled records. You can use property management actions for records that are available for your subscription:

  • Contact, company, and deal properties can be managed in all products and plans that include workflows.
  • Lead properties can only be managed in Sales Hub Professional and Enterprise accounts.
  • Quote properties can only be managed in Revenue Hub Enterprise accounts.
  • Ticket and feedback submission properties can only be managed in Service Hub Professional and Enterprise accounts.
  • Custom object properties can only be managed in Enterprise accounts.
  • In conversation-based workflows, you can only manage properties of contacts associated with the conversation. Conversation properties are automatically set by HubSpot and cannot be edited.
  • Email subscription status can only be set in contact-based workflows.

If the access to a property has been restricted, keep in mind the following:

  • When creating a new workflow, users who have no access or with View only permissions cannot add workflow actions that affect property values in new workflows.
    • When setting up these actions, the property will be greyed out. For example, these users will not be able to use the Clear property value action.
    • The property can still be used in enrollment triggers or other actions such as if/then branches.
  • If an existing workflow references the restricted property:
    • Users with View only permissions cannot edit the workflow. This includes enrollment triggers and other workflow actions. The workflow will display in view-only mode.
    • Users with no access to the properties will not be able to access the workflows.

Action

What the action does

Validate and format phone number

Format your phone numbers for calling. Then, use the Edit record action to update your phone number properties with the formatted number. Learn more about formatting phone numbers using workflows.

Enrich record

Enrich enrolled contacts or companies. When setting up this enrichment action, you can choose whether to overwrite existing property data. This will take precedence over any overwrite rules set in your enrichment property mapping.

For example, if you’ve configured the enrichment property mapping to Fill empty values only, but the workflow action has been set to overwrite existing data, any existing data for enrolled records in that workflow will be overwritten.

Learn more about contact and company enrichment.

Edit record

Set, edit, copy, and clear property values. This can be a property in the enrolled record, or a property in an associated record. Learn more about editing records with workflows.

This action can also be used to copy values from previous workflow actions. For example, if a workflow includes an Add to Zoom webinar action, you can copy the resulting Zoom webinar link into a custom contact property. Learn more about adding contacts to a Zoom webinar using workflows.

When using this action, please note the following:

  • When using this action, ensure your source and target properties have compatible property types. Learn more about compatible source and target property types for copying property values.
  • When copying between two multiple-checkbox properties or HubSpot user properties, where the option Multiple users can be selected has been configured, you can select one of the following options:
    • Append to current value(s): adds the selected values to any of the record’s existing values. Select this option if you want your records to keep any values currently in the property.
    • Replace current value(s): sets the property for each record to the selected values. Select this option if you want to overwrite a record’s existing values in the property.
  • To use this action in a Custom object-based workflow, only objects that have an association created with the primary custom object will appear in the dropdown menu.
Create record

Automatically create new records. You can create records for the following object types:

  • Contacts
  • Companies
  • Deals
  • Tickets (Service Hub Professional and Enterprise only)
  • Leads (Sales Hub Professional and Enterprise only)
  • Custom objects (Enterprise only)

Learn more about creating records with workflows.

Copy ticket

Copy details of an existing ticket record to a new ticket.

Add line item to deal

Associate line items with deals in deal-based workflows. Learn more about adding line items to deals using workflows.

Edit/create record in another account (Marketing Hub, Sales Hub, Service Hub, or Data Hub Professional and Enterprise only)

Edit an existing contact or create a new contact in a different HubSpot account in your organization.

This action is only available in accounts with multi-account management turned on. Learn more about creating multi-account workflows.

Create deal in another account (Marketing Hub, Sales Hub, Service Hub, or Data Hub Professional and Enterprise only)

Create a new deal in a different HubSpot account in your organization.

This action is only available in accounts with multi-account management turned on. Learn more about creating multi-account workflows.

Create Salesforce task

Create a customized Salesforce task associated with the enrolled contact. The contact owner or integration user will receive a task in Salesforce when an assigned contact is enrolled in the workflow. This action is only available in contact-based workflows.

Create task

Automatically create new tasks.

Create note

Automatically create notes. These notes will be automatically associated with the enrolled record.

For example, you can create notes for contacts that submitted a form. You can also add additional details to the note using tokens based on the form fields, such as a Comment field.

When setting up your Create note action, you can bold and italicize the message in your note. You can also add links, emojis, and more.

Delete contact

Automatically delete enrolled contacts. For example, you can set up a workflow to enroll and delete inactive contacts in bulk.

This action can be used with all workflow types. Contacts can be restored within 90 days of deletion. Learn how to restore deleted contacts.

Increase or decrease property value

Increase or decrease the value in a Number type property of the enrolled record. For example, you can increase the value of a custom number property, Orders bought, for every enrolled company.

Manage communication subscriptions

Set the subscription status of the enrolled contact. You can set the subscription status for a specific channel, subscription type, the lawful basis for communicating with the contact, and the explanation for this communication consent. Learn more about setting subscription types with workflows.

You can use this action in both contact-based workflows and other workflow types. Learn more about using contact-based workflow actions in other workflow types.

Rotate record to owner (Sales Hub and Service Hub Professional and Enterprise only)

Assign the enrolled records to users equally within a selected team or between specified users. This action is only compatible with activated, paid users.

When rotating records in ticket, deal (BETA) and lead-based workflows, additional distribution options are available. Learn how to rotate records using workflows.

Rotate record by skill

After assigning user skills in help desk, you can rotate tickets to users based on their skills. Learn how to rotate ticket owners by skill with workflows.

Rotate conversation owners

Automatically move a conversation to another inbox and assign it to a specific user or team based on access to the inbox. Learn how to rotate conversation owners with workflows.

Set Salesforce campaign

Set a Salesforce campaign for the enrolled contact. This action is only available in contact-based workflows.

Create associations

Create new associations within CRM records. For example, you can create associations between contacts and companies when they have matching Company name property values.

Learn more about managing CRM record associations with workflows.

Apply association labels

Apply an association label to already-associated records. You can choose to apply association labels to all associated records of a certain object type or further refine which associated records to apply the association label to.

Learn more about managing CRM record associations with workflows.

Update association labels

Replace your existing association label or append a new association label to associated records. Learn more about managing CRM record associations with workflows.

Remove association labels

Clear your existing association labels. Learn more about managing CRM record associations with workflows.

Copy associations

Create associations between records based on an intermediary record. Learn how to use the Copy associations action.

Stop tracking intent signals

Deactivate tracking and continuous enrichment of intent signals. Learn more about intent signals.

Track intent signals

Activate tracking and continuous enrichment of intent signals. Learn more about intent signals.

Convert to invoice

Create a one-time draft invoice from a deal or quote. Learn how to create a draft invoice from a deal or quote using workflows.

Create quote

Create a new quote based on an existing deal.

Create renewal quote from contract (Revenue Hub only)

Create a renewal quote based on an existing contract. Learn more about creating a renewal quote on a contract.

AI actions

HubSpot Credits required HubSpot Credits are required to use AI workflow actions. Learn how to understand HubSpot credits.

Action

What the action does

Assign to Customer Agent

Assign a conversation or ticket to the customer agent.

Learn more about using the customer agent.

Data Agent: Custom prompt (BETA)

Use custom prompts to analyze, summarize, and categorize data from enrolled records. Learn more about using Breeze to manage data in workflows.

Data Agent: Research (BETA)

Generate and extract data to research your records using properties or call transcripts associated with the enrolled record. Learn more about using Breeze to manage data in workflows.

Data Agent: Fill Smart Property (BETA)

Run existing smart properties for companies or contacts. Learn more about using Breeze to manage data in workflows. Learn more about creating and using smart properties.

Summarize record (BETA)

Summarize data from enrolled records or any associated records. Then, use outputs from the action with other workflow actions.

If your account has a Marketing Hub Enterprise subscription, you can also use this action to generate personalized content to use in automated marketing emails.

Learn more about summarizing data in workflows.

Infer company value proposition and ICP (BETA)

Generate selling profiles for prospecting agent, including target personas, value propositions, and more. Learn how to use Breeze to infer company value proposition and ICP in workflows.

Enroll in prospecting agent (Sales Hub Professional and Enterprise only) (BETA)

Automatically enroll contacts in the prospecting agent. HubSpot supports one agent, so there’ll be one option labeled Default agent.

Learn more about how to use the prospecting agent.

Unenroll in prospecting agent (Sales Hub Professional and Enterprise only) (BETA)

Automatically unenroll contacts in the prospecting agent. Learn more about how to use the prospecting agent.

Use a custom LLM (BETA)

Connect your workflows with Large Language Models providers (LLMs) and start using AI-powered workflow actions. Learn more about using LLMs in workflows.

Run Agent

Deploy AI-powered agents directly from workflows. For example, you can use this action to trigger and run the Company Research Agent. Learn how to run agents using workflows.

Generate prospect profile

Use AI to generate a profile summary for a given prospect.

Marketing actions

Action

What the action does

Add to ads audience (Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise)

Add contacts to a new or existing ads audience. When selecting an existing audience, you can only choose an audience that was created in the workflows tool. This action can be used with all workflow types.

Remove from ads audience (Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise)

Remove contact from an ads audience. You can only choose from audiences that were created in the workflows tool. This action can be used with all workflow types.

Add to campaign (Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise)

Add contacts, tickets, or deals to marketing campaigns. Learn more about associating records with campaigns.

Remove from campaign (Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise)

Remove a record from a HubSpot campaign. Learn more about associating contacts with campaigns.

Add to static segment (Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise)

Add enrolled contacts, companies, or deals to a static segment. This action can be used with all workflow types.

Remove from static segment (Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise)

Remove enrolled contacts, companies, or deals from a static segment. This action can be used with all workflow types.

Set marketing contact status

Set the marketing contact status of the enrolled contact. Contacts can be set as marketing at any time, but will only update to non-marketing on your account’s update date. Learn how to find the update date for your account.

You can use this action in both contact-based workflows and other workflow types. Learn more about using contact-based workflow actions in other workflow types.

Add participant to marketing event

Add contacts to and update the participant state of these contacts in manually created marketing event. Learn more about managing marketing event participants using workflows.

Data ops actions

Action

What the action does

Custom code (Data Hub Professional and Enterprise only)

Write and execute JavaScript in your workflow. You can extend workflow functionality within and outside of HubSpot with custom code actions.

Learn more about using custom code actions, and view examples of custom code actions in HubSpot’s Programmable Automation Use Case catalog.

Format data (Data Hub Professional and Enterprise only)

Automatically format and maintain your CRM data. For example, you can use this action to capitalize contact or company names, calculate values, or structure your date properties.

Keep in mind that using this action on its own will not update a property for the enrolled record. You’ll need to use this action in combination with the Edit record action to update the properties of enrolled records.

Learn more about formatting data with workflows.

Send a webhook (Data Hub Professional and Enterprise only)

Trigger a webhook to an external application. This allows your workflow to communicate with this external application. For example, webhooks can send a HubSpot company’s information (formatted in JSON) to an external CRM. This action can be used with all workflow types.

Learn more about triggering webhooks.

Connected app actions

When you connect an app to your HubSpot account, the app may include workflow actions. When a connected app provides workflow actions, those actions will be listed under the name of the app.

HubSpot supports certain app actions such as sending a Slack notification or adding data to Google Sheets. App partners can also create extension actions that interact with their application.

All connected app or integration actions can be used in all available workflow types.

Action

What the action does

Add contacts to a Zoom Webinar

Add contacts as registrants to a Zoom webinar. HubSpot’s integration with Zoom only accepts and syncs with three required fields in the Zoom registration link: First name, Last name, and Email. If the registration link requires any other fields, the registration action will fail.

Send Slack notification

Send a Slack notification to your integrated Slack workspace. Learn more about sending Slack notifications through workflows.

Create a Slack channel

Create a Slack channel from within HubSpot. When the channel is created, it will display on the associated Company or Deal record. The card will note that the channel was created by a workflow. This action is only available in company and deal-based workflows.

When using this action, please note the following:

  • When setting up the Channel Name, you can specify the channel name or use a personalization token. Channel names must be 80 characters or less, and can only contain lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores.
  • When setting up the Channel Visibility, you can specify the channel name or use a personalization token. You can select whether the created channel will be public or private. A private channel will only be visible to the user who owns the enrolled record.
  • The record you’re enrolling in the workflow must have an owner. If a company or deal record does not have an owner the channel will not be created.
  • By default, the record owner will be invited to the channel.
Send Google Chat notification

Send a Google Chat notification to your integrated Google Chat spaces. Learn more about sending Google Chat notifications through workflows.

Create an Asana task

Create an Asana task from within HubSpot. Learn more about creating Asana tasks through workflows.

Create a Trello Card

Create a Trello card from within HubSpot. Learn more about creating Trello cards with workflows.

Set a Salesforce task

Set a customized Salesforce task associated with the enrolled contact. The contact owner or integration user will receive a task in Salesforce when an assigned contact is enrolled in the workflow. This action is only available in contact-based workflows.

Set a Salesforce campaign

Set a Salesforce campaign for the enrolled contact. This action is only available in contact-based workflows.

Create a NetSuite sales order

Create a NetSuite sales order for an enrolled deal record. This action is only available in deal-based workflows.

Learn more about creating NetSuite sales orders through deal-based workflows.

Send a Docusign template

Send a Docusign template to the enrolled contact record. Learn more about sending Docusign templates through workflows.

Choose your workflow actions in Agent Hub

When setting up workflows in Agent Hub, you can choose actions from the following categories:

  • HubSpot: take actions within HubSpot. For example, you can create a note or a new CRM record. The workflow actions available depend on your account’s subscriptions.
  • AI: execute AI actions and agents. When triggering an agent, you do not need a record to trigger the action.
  • Apps: take action in third party applications such as Google Sheets, Airtable, and more. For example, when a record is updated in HubSpot, create a new row in Google Sheets. The actions available depend on the applications connected to your HubSpot account.

You can also use custom code actions in the modern workflow builder, and use Breeze Assistant to automatically generate the corresponding code. Learn more about building workflows using Breeze Assistant.

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to use the workflows tool.

HubSpot

Use the following action types to automate processes in HubSpot.

Flow control
  • Branch: direct enrolled records down a certain path based on filter criteria or random distribution. When setting up branches in Agent Hub workflows, you can use either:
    • Conditions: use AND and OR criteria to determine which branch records will be directed to. For example, you can direct records to different branches based on properties such as geographical region, industry, and more. You can add up to 20 branches in this branch action.
    • Random distribution by percentage: randomly direct records down different branches. You can set the percentage of records down each branch. For example, you can want to do a 50/50 split or a 30/30/40 distribution. Use this type of branch to A/B test different strategies in your workflow. You can add up to 100 branches in this branch action.
  • Delay: delay enrolled records for a set amount of time, until a specific ay of the week, or a specific time of the day. Learn more about using delays in Agent Hub workflows.
Communication
  • Enroll in a sequence (Sales Hub and Service Hub Enterprise only): automatically enroll contacts in a sequence. Learn more about automating sequence enrollment using workflows.
  • Unenroll from sequence (Sales Hub and Service Hub Enterprise only): Automatically unenroll contacts from the sequence they’re currently enrolled in.
  • Learn more about automating sequence enrollment using workflows.
  • Send email: send marketing emails that have been saved for automation to contacts associated with the enrolled record.
    • When using this action in the Agent Hub workflow builder, you can use tokens from other associated records using the Find one record or Find one associated record action. For example, use data from deal or ticket records in your automated email.
    • When using contact personalization tokens, only the recipient contact’s property values will be used. Similarly, only the recipient’s primary company will be used for any company personalization tokens.
  • In-app notification: send an in-app notification to specified teams or users. The notification will appear in both the HubSpot notification center and in the HubSpot app as a notification.
    • Only primary members of teams will receive notifications. Extra team members will not receive any team notifications.
  • Send internal email notification: send an internal email to specific users, teams, or owners.
    • You cannot select from existing automated emails. The internal email notification must be created from within the editor.
    • Only primary members of teams will receive notifications. Extra team members will not receive any team notifications.
  • Send survey: if you’ve created a custom survey with the delivery method Workflow, you can automatically send the survey to enrolled contacts. Learn how to create a workflow survey.
  • Send WhatsApp message: send WhatsApp messages to a contact’s Whatsapp phone number. Contacts must have a valid number in the default property and be opted in to receive WhatsApp messages. Learn more about connecting a WhatsApp channel to the conversations inbox.
CRM
  • Add line item to deal: associate line items with deals in deal-based workflows. Learn more about adding line items to deals using workflows.
  • Assign conversation owner: automatically change the inbox and ownership assignment for a conversation. Learn more about automatically assigning a conversation owner in a workflow.
  • Convert to invoice: create a one-time draft invoice from a deal or quote. Learn how to create a draft invoice from a deal or quote using workflows.
  • Copy ticket: copy details of an existing ticket record to a new ticket.
  • Create record: create new records. Learn more about creating records with workflows.
    • You can create records for the following object types using Agent Hub Workflows: appointment, company, contact, course, deal, listing, order, payment, project, service, and ticket.
    • By default, properties displayed in each Create record action will match the properties set in the create form for each object. To customize the properties displayed, update the form directly.
    • When creating records with Agent Hub workflows, record associations will not be automatically created. You will need to use the Create associations action to set up and manage additional associations and association labels. Learn more about managing CRM record associations with workflows.
  • Create associations: create new associations within CRM records. Learn more about managing CRM record associations with workflows.
    • For example, you can create associations between contacts and companies when they have matching property record values.
    • You can also create associations with specific records, including other records referenced in the same workflow
  • Create task: create a task. Learn more about creating tasks with workflows.
    • By default, the task will not be associated to any records. You’ll need to use the Create associations action to associate the task with other records. Learn more about managing CRM record associations with workflows.
  • Create note: create notes for a CRM record.
    • When creating a note, you must select an associated record from the workflow, such as a record from a Find one record workflow action.
    • If no record is selected, the note will be automatically associated with the enrolled record by default.
    • If no records are available, an error will appear for the action.
  • Create quote: create a new quote based on an existing deal.
  • Create renewal quote from contract (Revenue Hub only): create a renewal quote based on an existing contract. Learn more about creating a renewal quote on a contract.
  • Delete record: delete a CRM record.
  • Edit record: set, edit, copy, and clear property values. This can be a property in the enrolled record, or a property in an associated record. Learn more about editing records with workflows.
  • Enrich record: enrich enrolled contacts or companies. Learn more about automatically enriching contact or company records.
  • Find one associated record: locate and use other associated records. You can use this action to find associated records with either the enrolled record or other records located from the Find one record action.
  • Find one record: identify and use a different record type with your action, add the Find one record action before your selected action.
  • Manage communication subscriptions: set the subscription status of the enrolled contact. Learn more about setting subscription types with workflows.
  • Remove association labels: clear your existing association labels. Learn more about managing CRM record associations with workflows.
  • Rotate record by skills: rotate tickets to users based on their skills. Learn more about rotating ticket owners by skill with workflows.
  • Stop tracking intent signals: deactivate tracking and continuous enrichment of intent signals. Learn more about intent signals.
  • Update association labels: replace your existing association label or append a new association label to associated records. Learn more about managing CRM record associations with workflows.
  • Validate and format phone number: format your phone numbers for calling. Then, use the Edit record action to update your phone number properties with the formatted number. Learn more about formatting phone numbers using workflows.
Marketing
  • Add participant to marketing event: add contacts to and update the participant state of these contacts in manually created marketing event. Learn more about managing marketing event participants using workflows.
  • Add to ads campaign: add records to an ads campaign.
  • Add to campaign: add contacts, tickets, or deals to marketing campaigns. Learn more about associating records with campaigns.
  • Add to static segment (list): add enrolled contacts, companies, or deals to a static list.
  • Remove from ads audience: remove contact from an ads audience. (You can only choose from audiences that were created in the workflows tool)
  • Remove from campaign (Marketing Hub only): remove a record from a HubSpot campaign. Learn more about associating contacts with campaigns.
  • Remove from static segment (list): remove enrolled contacts, companies, or deals to a static list.
  • Set marketing contact status: set the marketing contact status of the enrolled contact. Contacts can be set as marketing at any time, but will only update to non-marketing on your account’s update date.
Utilities
  • Custom code: write and execute JavaScript in your workflow. You can extend workflow functionality within and outside of HubSpot with custom code actions.
    • You can use Breeze Assistant to automatically generate the corresponding code based on text prompts.
    • Learn more about using custom code actions, and view examples of custom code actions in HubSpot’s Programmable Automation Use Case catalog.
  • Format data: format and maintain your CRM data. Uing this action on its own will not update a property for the enrolled record. You’ll need to use this action in combination with the Edit record action to update the properties of enrolled records. Learn more about formatting data with workflows.

AI

HubSpot Credits required HubSpot Credits are required to use AI and agentic workflow actions. Learn how to understand HubSpot credits.

Agents
  • Run custom agent: run a custom agent installed in your account. Learn more about custom agents.
  • Add agentic step: enter a custom prompt to determine what the agentic step does. You can also enter inputs for the agentic step.
AI
  • Generate Prospect Profile: use AI to generate a profile summary for a given prospect.
  • Infer company value proposition and ICP: generate selling profiles for prospecting agent, including target personas, value propositions, and more. Learn how to use Breeze to infer company value proposition and ICP in workflows.
  • Research company news: generate and extract data to research your records using properties or call transcripts associated with the enrolled record. Learn more about using Breeze to manage data in workflows.
  • Summarize record: summarize data from enrolled records or any associated records. Then, use outputs from the action with other workflow actions.
  • Use a custom LLM: connect your workflows with Large Language Models providers (LLMs) and start using AI-powered workflow actions. Learn more about using LLMs in workflows.
HubSpot agents
  • Data Agent:
    • Data agent: Custom prompt: use custom prompts to analyze, summarize, and categorize data from enrolled records. Learn more about using Breeze to manage data in workflows.
    • Data Agent: Fill Smart Property: run existing smart properties for companies or contacts. Learn more about using Breeze to manage data in workflows. Learn more about creating and using smart properties.
    • Data Agent: Research: generate and extract data to research your records using properties or call transcripts associated with the enrolled record. Learn more about using Breeze to manage data in workflows.
  • Prospecting Agent:
    • Enroll in prospecting agent: automatically enroll contacts in the prospecting agent. Learn more about how to use the prospecting agent.
  • Customer Agent:
    • Assign to customer agent: assign a conversation or ticket to the customer agent. Learn more about using the customer agent.

Clone workflows and workflow actions

Clone workflows as a starting point when creating new workflows. After adding actions, you can also copy or move them to create workflows more efficiently. This can be especially useful when building out repetitive actions that need only minor adjustments. When building these kinds of workflows, you can also consider using go-to-actions.

For example, you’re building a workflow to create deals based on a contact’s location. Instead of creating four Create deal actions, you could create one action, clone it three times, and make adjustments.

Permissions required To clone workflows and workflow actions, users must have Edit permissions for workflows or Super Admin permissions. To publish workflows, users must have Publish permissions for workflows.

Clone workflows

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Hover over the workflow and click Clone.
  • In the dialog box, enter a name for your new workflow.
  • If you have the Brands add-on, click the dropdown menu and select a brand for your new workflow.
  • Click Clone.

Please note: workflows with more than 500 actions may encounter issues when cloning. If you’ve encountered an issue, you can try reducing the number of actions, splitting the workflow into smaller workflows before cloning, or manually recreating the workflow instead.

Clone and move workflow actions

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of a workflow, or create a new workflow.
  • Add a new action to the workflow, or locate an existing action you want to clone or move.
  • To clone a workflow action:
    • In the action box, click the duplicateClone icon. Then, select from the following options:
      • Clone this action only: clone only the selected action.
      • Clone this action and all following actions: clone the selected action and all following actions.
    • Choose where the cloned actions will be placed by clicking Place here in the desired location.
    • In the dialog box, click Save

Please note:

  • Cloned if/then branches can be placed only at the end points of a workflow.

  • To prevent any potential errors, workflow actions that reference workflow action outputs within a branch cannot be cloned or moved to a different branch. The option to clone or move the action will be greyed out.

  • To move a workflow action:

    • In the action box, click the move Move icon. Then, select from the following options:
      • Move this action only: move only the selected action
      • Move this action and all following actions: move the selected action and all following actions. This option may only appear on certain actions.
    • Choose where the selected action will be placed by clicking Place here in the desired location.
    • After moving your action, click Save.

Compatible property types for copying values with workflows

When using the Edit records action in a workflow to copy property values, only properties with compatible property field types can be selected. Review which property types can be copied to other property types below.

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to use the workflows tool.

Text properties

Single-line and multi-line text properties can be copied to the following property types:

  • Single-line text
  • Multi-line text

Number properties

Number properties can be copied to the following property types:

  • Single-line text
  • Multi-line text
  • Number

Date properties

There are two types of date properties in HubSpot: date picker properties and date and time picker properties.

  • Date picker properties can be copied to both date picker properties and date and time picker properties
    • When a date picker property is copied to a date and time picker property, the time will default to midnight UTC which can cause unexpected results.
    • For example, the datetime value for May 1, 2015 is 01 May 2015 00:00:00 UTC. If your account’s timezone is in UTC-04:00 Eastern Time, the datetime will appear as 30 April 2015 20:00:00, four hours behind midnight UTC.
  • Date and time picker properties can only be copied to other Date and time picker properties.
  • All HubSpot default date properties (e.g., Create date, Last modified date) are date and time picker properties.

Checkbox and select properties

Single checkbox, multiple checkbox, radio select, and dropdown select properties can be copied to the following property types:

  • Single-line/multi-line text: when enumeration property values are copied to a text property, the label value for the enumeration property will be copied, not the internal value.
    • This will also apply to the following properties:
      • First touch converting campaign
      • Last touch converting campaign
    • When copying the Original source drill-down 2 property, the internal value of the property will be copied instead.
  • Other checkbox or select properties of the same type: to copy from one checkbox or select property to another, properties must meet both requirements:
    • The target and source properties must be the same property type:
      • For example, both the source and the target property must be dropdown select properties.
      • If the source property is a checkbox property, and the target property is a dropdown select property, the properties will not be compatible.
    • The internal property values must exist in both properties.
      • For example, if the source dropdown select property has three options, Cold Lead, Warm Lead, and Hot Lead, the target property must also have those options.
      • The internal value must match exactly, including capitalization, spaces, and any underscores. After an option is saved, it cannot be changed. If you have mismatched internal values, it is recommended to create a new option with the correct internal value.
    • If the target checkbox or select property is missing values found in the source property, the properties are considered mismatched.
      • To copy mismatched properties, you’ll need to edit the source or target property to contain all property values in the other property.
      • You can do this by adding new property options to the source or target property, or by copying the values from one property to the other.

HubSpot user properties

HubSpot user properties automatically include all users in the account and can be copied to the following property types:

  • HubSpot user: when copying from one HubSpot user property to another, the user’s display name will be copied.
  • Single-line/multi-line text: when copying from a HubSpot user property to a text property, the user’s internal value will be copied.

Source-only properties

Read-only, calculation, and rollup properties cannot be edited. When using these property types with the Edit record action, they can be selected as a source property to copy values from, but cannot be selected as the target property to be updated.

Read-only properties

Read-only properties, such as Create date and Original source are set by HubSpot analytics or third-party integrations and cannot be edited. They can be selected as a source property but cannot be selected as the target property.

Calculation and rollup properties

Similar to read-only properties, calculation and rollup properties can only be selected as the source property, but cannot be selected as the target property.

Calculation and rollup properties can only be copied to the following property types:

  • Single-line text
  • Multi-line text
  • Number

Connect workflow branches using Go to actions

To streamline your workflow building process, you can connect branches with the Go to action action instead of adding the same steps multiple times. This is recommended for workflows with multiple branches.

Permissions required To add actions to workflows, users must have Edit permissions for workflows or Super Admin permissions. To publish workflows, users must have Publish permissions for workflows.

To set up a Go to other action action:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow, or create a new workflow by clicking Create workflow.
  • Within a branch, click the + plus icon.
  • In the left panel, select Go to action.
  • Select another action in the workflow to connect to.
    • You can only select actions in other branches. This prevents workflow loops.
    • Actions that are not available for selection will be greyed out.
  • In the dialog box, click Done to connect the actions.
    • A dashed arrow will appear showing the connected actions.
    • When a record reaches the Go to action, it will be sent to the connected action.
  • To edit the Go to action, click the action. You will be directed to the editor to select another action in the workflow to connect to.

Create ‘Specific date’ or ‘Contact date property’ contact-based workflows

Create Specific date or Contact date property contact-based workflows to center your workflow actions on a calendar date or contact date property. This allows you to schedule and execute workflow actions relative to a specific date.

Please note: Specific date or Contact date property contact-based workflows have been sunset and are being phased out.

  • Starting 10th July 2024, users will not be able to create new Specific date or Contact date property contact-based workflows.
  • Existing workflows will still be accessible and function normally.
  • Moving forward, use the Based on a schedule enrollment triggers and the Delay until date workflow action to recreate and further customize the functionalities of date-centered workflows.

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to create and edit workflows.

Select workflow type

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • In the upper right, click Create workflow > From scratch.
  • In the left panel, select Contact-based as your workflow type.
  • In the right panel, under How do you want this workflow to start?, select Specific Date or Contact date property. Learn more about contact-based workflow types.
    • If you select Specific date, click the Date of event dropdown menu and select the date the workflow actions will revolve around.
    • If you select Contact date property, click the Contact date property dropdown menu and select the contact date property the workflow actions will revolve around.
  • Click the pencil icon edit to give your workflow a name, then click Next. You’ll then be brought to the workflow editor.

Set enrollment criteria

When a contact meets the enrollment criteria, they’ll automatically be enrolled. If you only want to enroll contacts manually, leave the enrollment trigger box blank. Learn more about manual enrollment.

  • In the workflow editor, click Set up triggers.
  • In the left panel, select a filter type for your enrollment trigger. Set up the criteria, then click Save.
  • By default, contacts will only be enrolled in a workflow the first time they meet the enrollment triggers. To enable re-enrollment for filter-based triggers:
    • In the left sidebar, click the Re-enrollment tab.
    • Click to toggle the Allow re-enrollment switch on.
    • Select the triggers that you want to use for re-enrollment. Learn more about adding re-enrollment triggers to workflows.
  • To enable re-enrollment for event-based filters:
    • In the left sidebar, navigate to the Should contacts be re-enrolled in this workflow? section.
    • Select Yes, re-enroll every time the trigger occurs.
  • For Contact date property workflows, add contact date property is known as an enrollment trigger. Actions will only execute for contacts who have a value for the date property, so this enrollment criteria will ensure all contacts who enter the workflow can go through actions successfully.
  • Click Save.
  • Any actions in the workflow are relative to the selected date or contact date property value. To set date and time the next action will execute, click the Delay action.

Please note: the Do the next action on… delay cannot be deleted as it is used to schedule the first workflow action based on the selected date or date property.

  • In the left panel, click the When will the next action execute? dropdown menu and select a date or if the action will execute before, on, or after the contact date property. Click the Time of day to execute dropdown menu and select a time.
  • Click Save.

Set the workflow to recur annually (optional)

By default, date-centered workflows won’t recur annually. However, you can set the workflow to re-enroll contacts based on the selected date or date property each year. For example, use this option to automatically enroll contacts in the workflow on their renewal date or birthday every year.

Please note: the default contact property Date of birth is linked to the ads tool and has a single-line text field type that cannot be modified. To create a workflow centered around a contact’s birthday, create a custom contact property (e.g., Birthdate) with a Date picker field type.

To set the workflow to recur annually:

  • Click the Specify a date action.
  • In the left panel, click to select the Recur annually checkbox.
  • Click Save.

When setting a Contact date property workflow to recur annually, the workflow will use the day and month of the property value, ignoring the year. In other words, actions in annually recurring workflows will be scheduled relative to the day and month in the current year.

For example, you create a workflow centered on a contact’s Became a customer date property. If the first action is scheduled to happen 300 days after that date, an enrolled contact will be scheduled based on the day and month of their Became a customer date property. Even if the contact became a customer on 1/20/2020, enrolling them in the workflow in 2021 will schedule the first action 300 days after 1/20/2021.

Specific date vs Contact date property workflows

Specific date

In Specific date workflows, all workflow actions are centered on a fixed calendar date. Similar to Blank workflows, contacts are enrolled in the workflow when they meet the enrollment triggers, or are manually enrolled into the workflow.

However, contacts will remain in the workflow until the first action is scheduled to execute, relative to the fixed calendar date. Delays added anywhere else in the workflow are relative to the fixed calendar date, not to the previous action.

Unlike Contact date property workflows, all contacts in a Specific date workflow will execute workflow actions at the same date and time. Some examples of Specific date workflows are:

  • Sending holiday emails to your contacts.
  • Sending reminder emails to contacts who registered for an upcoming webinar.
Contact date property

In Contact date property workflows, all workflow actions are centered on a contact date property. Similar to Blank workflows, contacts are enrolled in the workflow when they meet the enrollment triggers, or are manually enrolled into the workflow. However, contacts will remain in the workflow until the first action is scheduled to execute, relative to their contact date property. Delays added anywhere else in the workflow are relative to the contact date property, not to the previous action.

Unlike Specific date workflows, actions in a Contact date property workflow will execute at different times for contacts, based on the date value in their contact date property. Some examples of Contact date property workflows are:

  • Sending welcome emails based on a contact’s account activation date.
  • Sending emails with coupons or personalized offers to contacts on their birthday.
  • Automating a series of actions (e.g., creating tasks for the contact owner) based on a contact’s trial expiration date.

Create and manage CRM record associations with workflows

Use workflows to create new associations between records. You can also apply, update, and remove your records’ association labels. When removing association labels, you can also remove all associations with the selected label. This action can also be used with other records associated with the enrolled record.

If you’re creating a record in a workflow, use the Create record action to set the association during record creation. Use Create associations to associate records that already exist. Learn more about creating records with workflows.

Understand requirements and limitations

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to use the workflows tool.

  • Association actions are only available for the following object types: contact, company, deal, ticket, lead, appointments, courses, listings, services, invoice, order, payment, subscription, contract (BETA), credit memo, and custom-objects.
  • These actions cannot be used with other objects such as products, quotes, etc.
  • The Create associations workflow action only creates associations between the selected object types by matching property values. To create associations based on a third-party record, learn how to associate records based on existing associations.
  • You can also create associations for other associated records, not only the enrolled record. For example, instead of the enrolled contact, you can create associations between a contact’s associated company and deals based on matching properties from these other object types. When doing so, you can select from the following targeting options for other object types:
    • All associated records (up to 100 most recently associated)
    • Most recently updated
    • Most recently created
    • First created
    • Most recently associated
    • First associated
    • Associated records with a specific label

Create new associations between records using workflows

Use the Create association workflow action to:

  • Create new associations within CRM records: you can create associations between the enrolled record and other associated record based on matching properties. This includes the following examples:
    • Create associations between contacts and companies when they have matching Company name property values.
    • Create a direct ticket-to-contact association by matching a ticket property to a contact property, such as a custom ticket email field matched to the contact’s Email property.
  • Create associations for associated records of the enrolled record: instead of the enrolled contact, you can create associations between the contact’s associated company and deals based on matching properties from these other object types.

When creating associations, it is recommended to use association labels allow for more management options from within the workflows tool. For example, you can remove associations between records using the Remove association labels action, but not for records without association labels.

To create a new association:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.

  • Click the name of an existing workflow or create a new workflow.

  • Set your enrollment triggers.

  • Click the + plus icon to add an action.

  • In the left panel, click to expand the CRM section. Then, click Create associations.

  • Configure your Create associations action details:

    • Objects to associate from: the object-type of the record where the new association will be created.
      • This will be set to the workflow’s enrolled object type by default (i.e., the enrolled contact in a contact-based workflow).
      • You can also create associations for associated records of the enrolled record, such as an enrolled contact’s associated company.
    • Object to associate to: the object type of the record to be associated with the enrolled record.
      • You can create associations with other objects or activities. For example, you can create an association between a contact and a deal or a contact and a meeting activity.
      • If you’re creating an association with an activity, you can select from the following activity types: Notes, Tasks, Meeting events, Calls, Emails, Communications, and Postal Mail.
    • Create association only without applying any label: select this checkbox to associate records without applying an association label.
    • Select a label to apply: select the association label to be applied to the newly associated record.
      • This option will only appear if you’ve chosen to create an association with an association label.
      • If no labels are available, you must create the association label for that association type first.
    • Create association when there are: for the Create associations action, select the Matching property values option.
      • When matching properties between records, only property values will be used for deciding the match. Generally, the label and internal name of the properties selected will not be used for matching, except for enumeration properties where the internal name will be used for matching.
      • For example, if a contact has a City property with the value Boston, and a company has a Location property with the value Boston, the contact and the company will be matched and an association will be created.
      • Alternatively, if a contact has a City enumeration property with the label Boston Logan International Airport and the internal name Boston, Boston will be used for property value matching.
    • Select a property of enrolled record: select a property from the enrolled record to be matched with a corresponding property from the record to be associated.
    • Select a property to match on: choose a property from the record to be linked to a matching property from the enrolled record. The association will only be created if the matching property values exist on both the enrolled record and the record to be associated. For example, to associate deals with companies, the workflow must match a deal property to a company property with the same value. You cannot use property values from associated records.

Please note:

  • You can only use single-line text, multi-line text, phone number, number, single checkbox, and single select (e.g., radio button) properties when matching records to create associations.
  • When matching records, the property values used are case-sensitive and must match exactly. For example, if the contact’s Company name property value is hubspot, but the company’s Name property value is HubSpot, the records will not be matched and the association will not be created.
  • This action has a daily limit of 5 million action executions, which includes action execution failures. If you haven’t selected the Create association only without applying any label checkbox, an association label will be added to your newly created association, and the action will count as 2 executions towards the limit.

Apply association labels to a record using workflows

Use this action to apply an association label to already associated records. You can choose to apply association labels to all associated records of a certain object type or further refine which associated records to apply the association label. You can also apply association labels for associated records of the enrolled record.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow or create a new workflow.
  • Set your enrollment triggers.
  • Click the + plus icon to add an action.
  • In the left panel, click to expand the CRM section. Then, click Apply association labels.
  • Configure your Apply association label action details:
    • Objects to associate from: the object-type of the record where the association label will be applied.
      • This will be set to the workflow’s enrolled object type by default (i.e., the enrolled contact in a contact-based workflow).
      • You can also apply association labels for associated records of the enrolled record, such as any contacts associated with an enrolled deal in a deal-based workflow.
    • Associated object: the object type of records associated with the enrolled record. Only objects with defined association labels will appear.
    • Select label for associated object: the association label to be applied to the associated records.
    • Apply selected label to all associated records: select this checkbox to apply the association label to all records of the selected object type associated with the enrolled record.
    • Refine which records to access: choose to refine which associated records the action will apply to. This field will only appear if the Apply selected label to all associated records has not been selected.
      • By matching property: the association label will only be applied when the specified property’s value matches the corresponding property’s value in the enrolled record. For example, you may only want to set a Decision maker when both the contact and associated company have the same Country/Region property value. When matching, the property values are case-sensitive.
        • Select a property for the enrolled record: select a property from the enrolled record to be matched with a corresponding property from the associated record.
        • Select a property of associated record: select a property from the associated record to be matched with a corresponding property from the enrolled record.

Please note: when matching properties between records, only property values will be used for determining the match. The label and internal name of the properties selected will not be used for matching. Generally, the label and internal name of the properties selected will not be used for matching, except for enumeration properties where the internal name will be used for matching. For example, if a contact has a City property with the value Boston, and a company has a Location property with the value Boston, the contact and the company will be matched and an association will be created.

    - By property value of enrolled record: the association label will only be applied when the enrolled record meets the requirements of the specified property values. For example, you may only want to apply an association label of Decision maker when the enrolled company has more than five employees.
        - Select a property of enrolled record: select a property from the enrolled record.
        - Operator: select from is equal to or is not equal to operators
        - Enrolled record input value: select or enter a property value to be used with the operator.

    - By property value of associated record: the association label will only be applied when the associated record meets the requirements of the specified property values. For example, you may want to apply an association label of Decision maker only when the contact's Job Title property has been set to Manager.
        - Select a property of associated record: select a property from the associated record.
        - Operator: select from is equal to or is not equal to operators
        - Associated record input value: select or enter a property value to be used with the operator.
  • After setting up your Create associations action, at the top, click Save.

Update a record’s existing association labels using workflows

Replace your existing association label or append a new association label to the associated record. You can also update association labels for associated records of the enrolled record. For example, in a deal-based workflow, you can enroll all closed-won deals that have moved to a closed-won. Then, target contacts associated with those deals who have the Decision Maker label to update the association label to Champion.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow or create a new workflow.
  • Set your enrollment triggers.
  • Click the + plus icon to add an action.
  • In the left panel, click to expand the CRM section. Then, click Update association labels.
  • Configure your Update association label action details:
    • Objects to associate from: the object-type of the record where the updated association label will be applied.
      • This will be set to the workflow’s enrolled object type by default (i.e., the enrolled contact in a contact-based workflow).
      • You can also update association labels for associated records of the enrolled record, such as any companies associated to contacts with an enrolled deal in a deal-based workflow.
    • Associated object: the object associated with the record. Only objects with defined association labels will appear.
    • Select existing label: the current association label used to associate the different records.
    • Add to or replace existing label: you can choose to add to or replace the existing association label.
      • Add to existing label: add an association label to the existing association label. For example, if a contact currently has an association label of Primary, adding a Decision maker association label will update the contacts associated with the enrolled records to Primary and Decision maker association label.
      • Replace an existing label: clear the existing association label and add a new association label. For example, if a contact currently has an association label of Primary contact, choosing this action with a Decision maker association label will update the contacts associated with the enrolled records to Decision maker association label only.
    • Select label to append to or Replace existing label with: select the new association label to append or replace the existing association label with.
  • After setting up your Update association label action, at the top, click Save.

Remove a record’s existing association labels and associations using workflows

Use this action to clear your existing association labels. When doing so, you can also choose to retain or remove the associations between records with this label. You can also choose to remove association labels for other associated records of the enrolled record.

However, it is not possible to remove associations without a label using workflows. Instead, it’s recommended to use the Remove an association or Delete multiple associations between CRM objects API endpoints to remove associations in bulk instead.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow or create a new workflow.
  • Set your enrollment triggers.
  • Click the + plus icon to add an action.
  • In the left panel, click to expand the CRM section. Then, click Remove association labels.
  • Configure your Remove association labels action details:
    • Objects to associate from: the object-type of the record where the association label will be removed.
      • This will be set to the workflow’s enrolled object type by default (i.e., the enrolled contact in a contact-based workflow).
      • You can also clear association labels for other associated records of the enrolled record.
    • Associated object: the object associated to the record. Only objects with defined association labels will appear.
    • Select existing labels to remove: select the association labels to remove from both the enrolled and associated objects.
    • Remove existing associations with this label: select this checkbox to remove the associations between the records.
  • After setting up your Update association label action, at the top, click Save.

Please note: this action has a daily limit of 5 million action executions, including action execution failures.

Create and use action sets

Use actions sets to save and re-use a group of workflow actions. For example, you may want to a set of Set marketing contact status and Email send actions across different workflows.

Before you get started

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to create and use action sets.

  • Action sets are only available in workflows of the same type. For example, only actions sets created in a contact-based workflow will be available to use in other contact-based workflows.
  • Data variables can be used in an action set. However, if you’ve added a new source and used data from an associated object, that data cannot be used in the action set.

Create an action set

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.

  • Click the name of an existing workflow or create a new workflow.

  • Set your enrollment triggers.

  • Click the + plus icon to add an action.

  • In the left panel, under Action sets, click Create action set.

  • In the pop-up box, enter your action set name. Add an optional description.

  • Select Copy all actions from current workflow or Start from scratch.

  • At the bottom, click Next.

  • If you’ve selected Start from scratch:

    • In the left panel, search for and configure your workflow actions.
    • After adding your actions, in the top right, click Save and exit. The action set will be automatically saved.
    • In the left panel, click Add to add the action set to your workflow. Or, click Cancel to exit.

  • If you selected Copy all actions from current workflow:

    • In the editor, review a preview of the actions in your workflow.

    • To add additional actions, click the + plus icon. Then, set up your action.

    • After reviewing or adding your actions, in the top right, click Save and exit. The action set will be automatically saved.

    • In the left panel, click Add to add the action set to your workflow. Or, click Cancel to exit.

Add an action set to a workflow

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow or create a new workflow.
  • Set your enrollment triggers.
  • Click the + plus icon to add an action.
  • In the left panel, under Action sets, click [object] action sets.
  • Click the name of the action set.
  • At the top, click Add. The action set will appear in your workflow editor.

Create Asana tasks with workflows

Asana is a web and mobile application designed to help teams organize, track, and manage their work. Using workflows, you can automate the creation of Asana tasks to keep your teams aligned.

Before you get started

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to use the workflows tool.

  • Before you can create Asana tasks with workflows, you’ll need to connect Asana to your HubSpot account. You can connect the app from the App Marketplace or from within a workflow.
  • The Asana user who connected the integration will be added as a collaborator on any tasks created from a HubSpot workflow.

Create Asana tasks with workflows

To create an Asana task with a HubSpot workflow:
