    • Select the Yes, save the value into a property checkbox.
    • At the top, click Save and continue. This will automatically create a new Edit record action.
      • By default, the action’s fields will be auto-populated and set to update the same record and property.
      • You can further customize this action, learn more about using the Edit record action.
  • After setting up your action, click Save.
Custom formula examples

Using custom formulas, you can customize complex formatting options for your outputs. Learn more about the functions you can use with custom formulas. For example, you can calculate the following

Please note: while it is possible to copy and paste functions into the Formula section, any tokens used such as Action outputs or HubSpot properties must be manually inserted.

Use Case

Formula

Removing special characters from phone numbers.

For example, to standardize the format of phone numbers across your account.

cut(cut(cut([phone], "-"), "*"), "#")

Calculating your sales representative’s commission amount.

For example, to log a commission rate on a deal record.

([Amount] * [commission_rate])

Concatenating strings values from different properties

concat([company_name], [month_and_year])

Reformat data into the time of the day that the action occurs.

For example, to create reports or segments based on the of time of day that specific events occur.

cut( regex_replace(datetimeformat([hs_email_last_open_date], "full"), ".*\b(at\b)", "") ,"Coordinated Universal Time")

Reformat data into the day of the week that the action occurs.

For example, to create reports or segments based on the day of the week that specific events occur.

regex_replace(format_datetime([createdate], "full"), ",.*$", "" )

Use formatted data

After you’ve added the Format data action, you’ll need to set up additional actions to use your formatted data. Within the format data action, you can automatically update an existing property with the formatted data.

You can also add the formatted data to your Google Sheet if you’ve installed the Google Sheets integration.

Update existing properties with formatted data

Set up an Edit record action to update properties with the newly formatted data. The action can use formatted data from any previous Format data action.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow, or create a new workflow.
  • In the workflow editor, click the + plus icon to add a workflow action.
  • In the actions panel, select Edit record.
  • In the left panel, click the Property to edit dropdown menu, then select a property.
  • For checkbox and other select-type properties:
    • Click the Choose a value dropdown menu and select choose data variable.
    • In the Choose a data variable panel, click on the Enrolled [object] dropdown menu and select Action outputs. When copying a value to a different property, the properties must be compatible. Learn more about compatible property types.
    • Click to expand the previous action name and select an action output.
  • For text input properties:
    • Click the Choose a value text box.
    • In the Choose a data variable panel, click on the Enrolled [object] dropdown menu and select Action outputs.
    • Click to expand the previous action name and select an action output.
  • Click Save. With the Edit record action set up, your workflow can now use previously formatted values to update CRM properties.
Add formatted data to Google Sheets

If you’ve installed the Google Sheets integration, you can add formatted data directly to your spreadsheet without updating any properties in HubSpot. For example, if the contacts’ names in the sheet need to be formatted in lowercase, but you still want their names to remain capitalized in HubSpot.

You can connect the Google Sheets app from the App Marketplace or from within a workflow.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow, or create a new workflow.
  • In the workflow editor, click the + plus icon to add a workflow action.
  • In the actions panel, select Create Google Sheet row.
  • Click the Spreadsheet dropdown menu. Then, select the spreadsheet you want to send data to. You can select from the spreadsheets that are owned by or have been shared with the user who connected Google Sheets to HubSpot.
  • Click the Sheet dropdown menu. Then, select the sheet you want to send data to. The Sheet field refers to the tabs at the bottom of your spreadsheet.
  • Set up your Google sheet rows to use formatted data:
    • Click the Header dropdown menu. Then, select the corresponding columns in your Google sheet.
    • Click the Property field.
    • In the data panel, click the View properties or actions output from dropdown menu and select Action outputs.
    • Click to expand a Format data action. To use the previously formatted value, select [output type] value. This action can use formatted data from any previous Format data action.
    • Repeat until you have completed your new row.
  • Click Save.

With the Create Google Sheet row action set up, your workflow can use previously formatted values to add new rows to your Google Sheet without affecting existing properties. Learn more about adding data to Google Sheets with workflows.

Manage workflow enrollment settings

Manage your workflow’s enrollment settings, such as re-enrollment, unenrollment, the enrollment of merged records, and the enrollment of synced Salesforce leads and contacts into workflows.

To configure other settings, such as the workflow’s execution timings, performance notifications, and other workflow connections, learn more about managing your workflow settings.

To configure your workflow’s timing settings:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of your workflow.
  • In the workflow editor, click the Edit > Edit enrollment trigger.
  • In the left panel, click the Settings tab.
    • Re-enroll: By default, records are only enrolled in workflows the first time they meet the workflow enrollment triggers or are enrolled manually. Set up your re-enrollment settings in your workflow to enroll records in a workflow again. Learn more about setting up re-enrollment triggers in workflows.
    • Unenroll if objects meet the following conditions: configure your workflow unenrollment criteria in different workflow types. Setting unenrollment criteria will also prevent records from being enrolled into the workflow. Learn more about setting up unenrollment triggers in workflows,
      • In contact-based workflows, you can choose to remove contacts that no longer meet enrollment criteria, meet the workflow goal, or have been added to suppression segments.
      • In other workflow types, you can set unenrollment triggers to exclude or unenroll records from a workflow.

Please note: if you’re enrolled in the Primary ID Preservation for Merged Records public beta, the primary record will remain enrolled in the workflow while the secondary record is unenrolled by default. Learn more about workflow enrollment behavior for merged records in this beta.

  • If you’re setting up a contact-based workflow, you can configure the following additional settings:

    • Automatically enroll merged records if the updated merged record meets the enrollment conditions: by default, workflows will not enroll merged contacts even if the contact meets the workflow enrollment criteria. However, merged contacts can later enroll if they meet the enrollment triggers again and re-enrollment is turned on.

      • For example, the enrollment trigger is Lifecycle stage is any of Customer. When two contacts that are currently in this stage are merged, the new contact will not enroll in the workflow.

      • However, if the newly merged contact changes lifecycle stage to a different stage, then returns to the Customer stage again, they will be enrolled in the workflow. When merged contacts are enrolled, they will start from the beginning of the workflow.

      • If this setting is turned on, to identify if a merge has triggered a re-enrollment, check the date when the contact was enrolled against the time that the contact was merged.

    • Enable manual enrollment of records from Salesforce using the HubSpot Visualforce window: enroll Salesforce leads and contacts that have synced to HubSpot directly into contact-based workflows. Learn more about enrolling your Salesforce leads or contacts into HubSpot workflows directly from Salesforce. To use this setting you must meet the following requirements:

      • Installed the HubSpot-Salesforce integration.
      • Added the HubSpot Embed or legacy HubSpot Visualforce window to your Salesforce page layouts.

Manage workflow settings

To add unenrollment triggers or a suppression list to determine when records should unenroll from a workflow, learn more about managing unenrollment in workflows.

When configuring your enrollment triggers, the option to add a suppression list or unenrollment triggers will appear in a Settings tab.

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to use the workflows tool.

Timing

Use timing settings to specify when a workflow should or shouldn’t execute actions. By default, workflow actions will run as soon as an enrolled record reaches the action.

This setting won’t affect your workflow enrollment, only actions after enrollment. If you’re facing issues with your workflow enrollment, learn how to troubleshoot common workflow enrollment issues.

Please note: if your HubSpot account does not have a set timezone, the workflow’s timing settings will default to EST (Eastern Standard Time). Learn more about customizing your account’s timezone.

To configure your workflow’s timing settings:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of your workflow.
  • In the top left, click Settings.
  • In the Timing section of the right panel, configure the following:
    • Run actions at specific times only: specify when records can run workflow actions based on your account’s time zone. . For example, to help prevent actions from running outside working days or hours, you can set the workflow to run from Mon - Fri from 9:00AM to 6:00PM only.
      • The timing for the rescheduled action is determined by when the enrolled record reaches the workflow action:
        • If a record reaches an action outside the specified days and time: the workflow will reschedule the action for the earliest available time on the next available day.
        • If a record reaches an action outside the specified days but during the specified execution hours: the workflow will reschedule the action for the same time on the next available day. This’ll also apply if a workflow has a pause date added to the Don’t run actions on specific date setting.
      • To prevent workflow overload, actions are rescheduled to execute within a 15-minute window. For example, if the next available time is 9:00 AM, actions will be rescheduled between 9:00 - 9:15 AM.
      • Delays and if/then branches are not rescheduled, but the following action will be. For example, a deal-based workflow is set to only execute actions Monday through Thursday, 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM. The deal enters a 2-day delay on Thursday, then exits the delay on Saturday. The next action will be rescheduled for Monday between 9:00 - 9:15 AM.
    • Don’t run actions on specific dates: pause a workflow to prevent actions from executing on specific dates. You can also set the dates to pause annually. On those dates, when a record reaches an action, it’ll pause until the next available date. When using pause dates, do note the following:
      • Pause dates will take other date settings into account when rescheduling actions. For example, a workflow is set to only execute actions on Monday to Wednesday from 9AM to 5PM. If you add a pause date that takes place on a Wednesday, any actions scheduled for that Wednesday will be moved to the next Monday at 9AM.
      • Records will still enroll and enter delays and if/then branches on paused days. Once they leave the delay or if/then branch, they will pause at the next action instead.
    • Schedule workflow to turn off automatically: schedule the workflow to turn off after a specific date and time. Learn more about turning off workflows.

Performance notifications

Subscription required An Enterprise subscription is required to configure performance notifications.

Permissions required Super Admin permissions are required to set notification preferences that apply to all users.

Before setting up notifications in the workflow editor:

  • Your user notifications must be turned on. If workflow email notifications are turned off for a user, workflows will still enroll records and run, but that user will not receive workflow notification emails. Learn more about setting up user notifications in HubSpot.
    • This includes custom notifications sent from the workflows tool.
    • This setting is user-specific and will only impact the individual user whose notifications are turned off.
  • Super Admins can set default notification preferences for other users, but preferences set by individual users will take precedence over the defaults.

To turn on user notifications:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Notifications.
  • At the top, click the Email tab.
  • In the Email section, click to toggle the switch on to receive email notifications to your inbox.
  • Scroll down and click to expand the Workflows section.
  • Select the checkboxes next to the relevant notification types.
Set workflow notifications

To trigger your workflow notifications:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of your workflow.
  • In the workflow editor, in the top left, click Settings.
  • In the Performance section of the right panel, configure the following:
    • Get notified when this workflow needs review: notify users and teams each time the workflow’s status changes to Needs review in the automation issues tool. Learn more about troubleshooting automation issues in HubSpot.

      • A notification is sent each time an issue occurs or reoccurs in the workflow.

      • If any issues reoccur or new issues are detected after that, the status will automatically change back to Needs review in the automation issues tool. A new notification will also be sent.

      • To prevent notification overload, notifications are automatically throttled per workflow. If multiple issues occur at once, you will not receive a separate notification for each issue. You can review all active issues in the Needs review tab in the automation issues tool at any time.

      • No additional configuration is required. Notifications will follow your existing workflow notification settings.

    • Get notified if the enrollment rate changes: notify users and teams each time the workflow’s enrollment increases or decreases past a specified threshold. You can choose to use Breeze Intelligence to determine this threshold or manually set a rate of increase or decrease to trigger the notification.
      • Use Breeze Intelligence: use Breeze, HubSpot’s AI, to automatically detect unusual changes to enrollment rates.
        • Breeze Intelligence will compare the enrollment rate each day to the pattern of enrollment during the past month. Unusual dips or spikes in enrollment rates will trigger email notifications.
        • When using this setting, users do not need to set a threshold.
      • Use a manual range: manually set a rate of increase or decrease to trigger the email notifications. When selecting this option, configure the following:
        • Check count: choose whether to check the enrollment count weekly or daily.
          • Weekly: check and send an internal email notification every Friday at 10AM if week-over-week enrollment rates for the workflow increase or decrease by the specified percentage.
          • Daily: check and send an internal email notification every day at 10AM if daily enrollment rates for the workflow increase or decrease by the specified percentage.
        • Increased at least: enter a percentage to trigger this notification if enrollment increases.
          • If enrollment rates increase by more than this percentage, the workflow email notification will be sent.
          • If this option is left blank, notification emails will not be triggered for increased enrollments in the workflow.
        • Decreased by at least: enter a percentage to trigger this notification if enrollment decreases.
          • If enrollment rates decrease by more than this percentage, the workflow email notification will be sent.
          • If this option is left blank, notification emails will not be triggered for decreased enrollments in the workflow.
    • Notification recipients: if the Get notified when this workflow needs review or Get notified if the enrollment rate changes option is toggled on, this field will appear. You can choose to send the corresponding notifications to individual users or specific teams.
      • Send to these users: select specific users to send the workflow notification email. Individual users must have workflow email notifications turned on in their settings to receive this email.
      • Send to these teams: select specific teams to send the workflow notification email. Users in these teams must have workflow email notifications turned on in their settings to receive this email.
    • Compare conversion for each branch and end-point: turn this setting on to begin tracking conversion and performance metrics for the workflow. Learn more about reviewing your workflow’s conversion and performance data.

Connections (contact-based workflows only)

If a contact meets all enrollment criteria for multiple workflows, the contact will enroll in each workflow automatically and immediately. In contact-based workflows, you can specify if a contact should unenroll from other workflows when enrolled into the selected workflow. This setting will not appear in other workflow types.

The setting will only apply at the time of enrollment, it will not unenroll the contact from other workflows in the future. By default, this setting is turned off.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of your workflow.
  • In the top left, click Settings.
  • In the right panel, in the Connections section, toggle on the Unenroll contacts from other workflows when enrolled in this workflow switch. Then, select which workflows the contact should unenroll from:
    • Unenroll from all other workflows: the contact will be removed from all other workflows at the time of enrollment.
    • Unenroll from specific workflows: the contact will be removed from the specified workflows at the time of enrollment.
      • To select a workflow, click the dropdown menu and select the checkboxes next to the workflow you’d like contacts to be removed from.
      • To remove a workflow from this setting, click the x icon next to the workflow name.

Manage workflows in the Agent Hub

After creating a workflow in Agent Hub, you can rename a workflow, or clone a workflow to use as a starting point for a new workflow. If you no longer require a workflow, you can also delete the workflow. If you’d like to retrieve a previous version of a workflow, restore your workflow from the workflow’s version history.

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to use the workflows tool.

Rename a workflow

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub.
  • At the top, click the Workflows tab.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow built in the Agent Hub workflow builder.
  • At the top, click the edit edit icon.
  • In the dialog box, enter a new name for your workflow. You can also enter a description for your workflow and what it does.
  • At the bottom, click Save.

Clone a workflow

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub.
  • At the top, click the Workflows tab.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow built in the Agent Hub workflow builder.
  • At the top, click the verticalMenuIcon three vertical dots icon. Then, select Duplicate.
  • In the dialog box, enter a new name for your workflow.
  • Click Duplicate.

Review and restore previous version of a workflow

From the Agent Hub workflow builder, you can restore previous versions of your workflow from up to 30 days ago. To restore a previous version of your workflow:

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub.
  • At the top, click the Workflows tab.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow built in the Agent Hub workflow builder.
  • In the top left, click the recentlySelectedIcon version history icon.
  • To filter your version history, in the top left, click Filters. Then, you can filter by the following:
    • Edited between: filter by the date that the Agent Hub workflow was edited.
    • Edited by: filter by the user that edited the Agent Hub workflow.
  • To review changes in a previous version of the workflow, click on the workflow version in the left panel. A preview of the workflow with the change highlighted will appear in the Agent Hub workflow canvas.
  • To restore a previous version of the workflow, hover over the version and click the three dot icon. Then, click Restore.

Delete a workflow

Permanently delete an workflow from the Agent Hub workflow builder. Deleted workflows from the Agent Hub workflow builder cannot be cloned or restored.

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub.
  • At the top, click the Workflows tab.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow built in the Agent Hub workflow builder.
  • At the top, click the verticalMenuIcon three vertical dots icon. Then, select Delete.
  • In the dialog box, click Delete workflow.

Manage your unused workflows

To help organize your workflows, HubSpot will automatically add unused workflows to a separate tab on your workflows dashboard.

If you’ve opted into the Account Cleanup (BETA), you can also configure your settings to automatically delete workflows that are turned off and have not been edited in over 6 months.

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to use the workflows tool.

Understand the Unused workflows tab

A workflow will appear in the Unused tab if it meets any of the following conditions:

  • The workflow is turned off.
  • The workflow has not executed any actions in the last 90 days.

A workflow will not count as unused if it’s referenced by a list or another workflow.

Review your unusued workflows

To view your unused workflows:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.

  • At the top of the workflows dashboard, click the Unused tab.

  • To action on your unused workflows:

    • Select the checkboxes next to the workflows that you’d like to take action on. To select all workflows on a page, select the checkbox in the header.
    • At the top, select Assign to team, Assign brand, Move to folder, Delete,Turn off, or Turn off metrics. This action will be applied to all selected workflows.
      • If you do not have permission to take action on one of the selected workflows, the action will be greyed out. You can reselect the workflows and try again.
      • Deleted workflows can be restored within 90 days of being deleted. After 90 days, the workflow will be permanently deleted. Learn more about deleting and restoring workflows.

Manually enroll records in workflows

While records are most commonly enrolled in workflows automatically based on the enrollment triggers, you can also manually enroll records from within a workflow or an object’s index page. For contact-based workflows, you can enroll contacts from within a contact record or segment.

You can also enroll other record types in a workflow using CRM cards. Learn more about enrolling records in workflows using CRM cards.

Before you get started

Understand requirements

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to use the workflows tool.

  • Users with Enroll permission only can enroll records into workflows from CRM cards or any record index pages.

  • Users with both View and Enroll permissions can enroll records directly from workflows.

  • If a user has Edit but no Enroll permission, they will not be able to enroll records, even when editing the workflow. The option to enroll records that currently meet the enrollment criteria after editing a trigger on a workflow, or when turning on a workflow will not appear.

  • If your workflow includes triggers or actions with restricted properties, users must also have access to these properties to enroll records.

  • The workflow must be turned on. You cannot manually enroll records when a workflow is turned off.

Understand limitations
  • This article applies to workflows created in the workflows tool only. For workflows created in the Agent Hub workflow builder, learn how to manually enroll records in Agent Hub workflows instead.
  • Manually enrolled records do not have to meet the enrollment triggers to enroll in the workflow.
  • If you’re trying to manually enroll a record that has previously gone through the workflow, you must turn on and select re-enrollment triggers. Learn more about workflow re-enrollment.
    • If re-enrollment is not turned on for specific records, the record will not be enrolled again. In the enrollment history, the following will appear: Not enrolled. The record was previously enrolled and re-enrollment isn’t enabled for the workflow.
    • This will also apply to bulk enrollment, such as enrolling multiple records from a list or object index page. If re-enrollment is not turned on and the record has been previously enrolled, it will also be skipped during a bulk enrollment.
  • Records cannot be manually enrolled in workflows:
    • If they are currently already active in the workflow.
    • If they’re on the workflow’s suppression list
    • If they meet the workflow’s unenrollment triggers.
  • Contacts cannot be manually enrolled in workflows if the workflow is set to remove contacts from the workflow when they no longer meet the enrollment conditions.
  • Manually enrolled records will always start at the beginning of the workflow. To have records start later or only execute specific steps, create or clone a separate workflow that begins at the desired action, and manually enroll those records there.

Enroll from a workflow

To enroll records directly in workflows, users will need Super Admin or View and Edit workflow permissions. T o enroll a record from within a workflow:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of a workflow.
  • In the top right, click enrEnroll.
  • In the right panel, select from the following:
    • Create a custom filter: select records based on a custom filter to manually enroll records in the workflow. Records refined from the custom filter will be manually enrolled. For example, you may want to manually enroll all contact records in the Evangelist lifecycle stage.
    • From a list: enroll a specified list of records in the workflow. You can only select the same type of list as your workflow for manual enrollment. For example, you cannot select a company or deal-based list for a contact-based workflow.
    • Choose individual contacts: search for and select specific records to enroll in the workflow. After a record is enrolled, the workflow’s enrollment history panel will appear, displaying the recent enrollment. For example, if you want to enroll a specific contact into your workflow, even if the contact does not meet the enrollment trigger criteria.
  • After setting up your manual enrollment criteria, the number of records will display at the bottom of the panel with an objects to be enrolled message. To enroll these contacts, click Enroll.

When manually enrolling a large number of records in a workflow, such as from a list, it is expected to take some time for all records to fully enroll. You may want to wait a few minutes before checking your enrollments.

Enroll records from object index pages

You can enroll records to workflows directly from the object’s index page. This includes all object types, including custom objects.

  • Navigate to your object index page.

  • Select the records to be enrolled:

    • To choose specific records, select the checkbox next to the record to enroll.
    • To select all records on the current page, select the checkbox in the table header.
    • To select all records in the segment, select the checkbox in the table header, then click Select all [X object types] at the top of the table.

  • At the top of the table, click Enroll in workflow.

  • In the dialog box, click the Select a workflow dropdown menu and select an existing workflow. Only published workflows will appear in the options.

  • In the Confirm enrollment field, enter the [number of records] to enroll in the workflow.

  • Select the Yes, I want to enroll all records checkbox.

  • Click Enroll.

Enroll from a contact record

To enroll contacts to workflows directly from a contact record:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly.

  • Click the name of the contact to enroll.

  • In the right panel, Workflow memberships section, click Manage.

  • In the upper right, click Enroll in workflow.

  • In the dialog box, click the dropdown menu and select the workflow.

  • Click Enroll.

Enroll a list of contacts from a segment

Subscription required A Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to enroll contacts via a segment.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Segments. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Segments directly.
  • Click the name of the segment.
  • Select the contacts to be enrolled:
    • To choose specific contacts, select the checkbox next to the contact to enroll.
    • To select all contacts on the current page of the segment, select the checkbox in the table header.
    • To select all contacts in the segment, select the checkbox in the table header, then click Select all [X] contacts at the top of the table.
  • At the top of the table, click the More dropdown menu and select Enroll in workflow.

.

  • In the dialog box, click the Select a workflow dropdown menu and select the workflow to enroll these contacts in.
  • Click Enroll.

Manually run Agent Hub workflows

When creating Agent Hub workflows, you can manually run records from within a workflow. You can select specific records, records from a segment, or use custom filter criteria to determine which records should manually run. You can also create a workflow for users to manually run.

Before you get started

Permissions required Workflows permissions are required to use the Agent Hub workflow builder.

  • To manually run CRM records, you must use a trigger associated with the corresponding record type.
  • When using the Run on demand trigger, records will not automatically run and the workflow will not automatically execute. Each run must be manually triggered by a user.

Use the Run on demand trigger to manually run Agent Hub workflows

To manually trigger your workflow, use the Run on demand trigger type. When using this trigger type, you can run your actions with or without a record. For example, you can use this workflow to manually run a set of agents.

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub.
  • In the top right, click Create and select Workflow.
  • Click Add trigger.
  • In the left panel, select Run on demand.
  • Configure your Run on demand trigger:
    • Click the Inputs for each run dropdown menu and select None, to run your workflow without any associated records, or CRM records.
    • If you’ve selected CRM records as the input type for your workflow run, click the Record type dropdown menu and select a type.
  • After setting up and turning on your workflow, in the top right, click Run.
  • In the dialog box, click Run workflow.

Manually run records in Agent Hub workflows

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub.
  • At the top, click the Workflows tab.
  • In the table, select the workflow you’d like to manually trigger.
  • In the top right, click Run. If you unpublished changes to your workflow, you can choose to run records in the workflow with drafted changes, or the current published workflow.
    • To run records in the drafted workflow, in the top right, click Run workflow draft. This will trigger the workflow and run the selected record. All workflow actions will be executed, including communication actions such as marketing email sends.
    • To run records in the published version of the workflow, in the top right, click the downCaratIcon down icon and select Run published. This may not be the workflow version currently displayed in the Agent Hub workflow builder.
  • In the right panel, configure your [object] to include in this run. You can select from the following:
    • Individual contacts: run the workflow for a specific individual record.
    • From a segment: run the workflow from a segment. Learn more about segments.
    • Create a custom filter: create custom filter criteria based on the record or associated records, and run the workflow for records that meet that criteria.
  • At the bottom, click Run.

Manually unenroll records from workflows

In addition to using suppression lists, goals, or unenrollment triggers to automate workflow unenrollment, records can also be manually unenrolled from workflows.

While all record types can be manually unenrolled from the workflow details page, contacts can also be manually unenrolled from the contact record.

If you’re looking to unenroll contacts from sequences instead, learn more about how sequence unenrollment works, and unenrolling contacts from sequences using workflows.

Before you get started

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to use the workflows tool.

  • The option to unenroll a record from a workflow will only appear if the record is still active in the workflow. If the record has completed the workflow, the option will not appear.
  • Unenrolling a record prevents future workflow actions from executing for the contact. It does not undo actions that have already executed.
  • Manually unenrolling records will remove them from the workflow. However, if they meet re-enrollment triggers, they can enroll in the same workflow again. To prevent contacts from ever re-enrolling in a specific workflow, you can use a suppression list or unenrollment triggers.

Unenroll records from the workflow details page

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Hover over the name of the workflow and click More. Then, select View details.
  • On the workflow details page, click the Action logs tab or the Enrollment history tab.
  • In the upper right of the tab, click the Choose contact dropdown menu and use the search bar to search for the record.
  • In the table, hover over an event for the record, then click Unenroll.
  • In the dialog box, click Yes. The selected record will be unenrolled from the workflow.

Unenroll records in a delay

You can unenroll a record directly when queued in a delay:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • In the table, click the name of the workflow.
  • In the workflow editor, on the specific delay action, click [number of records] in action.

.

  • In the left panel, select the checkboxes next to the records that you’d like to unenroll. It is not possible to unenroll all records in a delay at once.
  • At the top, click Unenroll.
  • In the dialog box, click Yes.

Unenroll contacts from the contact record

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly.
  • Click the name of the contact.
  • In the Workflow memberships card on the right panel, click Manage.
  • To search for a workflow, in the upper right, use the search bar to search for the workflow name.
  • In the status column of the table, click Unenroll.
  • In the dialog box, click Yes, unenroll from workflow.

Migrate workflows from the workflows tool to Agent Hub

Migrate eligible workflows from the workflows tool to the Agent Hub workflow builder. For example, you may want to add actions not available in the workflows tool, such as the Find one associated record to target other associated records.

Alternatively, you can also clone your workflow to Agent Hub to try your workflow with test records before migrating your workflow altogether. When migrating or cloning your workflow to Agent Hub, all triggers and actions will carried over exactly as configured.

Before you get started

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to migrate workflows to Agent Hub.

  • To migrate your workflows from the workflow tool to the Agent Hub workflow builder, you must be opted into the Migrate your legacy Workflow to Agent Builder beta.

  • The option to migrate the workflow will only appear on eligible workflows. If your workflow is not eligible, the Convert to new builder button will be greyed out.

  • Migrating your workflow from the workflows tool to the Agent Hub workflow builder is permanent.

    • After migration, it will not be possible to use the workflows tool to review and edit the workflow, only the Agent Hub workflow builder.

  • When migrating your workflows:

    • If your workflow is in a published state, it will continue running without interruption.

    • The migrated workflow will retain it’s workflow ID, history, and reporting.

    • Your workflow run history will be retained. However, your workflow’s version history will be restarted in the Agent Hub workflow builder. It will not be possible to access previous versions of the workflow.

Migrate your workflow to the Agent Hub workflow builder

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.

  • Click the name of an existing workflow.

  • In the top left, click File and select Convert to new builder. If your workflow is not eligible for migration, this option will be greyed out.

  • In the dialog box, you can migrate your workflow immediately or review a preview of the workflow before migration:

    • To migrate the workflow immediately, click Convert now.
    • To preview the migrated workflow in the new builder before migration, click Preview first. Then, click Convert in the top right.

After migrating your workflow, a Conversion complete message will appear and you’ll be automatically redirected to the migrated workflow in the Agent Hub workflow builder.

Clone your workflow to the Agent Hub workflow builder

Instead of migrating your workflow, you may want to create a separate copy in the Agent Hub workflow builder instead. After reviewing and testing your clone, you can:

  • Delete the clone and convert the original workflow to retain the workflow’s run history and flow id.
  • Keep the clone and delete the original workflow.
  • Turn on the clone and turn off the original workflow.

To clone your workflow from the workflows tool to the Agent Hub workflow builder:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow.
  • In the top left, click File and select Clone. If your workflow is not eligible for migration, this option will be greyed out.
  • In the dialog box, configure your workflow clone:
    • Enter a name for your cloned workflow.
    • In the Clone in section, select New builder.
  • At the bottom, click Clone.

Monitor your workflow health

Use the workflows health page to review the overall health of your workflows. In the workflow reports, you can review and analyze the performance of your workflows. For example, you can analyze an overview of workflows with issues or unused workflows.

To review your overall enrollment data and any enrollment opportunities, learn how to analyze your workflows.

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to use the workflows tool.

Review your workflow health reports

To access your workflow health page:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • At the top, click the Health tab.
  • You can review the following workflow health reports:
    • Workflows needing review: this report shows the count of workflows where the Issue status has been set to Needs review over different time periods.
    • Unused workflows: this report shows the count of workflows that have had no enrollments for at least 90 days over different time periods.
    • Opportunities to review workflows with issues: this report shows the number of workflows where the Issue status has been set to Needs review by date. To view current workflows with a Needs review status, at the bottom of the report, click Needs review.
    • Opportunities to delete unused workflows: this report shows the number of workflows where the workflow has had no enrollments for at least 90 days by date. To view current workflows with a Unused status, at the bottom of the report, click Unused.

Please note: the Similar workflows report has been sunset. You’ll no longer be able to access the report in your account.

Optimize processes with workflows and other tools

Use workflows and other tools to automate processes based on your organization’s needs. Workflows can automate processes both within HubSpot and externally.

For example, Sprocket Supply Co., a sustainable office supply company, is attending a conference. Before the conference, a workflow is used to automatically send a series of informative marketing emails to potential customers. After the conference, workflows are used to evaluate and score leads who have signed up at the conference booth, assign them to different sales representatives, and send this information to a Google Sheet.

Review the following recommendations to determine which workflow templates, actions, and other tools align with your business goals.

Learn more about this feature by joining a small group coaching session

Considerations when building your workflow

Before setting up a workflow and when building out your workflow, it’s recommended to determine your workflow goals and manage your workflow structure.

Determine your workflow goals before building a workflow

Before setting up your workflow, it’s important to determine the purpose or outcomes of the workflow. A workflow may have multiple goals.

For example, when building a lead nurturing workflow, you may want to consider whether each step of the workflow contributes to customer engagement, such as whether an offer is likely to result in customer conversions.

After completing the workflow, performance metrics can be used to create a segment of leads that are engaged and worth investing more effort into. Cold leads can then be removed as marketing contacts.

In this case, the workflow’s outcomes include promoting a product, qualifying leads, and managing your account’s marketing contacts. Use the purpose, outcomes, or quantitative workflow goals as guiding principles when selecting actions and building your workflow.

Manage your workflow structure when building a workflow

When automating your processes, it’s recommended to have multiple workflows, each with a dedicated purpose, rather than building large and complex workflows that encompass multiple goals. When reviewing a well-configured workflow, it should be possible to discern the purpose of the workflow.

For example, after the conference, a sales manager at Sprocket Supply Co. creates one workflow for lead scoring and enrichment, and another for lead assignment.

Understand different HubSpot tools and features for your automation goals

Below, review different recommendation types for your automation and process goals. Before determining which approach to use to solve a business need, it’s recommended to consider the different approaches available and whether they align with your goals, using automation or otherwise.

Each recommendation can be used separately, but in many instances, works best when used simultaneously. For example, while using a workflow template may be the quickest to implement, it may still be necessary to customize with additional workflow actions. Or, when managing your marketing contacts, it’s recommended to both use maximum contact limits and a workflow to automatically update your marketing contact status.

  • Templates: automatically generate a template workflow with placeholder actions. Learn how to use templates to create workflows. You can also install templates from the HubSpot Marketplace.
  • Actions: individual actions recommended when configuring a workflow for a specific purpose. To achieve your goals, use different combinations of workflow actions, as well as outcomes from earlier actions with other actions in a workflow. Learn more about the different workflow actions available.
  • Other features: when working toward your business goals with automation, there may be different strategies available, including using other tools instead of, or together with workflows.

Sprocket Supply Co. is planning to update an Industry or Interested in property on all contact records.

To do a one-time update, they can enroll a list into a workflow, and use different branching methods and the Edit record workflow action to update the property.

Alternatively, if this data already exists in another platform, it may be more efficient to manually import that data.

Workflow goals and recommendations

Below, you can review the following common business goals and possible ways to approach them, with using workflows and other automation tools, within HubSpot.

Nurture new contacts

Subscription required A Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to send automated emails with workflows.

As part of your digital marketing efforts, use email marketing to nurture new contacts to build brand loyalty, promote new products, and also qualify leads that are interested based on email clicks and opens.

Recommendation

Instead of spending time manually setting up workflows, use the following templates as starting points to build common lead nurturing workflows for new contacts.

Example

Sprocket Supply Co. sends a welcome email with a list of products that they may be interested in (e.g., office chairs, printers, and more) to users who have registered on their website.

They can later enroll records into other workflows based on which product links customers have clicked on in this email.

Recommended workflow templates

  • Send an email series when a form is submitted
  • Send welcome email to new customers
  • Send welcome email to new blog subscribers
  • Send welcome email after first login
  • Add new contacts to a nurture campaign
Nurture existing contacts

Subscription required A Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to send automated emails with workflows.

Similar to nurturing new contacts, use email marketing to continue building brand loyalty, promoting products based on your existing customers’ interests, and also continue qualifying customers that may become your brand evangelists.

Recommendation

Instead of spending time manually setting up workflows, use the following workflow templates to build common lead nurturing workflows for existing contacts.

Example

Sprocket Supply Co. uses a workflow to send a discount code to existing customers on their first purchase anniversary. This encourages customers to repurchase and acts as a reminder to refill any necessary office supplies.

Recommended workflow templates

  • Email website visitors based on page visited
  • Email customers on an anniversary
  • Send re-engagement email to cold leads
Prioritize the correct leads

Subscription required A Marketing Hub or Sales Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use the lead scoring tool.

Use different tools to ensure that you have all the necessary information to prioritize the right prospects and focus on companies already showing buying signals to shorten your sales cycle.

Recommendation

Use both workflows and other tools such as lead scoring, buyer intent, and prospecting agent to accurately identify high-value prospects.

Then, use workflows to enroll records to prospecting agent. Ensure that no potential deals are missed by notifying relevant stakeholders such as sales teams, individual reps, and sales managers.

Example

Sprocket Supply Co. uses lead scoring to identify potential prospects. For example, customers in industries that often use paper and printing supplies, such as legal services, are scored higher.

When records reach a certain threshold and are considered qualified, they are automatically enrolled in prospecting agent using a workflow. Within the same workflow, a sales rep is notified with information on the prospect in the notification email.

Recommended tools for qualifying leads

  • Enrich record

  • Lead scoring

  • Prospecting agent

  • Buyer intent

Recommended workflow templates

  • Auto-Enrich Target Account Companies workflow template
  • Update company properties based on defined criteria workflow template
  • Get notified when a lead becomes qualified workflow template
  • Notify your team when a high-value company is identified workflow template

Recommended workflow actions

  • Enrich record workflow action
  • Enroll in prospecting agent workflow action
  • Send an internal email notification

Accurately assign leads

Subscription required A Sales Hub or Service Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use the Rotate record to owner workflow action.

Seats required When assigning users with this action, users must have a paid sales or service seat.

Accurately and automatically assign records to sales reps to ensure that potential deals are managed in a timely manner.

Recommendation

In addition to the recommended workflow templates, if you have specific requirements for lead assignment, you can use workflow branching to route records based on properties such as country, company size, and industry. Then, use the Edit record workflow action to update the [object] owner property.

Example

Sprocket Supply Co. receives a quotation request on their international website. Contacts are automatically directed to different branches in the workflow based on region, such as APAC, EMEA, and NAM.

Then, within the Rotate record to owner action, contacts are assigned to specific users based on random assignment.

Recommended workflow templates

  • Assign contacts to an owner based on their U.S. region workflow template
  • Assign new web leads to contact owners workflow template.

Recommended workflow actions

  • Rotate record to owner workflow action
  • Edit record workflow action
  • Workflow branches
Accurately align data across different applications

When working across your tech stack, to ensure that all stakeholders are aligned and that decisions are made with the most accurate information, you’ll want to make sure that your data is synced between HubSpot and other external applications.

Recommendation

Use the import tool for one-time data transfers. To ensure that your data is continuously kept up to date, use data sync for one way, or bidirectional syncs.

When aligning your data, to ensure that data from HubSpot can be parsed across different platforms, use the Format data workflow action to standardize your property values. For example, use a custom formula function to remove any additional spaces and format your string as a number.

It is also recommended to use Agent Hub workflows if you’d like to take action or include specific pieces of data based on external applications. For example, you can trigger a workflow based on a webhook sent by your external application, then use data from that webhook with the Edit record workflow action to update your CRM record in HubSpot.

Example

Sprocket Supply Co. manages marketing campaigns and assets from HubSpot, and direct sales from Salesforce. They keep their record information synced using the HubSpot-Salesforce integration.

When a contact is influenced by a campaign in HubSpot, they’re added to a corresponding campaign in Salesforce using the Set a Salesforce campaign workflow action. This allows them to have accurate attribution reporting across their entire tech stack.

Recommended data management tools

  • Import tool
  • HubSpot data sync
  • Agent Hub workflows (BETA)

Recommended workflow actions

  • Format data workflow action
  • Connected app workflow actions
  • Edit record workflow action
Use custom solutions in your workflows

Subscription required A Data Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use the Custom code workflow action.

Beyond the existing actions available within the workflows tool, use custom code actions and create custom workflow actions to meet any specific automation requirements, both within HubSpot and externally.

Recommendation

For more complex business needs, you may require custom solutions for automating your processes. In these cases, use the Custom code workflow action to write and execute JavaScript or Python (beta) to extend workflow functionality both within HubSpot and externally.

When using custom code actions in the Agent Hub workflow builder, describe your required functionality within Breeze Assistant to automatically generate the corresponding code.

If you need to automate processes with external applications, create custom workflow actions to integrate your service within HubSpot’s workflows. For example, create a workflow action to invoke a serverless function, or fetch options from external APIs.

Example

Sprocket Supply Co. assigns leads within North America based on the postal code of the customer’s business address. To do so, they build a custom HubDB table to store their lead assignment logic (e.g. postal code X is covered by owner Y). Then, within a workflow, they add a custom code action to use postal code as input, reference the HubDB table, and assign it with the corresponding owner.

After making a sale, a custom workflow action connected with their warehousing and logistics platform is used to create and send an order, using fields derived from corresponding property values such as order details, customer address, and more.

Recommended data management tools

  • Build custom workflow actions
  • Agent Hub workflows (BETA)

Recommended workflow actions

  • Custom code workflow action
Manage marketing contacts

Subscription required A Marketing Hub Starter, Professional, or Enterprise with marketing contacts subscription is required to use and manage marketing contacts.

Manage the number of marketing contacts in your account to both market to the contacts that have potential and still manage the volume of marketing contacts in your account.

Recommendation

In addition to the built-in tools such as maximum limits and user permission restrictions, use the Set marketing contact status workflow action to automatically manage the number of marketing contacts in your account.

Example

To prioritize engaged contacts and manage their volume and costs surrounding marketing contacts, Sprocket Supply Co. uses a workflow to automatically set contacts as non-marketing when they’ve bounced from their marketing emails.

Recommended marketing contact management tools

  • User marketing contact permissions
  • Marketing contact maximum limits
  • Contact tier notifications

Recommended workflow actions

  • Set marketing contact status workflow action

Additional resources

  • Community workflow library
  • Automate your processes

Organize and manage your workflows

Organize workflows by managing your workflow tables and grouping your workflows into folders. For example, you can group your workflows into separate folders for different purposes, such as contact assignments or lead nurturing workflows.

To analyze your overall workflow performance, you can use the workflow Analyze tab. If you’ve set up multi-account management (BETA), you’ll also be able to copy workflows between accounts.

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to use the workflows tool.

Understand your workflows index page

From the workflows page, you can navigate to the following tabs:

  • All workflows: all workflows created directly in the workflows tool and workflows created from other tools such as forms, emails, tickets, or deals.
  • Needs review: workflows that have encountered errors in the last 7 days will display. Learn how to identify and troubleshoot common workflow errors.
  • Unused: workflows that are turned off or haven’t executed any actions in the last 90 days will display. Learn how to manage your unused workflows.
  • Deleted: workflows that have been deleted in the past 90 days will display. You can restore deleted workflows from the Recently deleted tab, learn how to delete and restore workflows.

Manage your workflow views

To find specific workflows, you can either search by name or filter your workflows. You can also update the columns in the views to display specific workflow data. Before choosing what to display on the workflow view, learn more about workflow details.

When reviewing your workflows, if an existing workflow references a restricted property:

  • Users with View only permissions cannot edit the workflow. This includes enrollment triggers and other workflow actions. The workflow will display in view-only.
  • Users with no access to the properties will not be able to access the workflows. The workflow will be greyed out for the user on the index page and won’t be accessible.

To manage your workflow views:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • In the top search bar, enter a keyword to search for a specific workflow. The search will match the keyword with the name or description of the workflow you want to locate.
  • You can refine your search results by filtering by workflow type:

    • On or Off: filter by workflows that are turned on or off.

    • Type: filter by the workflow object type, such as deal or company-based workflows.

    • Brands: if you have a Marketing Hub Enterprise subscription and the Brands add-on, you can filter by the workflow’s assigned brands.

    • Creator: filter by the user that created the workflow.

    • Teams: filter by the team that the workflow is assigned to.

    • Folder: filter by the folder the workflow has been added to.

    • Created in: filter by the tool that the workflow was created from, such as the forms tool or the workflows app.

    • Action type: filter by the actions within a workflow. For example, you can filter by workflows that contain a delay or a Create record action.

    • Advanced filters: filter by advanced workflow details such as workflow enrollments or triggers. Learn more about filtering your records in HubSpot.

      • In the right panel, click Add filter.

      • To add more filter criteria, click AND or OR. Learn more about using AND and OR logic in HubSpot.

      • To clone a filter group, click Clone.

      • To delete a filter group, click Delete.

      • To remove existing filter criteria, hover over the criteria and click the delete delete icon.

  • You can add additional filter options to your table with quick filters. These will appear next to the standard filters listed.
    • To add an additional quick filters, click the addIcon add icon. In the pop-up box, select a quick filter.
    • To edit the quick filters displayed, click the edit pencil icon. In the dialog box, configure your quick filters:
      • To arrange your quick filters, click and drag the drag icon next to your quick filter to place them in order.
      • To remove a quick filter from the table display, click the delete delete icon.
      • To add another quick filter, click + Add quick filter. You can add up to 5 quick filters.
      • To remove all quick filters, click Delete all quick filters.
  • To customize the workflow data displayed in the view, in the top right, click Actions > Edit columns. Update the view from the dialog box:
    • On the left, select the checkboxes next to the properties or associations you want to appear in the view.
    • On the right, click and drag the properties to rearrange them in the view.
    • To remove a property, click x.
    • Click Save.
  • To save the selected filters as a view, click Save view in the top right.
  • In the dialog box, enter a name for your view and select which users can access the saved view. Then, click Save.

Organize your workflows with folders

Organize your workflows into folders on the workflows dashboard. Once created, folders will display on the dashboard with your workflows. Within a folder, you can also apply filters to further refine a search, or set a folder as your default workflow view.

If you have an Enterprise subscription, you can also automatically file workflows using the Workflow Filing Agent.

Create and manage folders

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.

  • In the top right, click the Folders tab.

  • In the upper left, click Create folder.

  • In the dialog box, enter the folder name. Then, click Save.

  • To refine the workflows displayed in your folder, at the top, select and apply different filters. Learn more about the filter types available,

  • To set a folder as your workflow tool’s default view:

    • In the top right, click Set as default view. You may need to scroll to reach this option.
    • In the dialog box, click Set as default.
      • Moving forward, whenever you navigate to your workflows tool, you will be automatically directed to this folder.
      • To remove the folder as a default, you must set another folder or view as the default. For example, you can set the All workflows view as a default.
Rename or delete a folder

To edit or delete an existing folder:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • In the top right, click the Folders tab.
  • To change a folder’s name:
    • In the left sidebar menu, click on the folder.
    • In the top left, click Actions and select Rename folder.
    • In the dialog box, enter your new folder name. Then, click Save.
  • To delete a folder:
    • In the left sidebar menu, click on the folder.
    • In the top left, click Actions and select Delete folder.
    • In the dialog box, click Delete folder.
Move workflows to folders
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • In the top right, click the Folders tab.
  • To move individual workflows to a folder:
    • Hover over the workflow and click Actions. Then, click Move to folder.
    • In the dialog box, select a folder.
    • At the bottom, click Move.
  • To move workflows to a folder in bulk:
    • On the Folders tab, select the checkboxes next to the workflows you want to move into the folder.
    • At the top of the table, click Move to folder.
    • In the dialog box, select the desired folder, then click Move.

Manage your workflows

From the workflows table, you can edit, clone, or take further action on your workflows.

Please note: workflows with more than 500 actions may encounter issues when cloning. If you’ve encountered an issue, you can try reducing the number of actions, splitting the workflow into smaller workflows before cloning, or manually recreating the workflow instead.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • To edit a workflow, hover over your workflow and click Edit.
  • To duplicate a workflow, click Clone.
  • To take further action on your workflow, click More and select from the following:
    • View details: in your workflow details page, review your workflow performance, action logs, and enrollment history.
    • View connections: review a list of connections to your workflow. This includes assets and tools that your workflow may use such as emails, forms, and more, as well as any tools that may use your workflow.
    • Assign to team (Enterprise only): assign the workflow to a team.
    • Assign brand: associate the workflow with a brand. You must have a Marketing Hub Enterprise subscriptions and the Brands Add-On.
    • Move to folder: move your workflow to a specified folder.
    • Delete: delete your workflow. Any deleted workflows can be restored within 90 days of being deleted. Learn more about deleting and restoring workflows.
    • Edit campaign: associate contact-based workflows with campaigns. Learn more about associating your asset and content with campaigns.

Assign brands to your workflows

Users with Marketing Hub Enterprise subscriptions who have purchased the Brands Add-On can assign workflows with brands.

By default, workflows are not assigned to a brand. A workflow does not have to have a brand assigned. However, brands are useful for organizing your workflow.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • To assign an individual workflow to a specific brand:
    • Hover over the name of the workflow and click More. Then, select Assign brand.
    • If the workflow already has a brand assigned, hover the name of the workflow and click More, then select Change brand.
  • To assign multiple workflows in bulk:
    • In the workflows table, select the checkboxes next to the workflows that you want to assign to the same brand.
    • At the top, click Assign brand. If the workflow has an existing brand, it will be reassigned to the new selected brand.
  • In the dialog box, click the brands dropdown menu and select a brand. Only one brand can be assigned to a workflow.
  • At the bottom, click Save.

Resolve invalid filter errors in workflow enrollment triggers

When a property value is merged or deleted, or if the internal value is edited, any workflows that enroll based on that value will show an error. This is because the workflow is trying to use a property value that no longer exists.

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to create and edit workflows.

To fix this error, by updating your enrollment criteria:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of the workflow displaying the error.
  • In the workflow editor, click the Enrollment trigger box.
  • In the left panel, locate the trigger with the error, then click the trigger to edit it.
  • Remove the property value that’s causing the error by clicking the x next to the filter.
  • Click Update filter.
  • Click Save. The workflow will no longer show an error for the enrollment trigger.

Restore workflow CRM property changes

Use the workflow data restore feature to undo CRM property changes made by a specific workflow, including changes from workflow actions such as the Edit record action. Instead of manually fixing records or rolling back unrelated data, you can restore only the values that were changed by a specific workflow during a selected timeframe.

From a workflow’s revision history, you can also review a history of changes made to the workflow and restore those changes. Learn more about viewing and restoring changes in workflows.

Understand limitations and considerations

Permissions required Super Admin permissions are required to restore workflow CRM property changes.

  • Restoring changes from a selected workflow run or action will restore all eligible field updates from that run or action, including changes you may want to keep. Consider this before proceeding. For example, this can restore previous owner values, and records become unassigned if they had no owner before the workflow ran.
  • You can only restore workflow CRM property changes from the last 14 days.
    • Workflow CRM property changes older than 14 days cannot be restored.
    • If the restore option is unavailable or the changes are older than 14 days, manually restore the values by identifying the affected records and properties, exporting records with record IDs, using property history or backups to find previous values, then importing the corrected values back into HubSpot.
  • Workflow CRM property changes restore only affects records directly impacted by the selected workflow. It will not restore changes made by other impacted workflows. For example, if an action in the workflow enrolls records into a different workflow, CRM property changes made by the other workflow will not be restored. Only changes made by the original workflow.
  • To restore your workflow CRM property changes, you must turn on your HubSpot user notifications to receive an in-app or email Review before you restore notification.
  • Changes made by custom-coded workflow actions will not be restored. Undo these changes separately, such as with another workflow, an import of corrected data, or via an API.
  • Changes to subscription statuses, such as via the Manage communication subscriptions workflow action, will not be restored. Instead, learn how to manage your contacts’ subscriptions.
  • It is recommended to turn off your workflow before restoring CRM property changes from a specific workflow to prevent any further CRM changes.

Restore workflow CRM property changes from the workflow editor

To restore property changes from your workflow editor:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.

  • Click on the workflow with CRM property value changes that you’d like to restore.

  • In the top right, click Performance history and select Enrollment history.

  • In the right panel, click Restore CRM changes.

  • In the dialog box, configure the following:

    • Source: the source of your CRM property restore. By default, this will be set to Workflow.
    • Workflow name: the name of the workflow where the CRM property values are to be restored. By default, this will be the selected workflow’s name.
    • Objects: select the object types that you’d like to be restored. For example, you can choose to restore only CRM changes for company or deal objects.
    • Run trigger started on: set your start and end timeframe. You can restore CRM property changes caused by workflows for up to 14 days ago.

  • To reset your triggers, at the bottom, you can select Clear all filters.

  • At the bottom, click Prepare preview.

    • When the preview is ready, you will receive a notification. Then, you can preview the records to be restored and complete your restore.
    • You must turn on your HubSpot user notifications to receive this notification.

Restore workflow CRM property changes from the workflow’s details page

To restore property changes from your workflow details page:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.

  • Hover over workflow with CRM property value changes that you’d like to restore and click More. Then, select View details.

  • Click the Action logs or Enrollment history tab.

  • In the top right, click Restore CRM changes.

  • In the dialog box, configure the following:

    • Source: the source of your CRM property restore. By default, this will be set to Workflow.
    • Workflow name: the name of the workflow where the CRM property values are to be restored. By default, this will be the selected workflow’s name.
    • Objects: select the object types that you’d like to be restored. For example, you can choose to restore only CRM changes for company or deal objects.
    • Run trigger started on: set your start and end timeframe. You can restore CRM property changes caused by workflows for up to 14 days ago.

  • To reset your triggers, at the bottom, you can select Clear all filters.

  • At the bottom, click Prepare preview.

    • When the preview is ready, you will receive a notification. Then, you can preview the records to be restored and complete your restore.
    • You must turn on your HubSpot user notifications to receive this notification.

Complete your CRM property changes restore

After preparing your restore preview from the workflow editor or details page, when the preview is ready, you’ll receive a Review before you restore notification.

  • From your in-app or email notification, click Review and restore data. You’ll be automatically directed to a restore preview page with the details of your records to be restored to their former state.
  • At the top, you can review records to be restored based on the change type:
    • Deleted records: CRM records that were deleted by the workflow.
    • Created records: newly created CRM record from the workflow.
    • Modified properties: changes in property values in the CRM record from the workflow.
  • To restore specific records to their former state, select the checkbox next to the records that you would like to restore.
  • To select and restore all changes displayed, select the checkbox in the top left of the table. Then, at the top of the table, click Select all [x] records.
    • This will select all changes only on the selected tab.
    • To select changes across all types, you’ll need to navigate between tabs and select all records in each tab.
  • In the bottom right, click Restore [x].
  • In the dialog box, enter the count of records to restore. Then, click Restore [x] changes. When your CRM record restore is complete, you’ll receive an email or in-app notification, depending on your notifications settings.

Review a record’s workflow paths and actions

From your workflow enrollment history, you can review and trace the enrollment history and path of your records through the workflow using an interactive diagram in the editor.

You can highlight exactly what happened with each enrollment, including the branch paths followed and the eventual endpoint reached. For example, you can use this to troubleshoot why a record went down a particular branch or why it may not have completed a specific action.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of the workflow to navigate to the workflow editor.
  • In the top right of the editor, click Performance history > Enrollments history. Or, from the navigation menu click View > Enrollment history.
  • To search for a specific object, use the search bar and enter the name of the record you’re searching for.
    • If you cannot find an expected record, check that your chosen date range is wide enough.
    • Historical data for enrollments is stored in HubSpot for 6 months.
  • To view additional details, hover over the name of the object and click View logs. The workflow history for the record appear.
    • In each individual record’s workflow history, review all events. To expand or collapse a specific section, click therightarroArarrow icon next to the section.
    • In the workflow preview, you can review the workflow and the success or failure of each action for the record.
    • In the workflow preview, you can review the path of your workflow. Selecting a step within the preview will expand or collapse that step’s matching log in the side panel. In the preview:
      • Successful actions and paths are highlighted in green.
      • Actions with errors are highlighted in red.
  • To exit the workflow enrollment history, in the top left, click the X icon.

Review Agent Hub workflow performance

After creating your Agent Hub workflow, you can review your workflow’s performance directly within the workflow editor.

Before you get started

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to use the Agent Hub workflows tool.

  • When reviewing your Agent Hub workflow performance, only 30 days of run history will appear.
  • If records are merged, both merged records will be unenrolled from the workflows.

Please note: if you’re enrolled in the Primary ID Preservation for Merged Records public beta, when merging records, the primary record will remain enrolled in the workflow while the secondary record is unenrolled by default. Learn more about workflow enrollment behavior for merged records in this beta.

Review Agent Hub workflow performance

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Agents > Agent Hub.
  • At the top, click the Workflows tab.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow built in the Agent Hub workflow builder.
  • In the top right, click Run history.
  • In the right panel, review your workflow details:
    • Started: the count of runs that have started in this workflow.
    • Done: the count of completed runs for the workflow.
    • Action required: the count of runs where an error may have occurred.
  • To review the run history of a specific record, click the Choose a trigger source dropdown menu. Then, configure the following:
    • Trigger source type: select the object-type that you’d like to review the run history for.
    • Trigger source: select the specific record that you’d like to review the run history for.
