  • To filter your data, click the filter icon. You can filter based on the following:
    • Date triggered: filter your data by when the workflow was run.
    • Version: filter your data by the workflow version.
    • Status: filter your data by the progress of the run. You can select from Done, In Progress, or Action required. To filter your runs by error, you can select the Only runs with errors checkbox.

Review your workflow’s conversion and performance data

Review and use your workflow actions’ conversion and performance data to analyze the effectiveness of each section of the workflow and optimize your automation strategies to improve business outcomes.

Use this feature to identify the workflow path with the most enrollments, review the counts of enrollments that reached each step, the counts of errors at each step, and the conversion rate of each branch and end point. You can also filter this data by workflow version to see how past changes affected these conversion rates.

To analyze your overall workflow performance and automation opportunities, learn how to understand the workflow’s Analyze tab.

Permissions required Super Admin or Edit permissions for workflows are required to track metrics in workflows.

Turn on metric tracking

To begin tracking the performance of your workflow, you must turn on the Metrics setting. This setting must be turned on in each workflow. This can also be turned on in the workflow’s performance settings.

You can apply this setting for up to 20 workflows in your account.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.

  • Click the name of your workflow.

  • At the top, click View > Metrics.

  • In the right panel, click Turn on metrics.

  • In the top left, you can click the X icon to exit the Metrics screen.

Review your workflow’s metrics

The workflow’s conversion and performance data will only include data from when the Turn on metrics option was selected. It will not include retroactive data, you must filter your metrics to select from a range of workflow versions.

Please note: metrics tracking provides a historical view of enrollments. Due to the larger data volume, there may be a lag of several hours after an object unenrolls before it’s reflected in the aggregate performance data.

To review the metrics for your workflow:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.

  • To identify workflows with metric tracking turned on:

    • In the top right, click Advanced filters. You may need to scroll horizontally to reach this option.
    • In the right panel, click + Add filters.
    • Search for and select Metrics status.
    • Set the filter to Is equal to and select True.
    • Click Apply filter.

  • Click the name of your workflow.

  • At the top, click View > Metrics. In the right panel, you can review the count of records that have started the workflow, records that are currently in the workflow, and records that have completed the workflow.

  • To further filter your metrics:

    • View metrics for completed enrollments that started between: use the date picker to review enrollment data between specific dates.
    • Choose a canvas in this date range: select the version of the workflow within the above dates.

  • After filtering your metrics, in the Summary section of the right panel, you can review the following:

    • The overall count of contacts enrolled.
    • The count of contacts that successfully completed an action or continued down a branch.

  • In the Conversion metrics tabs of the right panel, you can review the percentage of contacts that successfully executed an action, continued down each branch, or ended the workflow.

  • To review all enrollments that have reached a particular step, hover over the action and click Matching enrollments. The Only enrollments that reached field in the enrollment history will be automatically set to the selected action. Learn more about reviewing your workflow’s enrollment history.

  • In the workflow preview, you can review the following:

    • The total enrollment count for the workflow.

    • The percentage of enrollments that reached each endpoint.

    • For any branch action, the percentage of enrollments that continued along each branch path.

    • For each action, the count of un-enrollments that occurred due to the action.

    • Any errors that may have occured on the action. If an error has occurred, the error icon will appear. The count of errors will appear next to the error icon .

  • In the preview, the overall workflow path with the most records and any individual branch paths followed by the most records will be highlighted in green.

    • If multiple branches have the same performance data, the first branch will take precedence when reviewing the highlighted path in the workflow preview.
    • If a path doesn’t have any actions or only has a go to action, the most travelled path may not be highlighted as expected. When tracking metric data, it is recommended all paths to have at least one action, or more than one action in addition to a go to action.

Review your workflow’s enrollment history

After turning on a workflow, you can review the workflow’s enrollment history from the workflow editor. From the workflow’s enrollment history, you can also review the workflow’s enrollment and path for individual records. You can also review a workflow’s enrollment history from the Enrollment history tab on the workflow’s details page.

Historical data for enrollments is stored in HubSpot for 6 months. There is a 100,000 log limit for successful workflow executions per day. Once the limit is exceeded, success and info logs will not be stored for the rest of the day, but error logs will continue to appear.

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to use the workflows tool.

Filter your workflow’s enrollment history

To filter your workflow’s overall enrollment history:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.

  • Click the name of the workflow to navigate to the workflow editor.

  • In the top right of the editor, click Performance history > Enrollments history. Or, from the navigation menu in the top left, click View > Enrollment history.

  • In the right panel, the enrollment history will be displayed in reverse chronological order, with the most recent events appearing at the top. To filter the enrollment history, click the date pickers and select custom date range.

  • To filter your enrollment history by the workflow version that the records are enrolled into, click the Filter by workflow versions checkbox.

    • When the checkbox is selected, a preview of the workflow version will appear.
    • If the checkbox is not selected, the workflow preview will not appear.

  • When filtering the enrollment history by workflow version, you can set up the following additional filters. These additional filters will not appear if the Filter by workflow versions checkbox is not selected.

    • Workflow versions: filter by records that enrolled in specific versions of the workflow, that share the same flow.
      • Select the first dropdown menu and select the starting version for the range of your workflow versions.
        • The options will be grouped by Uses the same flow diagram. The versions within each group will have the same number, type, and order of actions. But the details for each action may vary between versions.
        • If the actions have been configured differently between versions, the details of the action will not appear. Instead, you will see the following alert: Details are hidden because the workflow versions filter includes multiple versions, and these details have changed between them.
      • Select the second dropdown menu and select the last version for the range of your workflow versions.
        • Only workflow versions that use the same flow and that are newer than the starting version will appear as options.
        • To see the widest range of versions within, select the oldest version for the first dropdown menu and the newest version of the group for the second dropdown menu.
    • Date range - within those versions: filter by the date range when the records enrolled into the workflow.
      • This will be limited by the dates of the workflow versions selected.
      • The newest date in this filter may be more recent than the date displayed in Workflow versions filter. The Workflow version filter is based on the creation date of that version of the workflow, while enrollments may have occurred after that date.
    • Only enrollments that reached: filter by records that have reached specific step in the workflow.
      • You can select more than one step. As long as the step’s action has been executed, the record will be visible, whether it proceeds through the workflow, completes it, or unenrolls after.
      • If no step have been selected, all enrollments that match the date range filter will appear.
      • To add or remove a step:
        • To add a step, click the dropdown menu and select the checkbox next to the action. Or, click the action card in the workflow preview. When a step has been added, the step will be highlighted in the preview.
        • To remove a step, click the x icon next to the action.

Export your workflow’s enrollment history

Permissions required Super Admin, or Workflows and Export permissions are required to export workflow enrollment history.

After filtering your enrollment history, you can export the filtered data to a static segment. Learn more about static segments.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of the workflow to navigate to the workflow editor.
  • In the top right of the editor, click Performance history > Enrollments history. Or, from the navigation menu click View > Enrollment history.
  • After filtering your enrollment history, click Export to list.
  • In the dialog box, enter a name for your new static segment.
  • Click Export.

Rotate conversation owners with workflows

Use the Rotate record to owner action in conversation-based workflows to automatically move a conversation to another inbox and assign it to a specific user or team based on access to the inbox.

Seats required An assigned Service Seat is required for users selected in the action. Users without an assigned Service Seat cannot be rotate and assigned to a conversation.

Before you get started

  • When using this action, changing the assignment on closed conversations will result in the conversation being reopened. It is recommended to exclude closed conversations when setting up the workflow’s enrollment criteria.
  • If using rules-based bots, it is recommended to exclude bot-based chatflows when setting up the enrollment criteria and using the Send to Team Member action directly within the chatflow instead.

Rotate conversation owner in a workflow

To rotate a conversation owner or move a conversation to a different inbox for a conversation from a workflow:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Select an existing conversation-based workflow, or create a new conversation-based workflow from scratch:
    • In the upper right, click Create workflow, then select From scratch.
    • In the left panel, click Met filter criteria.
    • In the left panel, select Conversation.
    • Continue setting up your enrollment criteria.
  • In the workflow editor, click the + add icon.
  • In the left panel, click CRM to expand the section. Then, select Rotate record to owner.
  • Set up your action:
    • Target inbox: select a target inbox. Only active, non-Help Desk inboxes will appear in the list.
    • Assign to: select an assignment method. By default, this will overwrite any existing conversation owners. You can select from the following:
      • Customer agent: assign the conversation to your Customer Agent. Learn more about setting up a Customer Agent.
      • Specific users and teams: assign the conversation to specific users and teams.
        • Only teams that have access to the target inbox and have users with an assigned Sales or Service seat will appear in the list.
        • Only users with access to the target inbox and an assigned Sales or Service seat will appear in the list.
        • You can also select the option to Assign to available users only. When this option is selected, if there are no available users, the conversation will be set to unassigned.
        • By default, conversations will be assigned using balanced distribution.
      • Contact owner: assign the conversation to the specific record’s owner. If the contact record has an owner assigned, then that owner will become the conversation owner. If there’s no contact owner assigned, then the fallback rule will be used to assign the conversation owner.
        • Set up your fallback options. You can select the option to assign to Specific users and teams or No owner. This will apply if the record does not have an owner, or if the owner does not have a paid service seat.
        • You can also select the option to Assign to available users only. When this option is selected, if there are no available users, the conversation will be set to unassigned.
  • After setting up your action, at the top, click Save.
  • Continue setting up your workflow.

Rotate ticket owners by skill with workflows

After assigning user skills in help desk, you can rotate tickets to users based on their skills using the Rotate record by skill action in workflows. For example, you can include the action as part of a larger workflow to update the ticket’s properties and assign the ticket.

You can also route tickets by skill directly in help desk. Learn more about routing tickets in help desk based on agent skills.

Before you get started

Seats required Users must have a Service Seat to be assigned skills.

When using the Rotate record by skill action, do note the following:

  • The Rotate record by skill action is only available in ticket-based workflows.
  • The action will use the existing help desk skills configuration. Learn how to assign skills to a user.
  • When creating a workflow with the Rotate record by skill action, the action will not replace the skill-based routing rules set within help desk.
    • Both skills-based routing in help desk and workflow ticket assignment rules can occur concurrently.
    • In certain cases, this can result in ticket owners being overwritten. For example, if a ticket was initially assigned within helpdesk, but later enrolls in a workflow with this action and the option to Overwrite any existing ticket owner selected.

Rotate records by skill in ticket-based workflows

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow, or create a new workflow.
  • Click the + add icon to add a workflow action.
  • In the left panel, click to expand CRM. Then, select Rotate record by skill.
  • Configure your Rotate record by skill action:

    • Object to rotate: the ticket record to be assigned by the action. By default, this will be set to the enrolled ticket. You can also select other associated tickets.

    • Assign to a user from these teams: assign incoming tickets to the teams selected.

    • Match skills based on: select which users are eligible for assignment based on skills. You can select from the following options:

      • User has all of the selected skills: the user must have all selected skills to be eligible for assignment. For example, if English and French have been selected in the Assign to a user with these skills option, the user must have both English and French to be eligible.
      • Users has at least one of the selected skills: the user will be eligible for assignment if they have at least one skill. For example, if English and French have been selected in the Assign to a user with these skills option, the user will be included if they have either English or French.

    • Assign to a user with these skills: select the checkboxes next to the skills that you’d like to include. You can select primary and secondary skills.

    • Distribution: select how the tickets will be distributed to eligible users. You can select from the following:

      • Load Balanced: distribute tickets to users with the fewest open tickets assigned.
      • Round Robin: distribute to users in rotating, sequential order.
      • Random: distribute tickets to users randomly.

    • Overwrite any existing ticket owner: select this checkbox to to overwrite existing ticket owners for selected records. If this option is not selected, only tickets without an owner will be assigned.

    • Assign to available users only: select this checkbox to assign tickets to available users only. Tickets will be unassigned if all users are set to away.

Run agents using workflows

Use the Run Agent workflow action to deploy AI-powered agents directly from workflows. Learn more about using agents and assistants. You can configure which agent to run, what information it receives, and the output generated. Then, use the generated outputs to update records, automate follow-ups, and more.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Use the Run Agent action

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow or create a new workflow.
  • Set your enrollment triggers.
  • Click the + plus icon to add an action.
  • In the left panel, click to expand the AI section. Then, click Run agent.
  • Click the Agent to run dropdown menu and select an agent. Only existing agents that have already been added to the account will appear when selecting an agent. Learn how to install agents.
  • Depending on the agent selected, manually enter or add your input data using the data panel. For example, if you’re using the Company Research Agent, you’ll need to add the Domain or Company Name for the company.

.

  • In the Outputs section, click the Agent response format dropdown menu and select from the following:
    • Text response: this will return the full agent’s response in text format.
    • Structured data: this will return the specific defined outputs. For example, if you’re using the data research agent, you may want a specific pieces of information, such as the company’s size or industry, or even an executive summary including recent news about the company.
      • To manually set your outputs, click + Add an output. Then, configure your outputs:
        • Output name: the name of the output returned. This will appear when selecting the action output for use with other workflow action types.
        • What data should be returned: use a prompt to determine what kind of data should be returned. For example, if you’re trying to determine the company’s size, you can use the prompt: the number of employees in the company. Then, select number for the following data format field.
        • Data format: you can select from the following data types: text, number, boolean, date, datetime, enumeration, and phone number.
      • To use AI to generate outputs, click Generate from instructions. Pre-filled structured outputs will be automatically generated by AI, based on the selected agent’s instructions.
  • At the top, click Save.

Use outputs with other workflow actions

After adding the Run agent action to your workflow, you can use the generated output in other workflow actions where the data panel is used.

  • After setting up your action, in the same workflow, click the + plus icon to add an action.
  • Select a workflow action.
  • In the All data tokens panel, in the Action data section, click Run agent.
  • If you’ve chosen to use Text response when setting up your run agent action, select Text response.
  • If you’ve chosen to use Structured data when setting up your run agent action, select a specified output.
  • Continue setting up your workflow action.

Example use cases

The following examples outline the different ways you can use the Run agents action in workflows to automate more complex processes:

  • Simplify research for sales reps: use the action with the Company research agent to review an executive summary of a contact’s company before setting up a first meeting or calling the contact. You can also copy this data to a custom property on the record.
  • Accurately nurture leads: use the Customer health agent to categorize a record, then send them down different workflow branches.

Save placeholder workflow actions

Most workflow actions, such as Create task and Send email, can be saved without setting all of the details. This can help streamline workflow building by allowing you to add your actions first as placeholders, then set up the rest of the details later before turning the workflow on.

For example, you’re setting up a workflow for an upcoming email marketing campaign. Before you’ve finished creating the emails, you can add all the Send email actions you need, then add the emails after they’ve been completed.

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to create and edit workflows.

To save an action as a placeholder:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of your workflow. Placeholder workflow actions can only be added to inactive workflows. You cannot add a placeholder when a workflow is turned on.
  • In the workflow editor, click the + add icon to add an action. Alternatively, select the action. Then, click Save. When adding a placeholder action this way, you can either partially set up the action or leave it entirely blank before saving.
  • The action will then be saved to the workflow timeline and will display the remaining details to fill before you can turn the workflow on. Then, continue setting up your workflow as needed.

Please note: the following workflow actions cannot be set as placeholders, and must be fully set up before continuing to build your workflow:

- Custom code
- Format data
- Delay for a set amount of time
- Delay until a day or time
- Actions from connected apps
  • To finish setting up a placeholder action, click the action, then fill in the missing details in the left panel.
  • You can also view all actions that need to be updated before turning on your workflow. In the top right, click Review. Any incomplete placeholder actions will appear in the right panel.

Select workflow triggers in Agent Hub

The following triggers are available when creating workflows in Agent Hub. Workflow triggers can be changed at any time.

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to use the workflows tool.

Please note: when adding triggers to workflows in Agent Hub, you can only select one event trigger per workflow.

Built-in triggers

  • Run manually: trigger the workflow manually with the run manually trigger type. When using this trigger type, you can run your actions without an enrolled record.
  • Run on a schedule: trigger your workflow on a set frequency. Learn more about using ‘Based on a schedule’ workflow enrollment triggers.

    • You can set a workflow to recur just once, on an annual, monthly, weekly, or daily schedule, or on a custom schedule (e.g., every three days, every two months).

    • When using Run on a schedule triggers in the Agent Hub workflow builder, when setting the Time of day field, the workflow will trigger on the same day, instead of the following day.

Custom events

  • All custom events: trigger the workflow based on custom events. You’ll be able to create and review the custom events in the event management tool. Learn more about creating and managing custom events in HubSpot.
    • To create a new event from the Agent Hub workflow builder, in the top right, click Create new event. You’ll be automatically redirected to the custom events tool.
    • If you’re creating a new webhook event, you can create the event directly in the Agent Hub workflow builder.
    • When using custom event triggers in the Agent Hub workflow builder, custom events created via Events API or webhook do not require an object association to trigger workflows in Agent Hub.
  • Webhook event is received: trigger the workflow whenever a webhook event is received. This allows you to trigger your webhook based on events that occur in external applications. Learn more about using webhook event workflow triggers in Agent Hub.

CRM

When using CRM change event triggers, the object types available for targeting depends on your account subscriptions:

When using CRM change event triggers, all subscriptions listed above can target the following object types:

  • Appointments
  • Carts
  • Calls
  • Contacts
  • Companies
  • Conversations
  • Deals
  • Emails (one-to-one emails only)
  • Goals
  • Invoices
  • Listings
  • Marketing Events (BETA)
  • Media
  • Meetings
  • Payments
  • Projects
  • Services
  • Subscriptions
  • Tasks
  • Users

When using CRM change event triggers, only specific subscriptions can target the following object types:

  • Custom objects (Enterprise only)
  • Campaigns (Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise only)
  • Social posts (Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise only)
  • Leads (Sales Hub Professional or Enterprise)
  • Survey responses (Service Hub Professional or Enterprise)
  • Tickets (Service Hub Professional or Enterprise)
  • Quotes
    • Standard workflows (Revenue Hub Professional)
    • Advanced approval workflows (Revenue Hub Enterprise)
  • Orders (Revenue Hub Professional or Enterprise)
  • Credit memos (Revenue Hub Professional or Enterprise)
  • Contracts (BETA) (Revenue Hub Professional or Enterprise)

Please note: when creating marketing event-based workflows (beta), actions related to contacts (e.g., attendees, registrants) are not supported. For example, you cannot send a thank you email to all attendees when the event ends. To target these records, it is recommended to use contact-based workflows with event activity triggers such as Registered for marketing event instead.

CRM change events
  • Record match criteria: trigger the workflow when a record matches a specific criteria, or changes segment (list) membership.
    • Custom criteria: trigger the workflow when a record meets a specific custom criteria. This is similar to filter enrollment triggers in the workflows tool, can be range from property values in the workflows tool, to count of form submissions or interactions with CTAs, and more.
    • Records added to a segment: triggers when a record is added to a specified segment (list).
    • Record removed from a segment: triggers when a record removed from a specified segment (list).
  • Playbook Log: triggers when a playbook is logged on a record in the CRM.
  • Property value changes: triggers when a property value is updated on a record in the CRM. This trigger represents exactly one property changing from one value to another. Unlike segment-based filters, it does not account for historical operators like Updated in last [X] days.
  • Record created: triggers when a new object is created in the CRM. This event does not have any associated properties. You must use refinement criteria to filter out unwanted objects from enrollment.
  • User Updated Association: triggers when a record is associated with a campaign. Learn more about manually associating CRM records with campaigns.
  • Quote Countersigned Event: triggers when a quote has been countersigned.

Please note:

  • The Segment membership changed trigger criteria has been moved. To trigger workflows based on segment memberships, use the Record match criteria workflow criteria instead.
  • When changing property values, the record may take some time to process in the Agent Hub workflow builder. For example, if you’ve changed a property on a contact record, and change it back immediately, the record may not trigger.

Contact & company signal events

  • Buyer Intent Saved View Change: triggers when a buyer intent saved view is updated. Learn more about buyer intent saved views.
  • Asset acquisition: triggers when a company acquires a new asset.
  • Asset divestiture: triggers when a company divests an existing asset.
  • Budget Mention: triggers when a company’s budget allocation or spend intent is captured from conversations in HubSpot (emails, transcripts, notes, etc.).
  • Client signing: triggers when a company signs a new client contract.
  • Company Spinoff: triggers when a company spins off a new company.
  • Deal timing: triggers when a company’s timing cues are captured from conversations in HubSpot (emails, transcripts, notes, etc.).
  • Division spinoff: triggers when a company spins off a new division.
  • Earnings report: triggers when a company releases an earnings report.
  • Event attendance: triggers when a company attends or may attend an event
  • Executive departure: triggers when a C-level executive leaves a company.
  • Executive hiring: triggers when a company hires a new C-level executive.
  • Executive retirement: triggers when a C-level executive retires in a company.
  • Funding: triggers when a company secures funding.
  • Geographic expansion: triggers when a company expands geographically.
  • Growth metrics: triggers when a company announces revenue growth or customer acquisition.
  • Industry recognition: triggers when a company has gained industry recognition.
  • IPO: triggers when a company has an IPO launch.
  • Key stakeholder identified: triggers when key stakeholders have been identified for a company, such as the company’s decision maker, budget holder, economic buyer, and champion.
  • Layoff: triggers when a company executes layoffs.
  • Leadership content: triggers when a company executive publishes a leadership article.
  • Mergers and acquisitions: triggers when a company has acquired, been acquired by, or merged with another company.
  • Office closure: triggers when a company has office closures.
  • Painpoint: triggers when a company’s painpoints are identified.
  • Physical expansion: triggers when a company has physical location expansion.
  • Product development: triggers when a company develops a new product or service.
  • Product integration: triggers when a company integrates a new product or service.
  • Product launch: triggers when a company launches a new product or service.
  • Regulatory approval: triggers when a company acquires regulatory approval.
  • Research: triggers when a company has completed research.
  • Research topic surge (Bombora): triggers when specific businesses are actively researching a company’s products or services
  • Revenue report: triggers when a company releases a revenue report.
  • Strategic partnership: triggers when a company announces a new strategic partnership or alliance.
  • Technology investment: triggers when a company receives technology investments in the form of public/government funding.
  • Valuation update: triggers when a company has a valuation update.
  • Visitor intent: triggers when a company enters or exits your visitor intent criteria. Learn how to configure your criteria. Learn how to configure your criteria.
  • Email bounce: triggers when an email bounce risk is detected for a contact associated with a tracked company. Event will be on the associated contact record as a contact signal.
  • Job ended: triggers when a contact associated with a tracked company starts a new job. Event will be on the associated contact record as a contact signal.
  • Job started: triggers when a contact associated with a tracked company leaves their job. Event will be on the associated contact record as a contact signal.

Call, document & meeting events

  • Call ended: triggers when a call has ended. This includes both calls initiated through HubSpot or through third-party integrations, such as Aircall. This will not trigger if the call is manually logged.
  • Call started: triggers when a call is initiated. This includes both calls initiated through HubSpot or through third-party integrations, such as Aircall. This will not trigger if the call is manually logged.
  • Feedback mention: [TBD]
  • Meeting booked: triggers when a contact books a meeting through the HubSpot meetings tool, or for logged and scheduled meetings from the CRM record page.
  • Meeting outcome change: triggers when a meeting outcome is changed in the account.
  • Contact finished viewing a document: triggers when a contact has finished viewing a sales document. This occurs when the user completes the view by clicking out of the document.
  • Contact viewed a document: triggers when a contact views a sales document. This represents the initial view of a document, regardless of whether the contact finished viewing it.
  • Document shared with contact: triggers when a sales document is shared with a contact.

Email events

  • Clicked link in marketing email: triggers when a contact clicks a link in a marketing email.
    • When further defining your email event enrollment triggers, both Raw URL and Original URL criteria will include any query parameters added by the user and tracking parameters added by HubSpot.
    • When using this filter criteria, it is recommended to use contains any of instead of is equal to any of.
  • Marketing or sales email bounced: triggers when a one-to-one or marketing email is sent to a contact and bounces.
  • Marketing or sales email delivered: triggers when a one-to-one or marketing email is delivered to a contact.
  • Marketing or sales email sent: triggers when a marketing email, or one-to-one email, is sent to a contact. This event will only trigger for one-to-one emails if sent through a hosted inbox.
  • Opened marketing email: triggers when a contact opens a marketing email.
  • Replied to marketing email: triggers when a contact replies to a marketing email.
  • Sales email send: triggers when a sales email is sent to a contact. This event will only trigger for one-to-one emails if sent through a hosted inbox.
  • Updated marketing email subscription status: triggers when a contact updates their email subscription status.

Whatsapp events

Subscription required A Marketing Hub or Service Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use Whatsapp events as workflow triggers in Agent Hub.

  • Clicked link in WhatsApp message: triggers when a contact clicks a link in a Whatsapp message.
  • Dropped WhatsApp message: triggers when a SMS message is dropped for a contact.
  • Opted out of WhatsApp subscription: triggers when a contact opts out of a Whatsapp subscription.
  • Replied to a WhatsApp message: triggers when a contact replies to a SMS message.
  • Sending WhatsApp message failed: triggers when an Whatsapp message wasn’t delivered to a contact.
  • Sent WhatsApp message: triggers when an SMS message is sent to a contact.
  • WhatsApp message delivered: triggers when an SMS message is delivered to a contact.
  • WhatsApp message read: triggers when an SMS message is marked as read by a contact.

Website & media events

  • Ad interaction: triggers when an ad is interacted with.

  • Campaign Influence: triggers when a contact is influenced by a HubSpot campaign.

  • Form interaction: triggers when a contact clicks on a text field in the form. This event will trigger before a form submission, since the user needs to interact with the form in order to submit it. However, a user may interact with a form without submitting it.

  • Form submission: triggers when a form is submitted. When configuring your triggers by URL, take note of the below elements:

    • Example URL: hubspot.com
    • Base URL: the URL without the protocol or query parameters. (e.g. www.hubspot.com/search)
    • URL domain: the domain only. (e.g. hubspot.com)
    • URL path: the section after the domain (e.g. /search)

  • Form view: triggers when a contact views a form. The user that viewed the form must already be a contact in the CRM. Visitors who have not yet converted into contacts will not trigger an enrollment.

  • Attention Span: [TBD]

  • Media Play: triggers when a contact plays a media file embedded in your content (e.g., on a website page, email, etc.)

  • CTA (Legacy) click: triggers when a contact clicks a CTA (legacy).

  • CTA (Legacy) view: triggers when a contact views a CTA (legacy).

  • CTA click: triggers when a contact clicks a CTA or Web interactive.

  • CTA view: triggers when a contact views a CTA or Web interactive.

  • Page visited: triggers when a contact views a landing page or website page. If a user views a page and has not yet converted from a visitor to a contact, this will not trigger the workflow. When configuring your triggers by URL, take note of the below elements:

    • Example URL: hubspot.com
    • Base URL: the URL without the protocol or query parameters. (e.g. www.hubspot.com/search)
    • URL domain: the domain only. (e.g. hubspot.com)
    • URL path: the section after the domain (e.g. /search)

Automation events

Subscription required A Sales Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use sequence-based event triggers.

  • Contact booked meeting through a sequence: triggers when a contact books a meeting through a sequence.
  • Contact enrolled in a sequence: triggers when a contact is enrolled in a sequence.
  • Contact unenrolled from sequence: triggers when a contact is unenrolled from a sequence.
  • Contact unenrolled from a sequence via workflow: triggers when a contact is unenrolled from a sequence via a workflow. Other unenrollment sources do not trigger this event.
  • Contact unenrolled manually from sequence: triggers when a contact is unenrolled from a sequence.
  • Sequence finished: triggers when a contact finishes a sequence.
  • Workflow run ended: triggers when an object is unenrolled from a workflow.
  • Workflow run started: triggers when an object is enrolled in a workflow.

Quote events

  • Anonymous Public Quote Download: triggers when an anonymous user downloads a public quote.
  • Anonymous Quote Print: triggers when an anonymous user prints out a public quote.
  • Anonymous Quote View: triggers when the quote gets a view that cannot be tied back to a CRM record.
  • Closing Agent Conversation Started: triggers when a buyer starts a conversation with closing agent.
  • Public Quote Download: Trigger when a user downloads a public quote.
  • Quote accepted: triggers when a quote enters an accepted state.
  • Quote approval recalled: triggers when a quote approval is recalled.
  • Quote approval requested: triggers when a quote approval is requested.
  • Quote approved: triggers when a quote approval is approved.
  • Quote buyer signed: triggers when a buyer signs a quote.
  • Quote Email Sent: triggers when a quote email is sent.
  • Quote Expiration Reminder Email Sent: triggers when the quote expiration reminder emails are sent.
  • Quote Expired Event: triggers when a quote enters an expired state.
  • Quote Followup Reminder Email Sent: triggers when the quote followup reminder emails are sent.
  • Quote manually signed: triggers when a quote is manually signed.
  • Quote published: triggers when a quote enters a published state.
  • Quote recalled: triggers when a quote enters a recalled state.
  • Quote rejected: triggers when a quote approval is rejected.

Apps

  • Slack: when triggering workflows with Slack events. Add additional filters to narrow down the exact event. For example, you can filter only messages that include the phrase ready to sign. Learn more about using Slack event triggers in Agent Hub workflows.
    • Slack user mentioned: triggers when a specific Slack user has been mentioned. You can filter by message text, channel ID, or sender user ID.
    • Slack message sent by user: triggers when a message is sent by a specific Slack user. This can be further filtered by message content.
    • Slack member joined channel: triggers when a new user joins a channel. You can filter by channel, user, or the user that invited the new user.
    • Slack thread reply: triggers when a thread is replied to in a specific channel. You can filter by message text or sender user ID.
    • Slack message posted: triggers when a slack message is posted to a specific channel. You can filter by message text or sender user ID.
  • Google Drive: when triggering workflows based on activity in files and folders in Google Drive.
    • File events
      • Google Drive file created: triggers when a file is created.
      • Google Drive file moved: triggers when a file is moved to a different folder.
      • Google Drive file content changed: triggers when the content of a file is changed.
      • Google Drive file deleted: triggers when a file is permanently deleted.
      • Google Drive file trashed: triggers when a file is moved to the trash.
      • Google Drive file restored from trash: triggers when a file is restored from the trash.
      • Google Drive file renamed: triggers when a file is renamed.
    • Comment events
      • Google Drive comment created: triggers when a comment is added to a file.
      • Google Drive comment edited: triggers when a comment is edited.
      • Google Drive comment resolved: triggers when a comment is marked as resolved.
      • Google Drive comment reopened: triggers when a resolved comment is reopened.
    • Reply events
      • Google Drive reply created: triggers when a reply is added to a comment.
      • Google Drive reply edited: triggers when a reply is edited.
      • Google Drive reply deleted: triggers when a reply is deleted.
    • Permission events
      • Google Drive permission created: triggers when a user or group is given access to a file.
      • Google Drive permission edited: triggers when a user’s or group’s access level for a file is changed.
      • Google Drive permission removed: triggers when a user’s or group’s access to a file is removed.
      • Google Drive access proposal created: triggers when a user proposes a change to access for a file.
      • Google Drive access proposal resolved: triggers when a proposed access change is accepted or denied.
    • Approval events
      • Google Drive approval created: triggers when an approval request is created for a file.
      • Google Drive approval cancelled: triggers when an approval request is cancelled.
      • Google Drive approval reset: triggers when an approval request is reset.
      • Google Drive approval completed: triggers when an approval request is completed.
      • Google Drive approval reviewers changed: triggers when the reviewers on an approval request are changed.
      • Google Drive approval responded: triggers when a reviewer responds to an approval request.
  • Google Sheets
    • Google Sheet row added or updated: triggers when a Google Sheet row is added or updated to a specific Google Sheet.
  • Microsoft 365 Excel
    • Excel spreadsheet row added or updated: triggers when a Excel spreadsheet row is added or updated to a specific Sheet.

Please note: the following will apply to both Google Sheet and Microsoft 365 Excel workflow triggers:

  • Connected sheets are checked every minute for changes. When a change is made to a sheet, it’ll take a minute for the workflow to trigger from the update.
  • If a column title is changed, every row of the spreadsheet will be re-enrolled. It is not possible to differentiate between a column name change and a column being deleted or re-added.
  • All columns in a Google or Excel sheet can be used as trigger filters. However, only values from the first 20 columns can be used as tokens for actions in the workflow.
  • If the same exact row of values has previously existed in the sheet, it will not trigger the workflow. This is a deduplication measure to ensure the same row doesn’t trigger the workflow more than once.
    • For example, if a row’s values are John | Doe | X, updating the row to John | Doe | Y will trigger the workflow. However, updating the row back to John | Doe | X after, will not trigger the workflow.

Set ‘Based on a schedule’ workflow enrollment triggers

Use Based on a schedule workflow enrollment triggers to center your workflow actions on a set frequency. You can set a workflow to recur just once, or on an annual, monthly, weekly, or daily schedule.

For example, you can create a workflow to send a celebratory email once a year, based on a contact’s birthday date property.

Understand limitations and requirements

Permissions required To set up workflow triggers, users must have Edit permissions for workflows. To publish workflows, users must have Publish permissions for workflows.

  • When setting up a Based on a schedule workflow enrollment trigger, the configured dates and times will be based on your account’s time zone settings.
  • This enrollment trigger type can be used across all workflow object types and with additional enrollment filter criteria.

Set up your Based on a schedule enrollment trigger

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of the workflow. Or, create a new workflow.
  • If you’re creating a workflow from scratch, in the left panel, select On a schedule.
  • If you’re working on an existing workflow:
    • In the workflow editor, click the Trigger enrollment for [object] card.
    • If there are existing workflow triggers, in the left panel, click Change start trigger. This will erase any current enrollment triggers.
    • In the dialog box, click Confirm.
    • In the left panel, select Based on a schedule.
  • If you’re creating a workflow from scratch, click the Enroll dropdown menu to select an object type for your workflow. If you’re updating an existing workflow, it is not possible to change the workflow’s object type.
  • Continue setting up your enrollment criteria based on the frequency that you’d like to use.
Set your workflow to recur only once
  • Set up your Based on a schedule workflow enrollment trigger.
  • In the left panel, click the Frequency dropdown menu and select Once.
  • Continue setting up your trigger:
    • Date: select a date or date property for your workflow to execute.
      • To select a fixed date, click the date picker and select a date.
      • To select a date property, click the date picker and select a property from the data panel. Then, select On date, Before date, or After date.
    • Time of day: choose when your workflow should trigger.
      • If you select Morning, Daytime, or Night, the workflow will begin checking for records the next day, after the workflow is turned on. During the selected window, the workflow will run at a time when HubSpot’s systems offer optimal performance.
      • If you select Specific time, the workflow will begin checking for records at the specified time on the scheduled date.
Set your workflow to recur annually

Use this frequency to enroll records at on a specific date every year, or based on a date property, such as a deal’s close date or a contact’s birthday. For a yearly birthday email or reminder, set the frequency to Annually. Then, you can add criteria such as Birthday is known to enroll only records with a value.

  • Set up your Based on a schedule workflow enrollment trigger.
  • In the left panel, click the Frequency dropdown menu and select Annually.
  • Continue setting up your trigger:
    • Date: select a date or date property for your workflow to execute.
      • To select a fixed date, click the date picker and select a date. Only the day and month options will appear.
      • To select a date property, click the date picker and select a property from the data panel. Then, select On date, Before date, or After date. Only the day and month of the date property will be taken into account.
    • Time of day: choose when your workflow should trigger.
      • If you select Morning, Daytime, or Night, the workflow will begin checking for records the next day, after the workflow is turned on. During the selected window, the workflow will run at a time when HubSpot’s systems offer optimal performance.
      • If you select Specific time, the workflow will begin checking for records at the specified time on the scheduled date.

Please note: if you turn on or update an annual workflow on its scheduled day and select Morning, Daytime, or Night, records won’t enroll until the next scheduled annual occurrence. To enroll records on the scheduled day, selected Specific time instead. For example, a workflow was set to recur annually on 4th July.

  • If the workflow was updated prior to 3rd July 2026, to trigger in the Night, the workflow will trigger and enroll on 4th July 2026.
  • If the workflow was updated on 4th July 2026, the next enrollment will be 4th July 2027.
Set your workflow to recur monthly
  • Set up your Based on a schedule workflow enrollment trigger.
  • In the left panel, click the Frequency dropdown menu and select Monthly.
  • Continue setting up your trigger:
    • Day of the month:
      • Specific days: select specific days of the month for the workflow to recur. For example, you can send a billing reminder every 15th of the month.
      • Flexible days: when selecting this option, you can select First Monday of the month or Last day of the month. The specific day of the month may vary when selecting this option.
    • Time of day: choose when your workflow should trigger.
      • If you select Morning, Daytime, or Night, the workflow will begin checking for records the next day, after the workflow is turned on. During the selected window, the workflow will run at a time when HubSpot’s systems offer optimal performance.
      • If you select Specific time, the workflow will begin checking for records at the specified time on the scheduled date.
Set your workflow to recur weekly
  • Set up your Based on a schedule workflow enrollment trigger.
  • In the left panel, click the Frequency dropdown menu and select Weekly.
  • Continue setting up your trigger:
    • Day of the week: select a day of the week for the workflow to recur on. For example, you may want to send a reminder for users to review for all open deals in a specific deal stage every Tuesday.
    • Time of day: choose when your workflow should trigger.
      • If you select Morning, Daytime, or Night, the workflow will begin checking for records the next day, after the workflow is turned on. During the selected window, the workflow will run at a time when HubSpot’s systems offer optimal performance.
      • If you select Specific time, the workflow will begin checking for records at the specified time on the scheduled date.
Set your workflow to recur daily
  • Set up your Based on a schedule workflow enrollment trigger.
  • In the left panel, click the Frequency dropdown menu and select Daily.
  • Continue setting up your trigger:
    • Time of day: choose when your workflow should trigger. - If you select Morning, Daytime, or Night, the workflow will begin checking for records the next day, after the workflow is turned on. During the selected window, the workflow will run at a time when HubSpot’s systems offer optimal performance. - If you select Specific time, the workflow will begin checking for records at the specified time on the scheduled date.

Finish setting up your enrollment trigger

After adding your enrollment trigger and setting up your enrollment frequency:

  • In the Only enroll records that meet the conditions section, click + Add conditions. Then, set filter criteria to define the records that you’d like to enroll in the workflow. On each scheduled date and time, all records that meet this criteria will enroll and go through the workflow.
    • If there is no filter criteria set, records will not automatically enroll in the workflow. Only manually enrolled records will be enrolled.
    • If a record is manually enrolled, it will not follow the set schedule. Manually enrolled records will execute the workflow immediately.
  • If you’re setting up the workflow for the first time, at the top, click Next. Then, finish setting up your enrollment criteria.
  • If you’re updating an existing workflow, click Save.
  • Continue setting up your workflow.

Set ‘When a webhook is received’ workflow triggers

Set enrollment triggers to automatically enroll records in a workflow when a webhook is received from an external third-party application. Learn more about setting up your workflow enrollment.

Understand limitations and requirements

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to create and edit workflows.

  • The workflow will only trigger if there is an existing record with a corresponding unique property value in your HubSpot account.

  • Webhook triggers only support incoming data sent with the application/json content-type.

Set a When a webhook is received workflow trigger

To trigger a workflow from a webhook:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.

  • Click the name of an existing workflow or create a new workflow.

  • If you’re creating a workflow from scratch:

    • In the left panel, click to expand the Custom events & external events section.
    • Click Received a webhook from an external app.

  • If you’re working on an existing workflow:

    • In the workflow editor, click the Trigger enrollment for [object] card.

    • If there are existing workflow triggers, in the left panel, click Change start trigger. This will erase any current enrollment triggers.

    • In the dialog box, click Confirm.

    • In the left panel, under Advanced options, click When a webhook is received.

  • To add a new webhook, click + Add a webhook. You can create up to 100 unique webhook events.

  • Add a Webhook event name. Then, click Next.

  • Copy the Webhook URL and paste it into the webhook settings page of the app you want to integrate with. From your app, use the webhook URL to send a test event.

  • In the Review your test event section, review the webhook event and make updates as necessary. Then, click Next.

  • Map the data for your webhooks properties:

    • Edit the HubSpot property label as necessary.
    • Click the Data type dropdown menu to select a data type for each property label.
      • You can use string, enum, number, and boolean values.
      • Datetime properties are not supported and should be mapped as string values instead. After, you can use a custom code action with strtotime to convert to a date time object, and then use unixtimestamp to get a timestamp.
    • To remove a property label, click the Delete icon.

  • Click Next.

  • Match your enrollment property by selecting a property from your third-party webhook that’s an exact match for one of your HubSpot custom properties. Then, click Next.

    • The workflow can only be triggered if the selected third-party webhook property has a non-empty value in the incoming webhook data.
    • The custom property must have Require unique values for property checkbox selected. Or, create a new property with a unique value required.

  • Click Continue to trigger setup.

  • To use the webhook as an enrollment trigger, click the name of the webhook in the left panel. Then, click Save.

Set a schedule to automatically trigger Agent Hub workflows

Use the Run records on a schedule or Run on a schedule workflow triggers to center your workflow actions on a set frequency. You can set a workflow to recur just once, or on an annual, monthly, weekly, or daily schedule.

For example, you can create a workflow to send a renewal notification to a sales rep once a year, based on a contact’s associated deal Close won date property.

Understand limitations and requirements

Permissions required To set up workflow triggers, users must have Edit permissions for workflows. To publish workflows, users must have Publish permissions for workflows.

  • When setting up a Run records on a schedule or Run on a schedule workflow enrollment triggers, the configured dates and times will be based on your account’s time zone settings.
  • When triggering your workflows based on a set schedule, you can select from the following options.
    • Run on a schedule: automatically run the workflow on a set schedule. For example, use this trigger to run a custom agent once a week.
    • Run records on a schedule: automatically enroll records in the Agent Hub workflow based on a set schedule. If no records meet the criteria, the workflow will not run.

Set event enrollment triggers

Set workflow enrollment triggers to automatically enroll records when an event is completed. Event triggers can be used if you want to trigger actions in a workflow only when an event occurs.

For example, you can use this to send an email when a form has been filled out or when a CTA has been clicked. Learn more about the differences between event triggers and filter-based criteria.

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to create and edit workflows.

How event enrollment triggers work

Event enrollment triggers only enroll records for events that occur after the workflow is turned on.

  • To include existing records, it is recommended to use a filter-based enrollment triggers and choose to enroll records that already meet the criteria, or manually enroll the records instead.
  • For event-based triggers such as Object created, all additional enrollment filters are evaluated only at the exact time the event occurs. Property updates or actions that happen after will not be re-evaluated for that original event.
  • For an event enrollment to trigger, the record must be created before the event occurs. For example, a website visitor completes a custom event that has been set as an event enrollment trigger, but only becomes a HubSpot contact a minute later. In this instance, as the contact was created after the custom event occurred, they will not be enrolled.
  • For event-based triggers such as Property value changed, enrollment is evaluated after the property value is updated, which can take a few minutes to process.

Understand limitations and requirements

When using event enrollment triggers, please note the following:

  • You cannot test record enrollment using event enrollment triggers. When testing enrollment, only filters in the AND only enroll contacts that also meet these filters used section will be taken into account.
  • You cannot use scheduled triggers with event enrollment triggers.
  • The following will apply for specific event types:
    • Call event triggers: call event triggers can be used with both calls initiated from HubSpot and calls from third-party calling apps using the calling extensions SDK.
    • Email: if a specific email is not defined, actions taken on all one-to-one or marketing emails, including batch marketing emails, can cause a record to meet the event enrollment trigger. When defining specific marketing emails, only A/B marketing and automated marketing emails can be used for event enrollment.
    • Segment membership: if you use segment membership as enrollment criteria in a workflow, automatic enrollment only triggers when a record joins a segment by meeting the segment’s existing criteria. If you later update the segment’s filters, any records added to the segment as a result of that change will not automatically enroll in the workflow. To enroll these records, learn how to manually enroll records from a segment.

Set event enrollment triggers

When setting up event enrollment triggers, all triggers will be separated using the OR operator. This means that only one of the event enrollment triggers must occur for the record to enroll in the workflow.

To set up your event enrollment triggers:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.

  • Click the name of the workflow or create a new workflow.

  • If you’re creating a workflow from scratch, in the left panel, select an event trigger.

    • Generally, event enrollment triggers will generally be labeled [type] events.
    • You can refer to the list of available event enrollment triggers.

  • If you’re working on an existing workflow:

    • In the workflow editor, click the Trigger enrollment for [object] card.
    • If there are existing workflow triggers, in the left panel, click Change start trigger. This will erase any current enrollment triggers.
    • In the dialog box, click Confirm.
    • In the left panel, select When an event occurs.

  • In the panel, select an event trigger.

  • Within the same trigger group, click + Add criteria to further define your trigger. For example, you can further specify Ad interaction event triggers by Ad Network or Interaction Type.

  • To add another trigger group, click + Add criteria and continue setting up your trigger group.

  • After setting your event triggers, above the trigger groups, click Done.

  • To further refine the records enrolled in the workflow based on additional filters, in the AND only enroll contacts that also meet these filters section, click + Add filter.

    • You can select additional properties to refine the records that you would like to enroll in the workflow.

    • Your event triggers must be saved before you can add additional refinement filters.

    • When using refining filter criteria, the record must also meet these filters when the event from the main trigger occurs.

  • By default, records will only enroll in a workflow the first time they meet the enrollment triggers. To turn on re-enrollment, under the Should [object] be re-enrolled in this workflow? section, select Yes, re-enroll every time the trigger occurs.

  • When you’re done, click Save. If you’re updating a published workflow, in the dialog box, select from the following options:

    • Save and enroll existing [object]: select this option to enroll all existing records that meet the updated trigger criteria, If re-enrollment is turned on, any records that may have previously enrolled in this workflow will be enrolled again.
    • Save and don’t enroll existing [object]: select this option to only enroll records that meet the trigger criteria moving forward.

Event enrollment triggers

It is not possible to enroll records that did not complete an event. For example, you cannot enroll contacts who did not submit a form. However, you can use if/then branches in the workflow to determine if an event has occurred or not. Learn more about event workflow enrollment triggers in the table below:
