Common workflow errors

The following are common workflow errors you might encounter. From your action logs in the workflow details page, you can review error logs and information logs. Error logs require steps to resolve, while typically, information logs will be retried automatically.

Error logs

After updating your workflow or record, you can try manually enrolling the contact into the workflow again.

Error

What the error means

Steps to resolve the error

When using outputs from AI actions with other actions, the output is populating with empty value

It is likely that the account has run out of credits and the action has failed.

For example, if you’re using outputs from the Data Agent: Custom prompt action with the Edit record action to update a contact property value, but the updated property is appearing as a blank value.

This will apply to AI actions, such as Data Agent: Fill Smart Property, Infer company value proposition and ICP, Data Agent: Custom prompt, and more.

To prevent your records from being affected or incorrectly updated with null values, you can create a One property or action output branch based on the success of the action. Then, add your action only after the Success branch. This will ensure that records are only updated if the action has succeeded.

The prope set because the record isn’t associated with any target records

The Edit records action is trying to execute, but there’s no associated record to update.

For example, if you’re using a contact-based workflow with the Edit records action to copy the industry property to a contact’s associated company, but the contact doesn’t have an associated company.

For individual records, you can manually associate the enrolled record to a target record before enrolling again.

To avoid this error moving forward, you can add an and criteria to your enrollment trigger to require an associated record, ensuring that only records with associated target records enroll. For example, in a contact-based workflow, you can use the criteria Record ID is known.

.

The lifecycle stage couldn’t be updated because it would have been set backwards

The Edit records action can only set a record’s default Lifecycle stage property to a value further down the funnel.

This error occurs if the workflow is trying to set a record’s Lifecycle stage property backward, such as from lead to subscriber.

Learn more about using lifecycle stages.

To set a record’s lifecycle stage to a specific value regardless of their current lifecycle stage, use the same action to clear the property value first.

Unable to create record because an existing record shares a value that must be unique

When creating a new record, HubSpot automatically deduplicates contacts and companies using email addresses and company domain names respectively.

If a record using the email or company domain name already exists, HubSpot will not create a duplicate record and the action will fail.

This also applies if you’ve also turned on the option to Require unique values for this property.

Existing records will not be overwritten or updated. any subsequent actions that rely on the newly created contact may also fail.

Update your workflow logic to avoid attempting to recreate existing records.

For example, you can use an if/then branch to check for an existing contact or use the create associations action to associate existing records.

Email was not sent to contact because this is a non-marketing contact

The Send email action in a workflow can only execute with marketing contacts. Learn more about marketing contacts.

If an email action is skipped because the contact is a non-marketing contact, the workflow will still continue to execute other actions. Any previously skipped emails will not be resent automatically even if the contact is later set as a marketing contact.

To enroll and email only existing marketing contacts in this workflow, you can add an and criteria to the enrollment trigger to enroll contacts with a Marketing contact status property of Marketing contact only.

To send this email to all contacts enrolled in the workflow, you can add a Set marketing contact status action and delay before the Send email action. Do take note that this action increases your marketing contacts count which can affect billing.

No eligible associated recipients for the email action

When sending an automated email, you can select the option to send the email to contacts with specific association labels only.

This error can occur when the associated contact does not have the required association label or has not yet been associated with the record when the email action was executed.

Confirm if a specific association label is required for the Send email action. To send an email to all associated contacts regardless of association label, select the option for All associated contacts.

This email couldn’t be sent because the contact doesn’t have an email address

Automated marketing emails can only be sent to records with associated email addresses.

For contact-based workflows, confirm that the enrolled record has a populated email address.

For other workflow types, check that the enrolled record has an associated contact record with a populated email address.

The email action appears as sent or completed but the contact did not receive it

In this instance, no error message is expected.

  • If you have multiple branches sending automated emails, it is recommended to verify which branch the record followed.
  • Reach out to the recipient to check their spam or junk folder and any mailbox filters for the message.

Previously unsubscribed from this subscription type

This error can occur for two reasons:

  • The contact previously manually unsubscribed from your emails.
  • This account has data privacy settings turned on and the contact is not opted into the email’s required subscription or is or missing a required legal basis for communication.

In this case, the solution depends on the cause of the error:

  • If the contact has manually unsubscribed from your emails, the contact will need to manually resubscribe themselves.
  • If a specific contact was not opted in, you can add the subscription to the individual contact. You can also update contact subscriptions in bulk using the Manage subscription status action.

Email to this recipient has previously bounced

Previous emails to this contact’s email address have hard bounced.

Learn more about email bounce types.

Confirm that the contact’s email address is valid. If so, you can manually remove the hard bounce from the record and try sending the email again.

It is not possible to resend an automated email, but you can:

  • Clone the automated email to a regular email.
  • In the cloned regular email, use the Send to more action to send this email to previously bounced contacts.

This email wasn’t sent because it is being reviewed by HubSpot

HubSpot’s automatic security tools have flagged this email for review.

The email will be reviewed by HubSpot’s content moderation team.

  • If the email is determined to violate HubSpot’s Acceptable Use Policy, the email will be stopped.
  • If the email is not in violation of HubSpot’s Acceptable Use Policy, and was not automatically sent:
    • Clone the automated email to a regular email.
    • Create a contact list with the same criteria as your workflow’s enrollment criteria, adding an addition criteria for: AND has not been sent [name of original email]
    • Send your cloned email to the list.

This email wasn’t sent because it is being blocked by HubSpot

Upon review, this email has been determined to violate the policies outlined in HubSpot’s Acceptable Use Policy, or the email was blocked by HubSpot’s automated systems.

The email will be reviewed by HubSpot’s content moderation team.

  • If the email is determined to violate HubSpot’s Acceptable Use Policy, the email will be stopped.
  • If the email is not in violation of HubSpot’s Acceptable Use Policy, and was not automatically sent:
    • Clone the automated email to a regular email.
    • Create a contact list with the same criteria as your workflow’s enrollment criteria, adding an addition criteria for: “AND has not been sent [name of original email]”
    • Send your cloned email to the list.

Recipient was suppressed due to low engagement

Graymail suppression has been enabled in either:

  • the specific automated email
  • the account’s marketing email settings

Learn more about graymail and unengaged contacts in HubSpot.

To send the email to unengaged contacts, ensure that graymail suppression has been turned off.

  • Check that the Don’t send to unengaged contacts checkbox is cleared in the Send tab of the workflow’s automated email.
  • Check that the Don’t send to unengaged contacts switch is toggled off in the Resubscription and Sending options section, in your account’s marketing email subscription settings.

Outside time window settings. Action rescheduled for [new date and time]

The What times do you want the actions to execute workflow setting has been set to a specific timeframe, but the enrolled record has reached an action while outside of this timeframe.

To allow your workflow actions to execute at any time, in the workflow editor:

  • At the top, click Settings.
  • Confirm that the Run actions at specific times toggle is turned off.

Alternatively, if you only want actions to execute in a specific timeframe, you can ignore the error and the action will execute in the next eligible date and time.

Unable to send email notification

An internal notification email was unable to be sent to the specified user.

To receive internal email notifications:

  • Ensure that the user’s settings are toggled on for email notifications. This must be done directly from the user’s account. You cannot turn on notification settings for another user.
  • Ensure that the Custom notification from workflow tool notification is turned on.
  • Troubleshoot why a user may not be receiving notifications.

This object does not have a WhatsApp phone number

The Phone number property was blank or invalid when the contact passed through the action, even if another custom phone-number property had a value.

Confirm that the contacts have Phone number property with a valid number, including the country code prefix.

This action’s feature is paused. Either you’re out of credits or your admin paused usage. Ask your admin to resume access or add credits

This error appears for AI actions that require credits, and typically occurs due to the following:

  • The HubSpot account has no remaining credits.
  • An admin has paused credit usage, such as by setting a credit limit on the account or specific tool.

The workflow will retry the action once every 24 hours, up to 60 days, before stopping retries.

If the issue is due to limited credits:

  • Add additional credits to your account to resolve the issue immediately.
  • Wait for the next billing cycle to reset your credits.

If the issue is due to credit limits on the account or tool:

  • You may want to request your admin to increase the credit limit on the account or workflows tool.
Information logs

The following are some common workflow information logs you might encounter in the action log of a workflow. They will retry automatically at a later time.

Information

What the information means

Rotate failed because other updates were attempted at the same time. The action will retry soon.

HubSpot will only allow one object to be rotated at a time in order to ensure fairness in distribution. If multiple objects are executing the rotate object action at the same time, only one will be allowed through while the others retry. This is because multiple objects within the same workflow were getting rotated at the same time.

Custom code wasn’t able to execute, but will retry soon.

The action created was unable to execute. For further details, contact the support team.

Action failed because HubSpot is being rate limited by the connected app, but will retry soon.

A limit was reached while transferring data between HubSpot and the connected app. The action will try again.

Webhook wasn’t able to execute, but will retry soon.

HubSpot allows webhooks a certain time frame to execute and send a response back. If the server is too slow to respond, HubSpot will log it as failed and will retry the action.

If the responding server is slow, the actions associated with the webhook may execute, but because there was no reply in the time frame, HubSpot logged it as failed and will retry at a later point.

Webhook failed because of a server error, but will retry soon

HubSpot received a failed response from the external Webhook server.

This action wasn’t able to execute, but will retry soon.

The action created was unable to execute. For further details, contact the support team.

Action failed because the connected app took too long to respond, but will retry soon.

There was a timeout in the requested action from the connected app. The action will try again.

This action was temporarily delayed due to high account activity, but will retry soon.

The workflow has encountered a rate limiting error.

This typically occurs if workflows in the account are engaged in actions involving reading or editing CRM objects such as contact records, etc. This error may surface due to activity from other workflows in the account.

The action will automatically retry and should succeed when there is less workflow activity that involve reading or editing CRM objects in the account.

Troubleshoot workflow enrollment issues

Review possible reasons why records are unexpectedly enrolling or not enrolling in workflows.

  • If you’re looking to resolve errors with your workflow’s execution, learn how to troubleshoot common workflow errors instead.
  • If you’re looking to test records against your workflow’s enrollment criteria, learn how to test your workflow. However, when troubleshooting your workflow, do note that the workflow in the editor might be different from the version that the record may have been enrolled into. For example, actions, triggers, or settings for the workflow may have been changed.

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to use the workflows tool.

Why didn’t my record enroll in a workflow?

Diagnose why an object isn’t enrolling in a workflow and review some common reasons why an object may not enroll in a workflow and the typical steps for resolution.

Troubleshoot workflow enrollment from the workflow editor
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of your workflow.
  • In the upper left, click Help > Troubleshoot enrollment.
  • In the right panel, click the dropdown menu and select the record that was expected to have enrolled.
  • Click the Date range and Time range dropdown menus to set the timeframe the enrollment was expected to occur.

If no enrollment data is available, it is strongly recommended to test the record against the workflow’s enrollment triggers.

Please note: only property, list, and form submission filters are supported in this tool.

Common reasons why a record may not enroll

Reason

Steps to resolve

The record doesn’t meet the workflow’s enrollment triggers

Check that the record meets the workflow’s enrollment triggers.

  • Check any AND and/or OR logic in the triggers.
  • It’s strongly recommended to test the record against the workflow’s enrollment triggers in the workflow editor.

The record was added to the list before the workflow was turned on, but existing records were not set to be enrolled

When using a list for your enrollment criteria, records will only enroll when a record joins the list.

If your record is on the list but has not been enrolled, check if existing records that meet enrollment triggers were set to be enrolled when the workflow was turned on. If this is the case, you can manually select and enroll the list in the workflow editor.

The record met the workflow’s enrollment triggers when the workflow was turned on or the enrollment triggers were updated, but existing records were not set to be enrolled

When turning on the workflow or updating your enrollment triggers, the option No, only enroll companies which meet the trigger criteria after turning the workflow on was selected. As a result, only records that meet the enrollment triggers moving forward are added to the workflow. Review the workflow’s version history to check whether existing records were excluded when the workflow was turned on.

  • To enroll specific records into an existing workflow, you can manually select and enroll records in the workflow editor.
  • To avoid this issue moving forward, learn how to enroll existing records that meet enrollment triggers in a workflow.

The record instantly qualifies for workflow unenrollment

Depending on the record’s object type, records can be automatically unenrolled at the point of enrollment, in the following instances:

  • If a contact meets the workflow’s goals or is on the workflow’s suppression list.
  • If the record meets the workflow’s unenrollment triggers.

If the record does not meet the above criteria, but has been suddenly unenrolled, it’s possible that the contact has enrolled into another workflow where the connection settings to Unenroll from all other workflows or Unenroll from specific workflows has been turned on.

Record was previously enrolled in the workflow, and re-enrollment is not turned on

By default, records are only enrolled in workflows the first time they meet the workflow enrollment triggers or are enrolled manually.

Older enrollments may no longer appear in workflow history, historical data of enrollments is stored for up to 6 months. To check for previous enrollments, review a record’s activity timeline.

If a record was previously enrolled in a workflow and re-enrollment is not turned on, it won’t be enrolled in the workflow if it meets the workflow’s original enrollment triggers again.

To allow for re-enrollment, add re-enrollment triggers to the workflow. When troubleshooting form-based re-enrollment, ensure the specific form is selected in the workflow’s re-enrollment settings, and take note of time-sensitive criteria such as less than 1 day ago.

The record was a merged record

By default, workflows will not enroll merged contacts even if the contact meets the workflow enrollment criteria, unless the option to Automatically enroll merged records if the updated merged record meets the enrollment condition is turned on in the workflow’s settings.

However, merged contacts can later enroll if they meet the enrollment triggers again and re-enrollment is turned on.

The merged record is still active in a workflow

After a merge, the primary record remains enrolled in its active workflows. However, the secondary record is unenrolled from all workflows.

If the primary record was already in the workflow, the record may still be active in the workflow, and cannot re–enroll until it completes the workflow and meets re-enrollment criteria.

The record uses a date property with an is more than or is less than filter

If the record uses a date property trigger with the filter is more than or is less than [x] days ago, the trigger will only be checked at the start of the day. This can result in a delay in your record enrollment.

Workflow is not turned on

Records can only be enrolled in a workflow that is turned on. To turn a workflow on:

  • In the upper right of the workflow editor, click Review and publish.
  • Then, click Turn on. The Workflow is ON switch will be toggled on in the top right.

Why did my record unexpectedly enroll in a workflow?

When a record enrolls in a workflow unexpectedly, you can use the Diagnose tool to find out when the record enrolled and what events occurred for this to happen. Learn more about reviewing your workflow’s enrollment history from the workflow’s details and directly within the workflow editor.

Diagnose workflow enrollment issues

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.

  • Hover over the workflow and click More. Then, select View details.

  • Click the Enrollment history tab.

  • To view further details about the enrollment event, hover over an enrollment event, then click Why did this enroll?.

  • In the right panel, view the date and time of enrollment, and the reason why the record enrolled in the Enrollment information tab. This view displays the exact values at the time of enrollment.

  • If you’re using a property value or form submission enrollment trigger, to view details about the state of the property when the record enrolled in the workflow, click Details.

  • To review details about the events that led up to the record enrolling in the workflow, click the Record timeline tab.

  • In the top right, click View in CRM to open the record in your HubSpot account.

  • Click Done to return to the Enrollment history screen.

Reasons a record can enroll unexpectedly

The following are some common reasons why a record may be unexpectedly enrolling in a workflow and how you can prevent this moving forward.

Reason

Steps to resolve

Enrollment triggers include OR logic

If a workflow’s enrollment triggers include OR logic, a record only needs to meet one set of the enrollment triggers to qualify for enrollment.

For example, let’s say your workflow has the following enrollment triggers:

  • Lifecycle stage is any of Customer
  • OR
  • has filled out Customer survey form on Any page

A contact with a lifecycle stage of Customer that did not fill out the form will be enrolled in the workflow.

To prevent this contact from enrolling, the criteria would need to be separated by an AND operator, rather than OR. Learn more about AND vs OR logic.

Enrollment triggers include does not contain any of or is not equal to any of (contact-based workflows)

Contact-based workflows using does not contain any of or is not equal to any of filter-based criteria will enroll contacts that don’t have a specified value for the selected property. If the property is blank, it will meet the enrollment trigger. This also applies to records associated with the contact, such as an associated company.

This can especially affect workflows that use analytics or association properties for enrollment, such as:

  • Create date
  • IP Country
  • Original source
  • Associated contacts

Analytics and association properties are processed and populated almost instantly. However, workflow enrollment may occur before HubSpot fills the property. For example, if your workflow enrolls contacts based on the trigger IP Country is not equal to any of United States, a contact with no value may enroll before HubSpot is able to set the property with the value United states.

To prevent contacts without property values from entering the workflow:

  • In the enrollment trigger editor, add an AND condition underneath the doesn’t contain any of filter.
  • Select the same property that you’re filtering for, then select the is known filter.
  • Click Done.

Enrollment triggers include is unknown

The enrollment trigger is unknown searches for records without a value for the specified property. Enrolled records will remain in the workflow even if they gain a value for the property after enrollment.

This can sometimes cause unintended enrollment when using properties that are automatically populated by HubSpot. While HubSpot fills these properties almost instantly, workflow enrollment can happen before the property is filled.

To avoid similar issues:

  • Add a 1 minute delay before the first action in your workflow. This delay provides a buffer for HubSpot to fill any automatically populated properties and unenroll them from the workflow.
  • Configure the workflow’s settings to unenroll any records that no longer meet the enrollment trigger:
    • Contact-based workflows: in the workflow’s Unenrollment and suppression settings, select the option to unenroll contacts when they no longer meet the enrollment triggers.
    • Other workflow types: in the workflow’s Unenrollment and suppression settings, add unenrollment triggers opposite to the original is unknown enrollment triggers. For example, if an enrollment trigger is IP country is unknown, add the unenrollment trigger IP country is known.

Enrollment triggers include is known

The enrollment trigger is known searches for records with any value for the specified property. This can sometimes cause unintended enrollment when you make frequent updates to a property, or it requires manual edits.

For example, your sales reps update five deal property values together. You have a deal-based workflow that triggers when Amount is known. The rep enters a value for Amount that automatically saves. They decide to change the value a short time later. This could result in multiple workflow enrollments for the record.

To avoid similar issues:

  • Add a specific time delay before the first action in your workflow. This delay provides a buffer for the user to enter an appropriate value into the property.
  • Add all desired properties to the enrollment trigger. For example, you can configure your workflow enrollment triggers to require all five deal properties, instead of one. This setup ensures the properties must contain values before the workflow enrolls the deal.
  • Use Property value changed event triggers instead. This means the enrollment should occur when the property changes to a specific value, preventing unintended enrollment (e.g., Amount is greater than 1,000).

The record has been enrolled in an earlier workflow version

If the record has been enrolled, but does not currently meet any of the enrollment triggers, the workflow may have been updated since the time of enrollment. It is recommended to check the workflow’s version history.

In rare cases, there may be a race condition when an earlier enrollment trigger has been met, while the workflow is being updated. This means that an eligible property value may be processed seconds before the workflow change was processed.

Turn off workflows

Turn a workflow off to stop new records from enrolling. When a workflow has been turned off, no records will be enrolled. Existing records that are still in the workflow will remain enrolled, but actions will not execute, except for delays, which are not skipped.

Turning off a workflow will not pause enrolled records at a specific step. To prevent actions from executing on a specific day, use pause dates instead. Learn more about setting up pause dates.

Permissions required To turn off workflows, users must have Publish permissions for workflows or Super Admin permissions.

Turn off a workflow manually

To manually turn off a workflow:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of the workflow.
  • In the upper right, click to toggle the Workflow is ON switch off.

Turn off workflows in bulk

To turn off multiple workflows at once:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the checkboxes next to the workflows that you’d like to turn off.
  • At the top of the table, click Turn off.
  • In the dialog box, click Turn off.

Turn off a workflow automatically

When creating or editing a workflow, you can schedule the workflow to turn off after a specific date in your workflow settings. For example, you may want to turn off the workflow that sends marketing emails for a conference after the event has ended.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of the workflow.
  • At the top, click the Settings tab.
  • In the right panel, click to toggle the Schedule workflow to turn off automatically switch on.
  • Click the Turn off this workflow on date picker and select a date. Then, select a time to turn the workflow off as well.
  • If the workflow is already turned on, click Save. The workflow will automatically update.
  • If the workflow has not been turned on, in the top right, click Review and publish, then click Turn on.

Impact on records in a workflow that is turned off

When a workflow is turned off:

  • Records that meet the enrollment triggers will not be enrolled.
  • Records currently enrolled in the workflow will stay enrolled, but any actions apart from delays will not be executed. For example, any Send email actions will be skipped and enrolled contacts will not receive automated emails.
  • Turning off a workflow will not pause enrolled records at a specific step or action, except for delays.
    • If your workflow includes a delay, and the workflow is turned back on before the delay ends, the record will continue through the workflow normally.
    • If your workflow does not include delays, or the record completes the delay and the workflow before the workflow is turned back on:
      • When the workflow is turned on, these records will not automatically resume in the workflow, as they will have exited the workflow. Instead, you can turn on re-enrollment, and manually re-enroll your records.
    • To prevent specific records from continuing to later steps if the record is in a delay, manually unenroll or remove them from the workflow before turning it back on.

Actions, if/then branches, delays, and scheduled actions will work as follows:

  • Actions: all actions will be skipped, and the workflow history will show an error for each skipped action. The error message will display: Action was skipped because the flow was turned off.
  • If/then branches: all branches will still evaluate enrolled records when the workflow is turned off. The workflow history will show a success message for each if/then branch, along with the resulting event.
  • Delays: records in the workflow will enter any delays. The workflow history will show a success message for each delay, along with the resulting event.
  • Scheduled actions: any scheduled actions will remain scheduled.
    • When the scheduled time arrives, the record will skip the scheduled action. For example:
      • A record has completed action #1 in your workflow, and it is scheduled for action #2 to execute two days later.
      • You turn the workflow off, and two days pass and the scheduled time for action #2 arrives. Because the workflow is still off, action #2 will not execute for that record.
      • The record will continue to the next action, scheduled delay, or will complete the workflow if there are no more actions.
    • If you turn a workflow off while a record is scheduled for an action, and then turn the workflow back on, the record will complete the scheduled action. For example:
      • A record has completed action #1 in your workflow, and it is scheduled for action #2 to execute two days later.
      • You turn the workflow off, then one day passes and you turn the workflow on again. One more day passes and the scheduled time for action #2 arrives. Because the workflow is on when action #2 is scheduled to execute, action #2 will execute for that record.
      • The record will continue to the next action, scheduled delay, or will complete the workflow if there are no more actions.

Please note: when a record skips actions when a workflow is turned off, these actions will not be executed when the workflow is turned on again. It is currently not possible to re-enroll a record into a specific step in a workflow.

Understand workflow object types

Select from the listed workflow object types when creating a workflow. When deciding which object type to use, you can review example use cases. It is also recommended to use the workflow template library and use workflow templates or refer to the community workflow library to review the different ways you can automate your processes in HubSpot.

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to create and edit workflows.

Workflow object types

When creating workflows, depending on your subscription, you can select from the following object types:

Available for all subscriptions listed above

Additional subscriptions required

  • Calls

  • Contacts

  • Companies

  • Conversations

  • Deals

  • Emails (one-to-one emails only)

  • Goals

Please note: when creating marketing event-based workflows (beta), actions related to contacts (e.g., attendees, registrants) are not supported. For example, you cannot send a thank-you email to all attendees when the event ends. To target these records, it is recommended to use contact-based workflows with event activity triggers such as Registered for marketing event instead.

Example use cases

The following examples outline the different ways you can use workflows to automate your processes. For more examples, you can review the workflow template library and use workflow templates to streamline your automation process. It is also recommended to use the community workflow library for ideas when setting up workflows.

  • Contact-based workflows:
    • Create a new deal when a contact submits a quote-request form.
    • Create a nurturing email flow when a contact submits a form on a CTA.
    • Update a contact’s lifecycle stage and properties based on interactions with your content.
    • Updated an external Google sheet based when a contact submits any form.
  • Company-based workflows:
    • Update property values based on associated contact records.
    • Start tracking intent signals when company becomes a target account.
    • Populate company data using agent actions.
  • Deal-based workflows:
    • Create tasks based on your deal stage.
    • Notify specific users when a deal moves into a specific deal stage.
  • Campaign-based workflows:

    • Trigger alerts when a campaign overspends its budget.

    • Create tasks based on campaign owner or team.

    • Use Edit record workflow action to update your campaign details.

  • Quote-based workflows:
    • Trigger an email or in-app notification when a prospect views a quote.
    • Send automated emails to follow up when a quote hasn’t been opened.
    • Send an automated email when a quote is signed.
  • Meeting-based workflows:
    • Set up a workflow to automatically update a deal stage after a meeting.
    • Set up a workflow to create a deal record anytime a demo meeting is booked. Then, automatically assign the deal to the meeting owner.
    • Use the Edit record action to update meeting details such as the Meeting Outcome from Scheduled to Completed.
  • Social post-based workflows (BETA):
    • Notify a Slack channel or send an internal email when a post is published so your team can share and promote the post.
    • Coordinate and trigger follow-up actions in other channels (e.g.,email, ads) when a social post goes live.
    • Send in-app or internal email notifications to alert stakeholders when scheduled content publishes for stakeholder visibility.
  • User-based workflows:
    • Use the Is out of office property to trigger a workflow when a user has an active Out of Office period set. Use it to automatically reassign their tickets, notify a backup agent, or update routing without manual intervention.
    • Use the Is in workflow hours property to trigger a workflow depending on an user’s configured working hours. Use it to direct traffic to Customer Agent after hours, escalate to a coverage team, or route differently on weekends.

Set specific workflow object types

When creating a workflow from scratch, it is generally recommended to set up your triggers first. However, there are instances where you may want to select your workflow’s enrollment object type first. For example, you may want to create a contact or company-based workflow, then set any relevant triggers after.

Please note: after you select your workflow record type, you will not be able to change the workflow type.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • In the top right, click Create workflow and select From scratch.
  • At the bottom of the left panel, click Skip trigger and choose eligible records.

.

  • Under the Choose a type of record that can enroll field, locate and select the desired object type for your enrolled records.
    • For example, to create a contact-based workflow, select Contact.
    • After you select your workflow record type, you will not be able to change the workflow type.
    • In the right panel, the enrollment trigger card will display Trigger enrollment for [object-type].
  • At the top, click Save and continue.
  • Continue setting up your workflow.

Understand your automation overview

From your automation overview page, you can use HubSpot’s AI to create new automations. You can also get recommendations for creating different automations, and review an overview of all automation tools in your HubSpot account.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Review your automation overview (Professional or Enterprise)

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Automations > Overview.
  • At the top, you can navigate to the following other tabs:
    • Workflows: navigate to your workflows index page. Learn more about organizing and managing your workflows.
    • Analyze: review and analyze the overall enrollment data and any additional opportunities for automating more processes in your account. Learn more about analyzing your workflow performance and opportunities.
    • Health: review the overall health of your workflows. For example, you can analyze an overview of workflows with issues or unused workflows. Learn more about monitoring your workflow health.

.

From your Automations overview page, you can monitor and engage with the following:

  • What do you want to automate: use AI to generate new automations in HubSpot.
    • To manually set a prompt, enter a prompt in the text field. It’s recommended to use the When [this happens], then [do this] structure when entering your prompt.
    • To use a suggested prompt, in the Prompts for you based on your portal activity section, choose the prompt that you want to use. The selected prompt will automatically appear in the text field.
    • Click Create automation. In the Breeze Assistant panel, you can review details about the generated automation.
    • To review the automation, click View [automation]. You’ll be automatically redirected to the corresponding editor.
  • Discover more automations: review a list of suggested automation recommendations.
    • To create a recommended automation, click Try this [automation].

  • Monitor performance: review the following automation reports.

      • For example, you can keep track of the number of workflows, chatflows, pipeline automations, and more.
      • For more details, click the number under each automation. You will be directed to the selected automation tool index page.
    • Workflow enrollments: review the count of workflow enrollments over the last 6 months, by each month.

Review your automation overview (Starter)

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Automations > Overview.
  • From your Automations overview page, you can monitor and engage with the following:

Understand your workflow details page

Use the workflow details page to review your workflow history and performance. You can review a workflow’s history to check past events and analyze its performance to measure effectiveness.

When troubleshooting specific records in your workflow, it’s strongly recommended to individual records’ paths directly in the workflow editor. You can also review the conversion and performance data for different actions from the workflow editor.

To understand your overall workflow performance, learn how to analyze your workflows and use the workflows health page.

Understand limitations and requirements

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to use the workflows tool.

After creating your workflow and turning it on, navigate to the workflow details page to view the events that have occurred in the workflow, including action logs and enrollment history.

  • HubSpot will store workflow data within the below time periods:
    • 90 days: all workflow action log data will be stored. This includes high-level action log data such as object ID (which contact, company, deal, etc.), event type (enrollment, unenrollment, etc.), and action type will be stored.
    • 6 months: historical data of enrollments will be retained in our system to enable workflow-based filters.
  • When reviewing your workflow history, there is a 100,000 log limit for successful workflow executions per day.
    • This is calculated from midnight in the account’s time zone.
    • Once the limit is exceeded:
      • Success and info logs will not be stored for the rest of the day.
      • Error logs will continue to appear.
      • Records will continue enrolling and executing normally through the workflow.
Action logs

On the Actions logs tab, view the past events within the workflow. The events are displayed in reverse chronological order, with the most recent events appearing at the top. In larger workflows, do note that contact enrollments and action activity may take time to appear.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.

  • Hover over the name of the workflow and click More. Then select View details.

  • At the top, click the Action logs tab.

  • The Action logs table displays:

    • Diagnose: review details on why an action occurred.
    • Action: the step of the workflow that caused the event.
    • Event: the result of the action.
    • Time: when the action happened. The timestamp reflects the account’s default time zone.

  • By default, the Actions logs display events for all event types. To filter events, in the upper left, click the dropdown menus:

    • Date range: filter by time period.
    • Event: filter by All events, Sucesses, Information, or Errors. This can help to identify workflow issues, such as an email failing to send.
    • Revisions: filter by the version history of the workflow shown by timestamp.
    • Actions in revision: filter by a specific action in the workflow. A specific revision must be selected to use this filter, this filter won’t work if the Revisions filter is set to All revisions.
    • Action types: filter by the workflow action type.

  • To remove all filters, click Clear filters.

  • To export your action log data, in the upper right, click Export and select Export action logs to .csv.

  • To search for a specific record, in the upper right, click Choose a trigger source. In the dialog box, click the Trigger source dropdown menu, then search for and select a specific record.

    • For example, when searching for a record, you can use a ticket record’s record ID or a contact record’s email address.
    • If the record is currently enrolled or has ever been enrolled in the workflow, you can review all workflow events that occurred to the object.
    • If an expected record doesn’t appear, you may want to try adjusting the selected date range.

  • To unenroll a record from the workflow, hover over an event, then click Unenroll. This option will only appear when the record is currently active in the workflow.

  • To view the workflow revision at the time of an event, hover over an event, then click Event details.

    • Click the Timestamp under Workflow revision at time of event.
      • This timestamp reflects when the workflow was revised.
      • You’ll also see the user who changed the workflow underneath the timestamp.
    • On the workflow revision screen, view the enrollment conditions and actions set in the workflow in that version. You can click the enrollment triggers and action boxes to view the details of that version. The workflow cannot be edited from this view.

Please note: the workflow’s revision history from the action logs do not include custom code actions, and settings such as unenrollment and suppression. These revisions are read-only and can’t be restored. To restore a previous version of a workflow, learn how to review and revert worfklow changes from the workflow editor.

Enrollment history

In the Enrollment history tab, view all workflow enrollments, including enrollments up to 6 months ago. It’ll also display all actions that occurred for a record.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Hover over the name of the workflow and click More. Then select View details.
  • At the top, click the Enrollment history tab.
  • To filter your workflow enrollment history, in the upper left, click the dropdown menus:
    • Date range: filter by time period.
    • Revisions: filter by the version history of the workflow shown by timestamp.
  • To export your enrollment history data, in the upper right, click Export and select Export action logs to .csv.
  • To search for a specific record, in the upper right, click Choose a trigger source. In the dialog box, click the Trigger source dropdown menu, then search for and select a specific record.
    • If an expected record doesn’t appear, you may want to try adjusting the selected date range.
  • To view the complete workflow history, hover over the record you want to see the history of, then click Enrollment details.
  • In the right panel, review the record’s workflow history.
  • To view the details of an event, click the name of the event to expand it.
    • Action: the step of the workflow where the action occurred.
    • Time: the time that the event happened.
    • Workflow revision at time of event: the version of the workflow at the time of the event. You’ll also see the user who changed the workflow. Click the timestamp to view the workflow layout at the time.
Issues

From the issues page, you can review an overall list of issues in your workflow that you may want to fix or ignore. In the workflow editor, you can then track individual records’ paths and errors to further troubleshoot any issues.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Hover over the name of the workflow and click More. Then select View details.
  • In the top right, click Review workflow issues.
  • Continue analyzing your workflow issues.

Analyze your workflow performance

On the Performance tab, analyze the performance of your workflow with metrics such as enrollments and email trends.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Hover over the name of the workflow and click More. Then select View details.
Top metrics

The Top metrics report will show the following workflow data:

  • Total [object-type] enrolled: the total number of times records were enrolled in the workflow. This includes records that may have enrolled more than once during re-enrollment.
  • Estimated unique [object-type] enrolled: the total number of unique records enrolled in the workflow since creation. This does not include records that have re-enrolled.
  • 7 day total enrollment: the number of enrolled records in the past 7 days based on your account’s timezone.
Enrollment trends

The Enrollment over time report shows the performance of enrolled records in the workflow in the selected time period:

  • [Object-type] enrolled: the number of records currently enrolled in the workflow.
  • [Object-type] lost: when a record is lost, this means that one of the following has occurred:
    • The record was manually unenrolled.
    • The record met the workflow’s criteria and was not sent a marketing email.
    • The record was on a suppression list.
    • The record was removed by enrollment in another workflow.
    • The record was removed by the When a contact no longer meets the enrollment conditions, remove them from this workflow? unenrollment setting.
    • The records were lost due to contacts unsubscribing from an email, hard bouncing, or by marking an email as spam.
  • Completed workflow: the number of records that completed the final action in the workflow.

To use the Enrollment over time performance report:

  • Hover over a data point in the chart to view a numerical breakdown of each metric.
  • To select or compare different time periods:
    • In the top right, click Actions, then select Edit.
    • In the dialog box, you can update the following:
      • Date range: select a new custom date range.
      • Data frequency: select from a Daily, Weekly, or Monthly data frequency.
      • Compare to: select the checkbox to compare your data to a different time period. Then, click the dropdown menu and select Last week, Last month, Last quarter, or Last year.
    • After updating your time period, at the bottom, click Save.
Email trends (Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise only)

Workflows with automated marketing emails that were sent with a Send email action will have the following email performance report:

  • Emails in workflow: this report shows all marketing emails sent in the workflow. You can review the the percentage of contacts who: skipped, were sent, delivered, opened, and clicked the email. Send counts will only include contacts that reached the Send email action. Contacts waiting in a delay before the action will not be included. If the Send email action was deleted or replaced, sends from the earlier action will not be counted toward the new action’s metrics.
    • To sort the report by a specific metric, click the corresponding column header.
    • To select a different time period, in the top right, click the date pickers and set a date range.
    • To view raw counts instead of rates (percentages), in the top right, click the View as dropdown menu.

Use action recommendations in workflows

When creating a new workflow, you can add actions recommended by Breeze, HubSpot’s AI, to streamline your workflow creation process.

Workflow actions will be suggested based on common usage patterns. As users accept recommendations, the suggestions provided will be further refined and surfaced.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

To use recommended workflow actions:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow or create a new workflow.
  • Set your enrollment triggers.
  • In the workflow editor, click the + plus icon and add your workflow actions.
    • If a recommendation is available, the suggested action will appear after your added action. Suggestions will be generated based on patterns from similar workflows.
    • If no strong recommendation is available, no suggestions will appear.
  • To use a recommendation, click Add. Then, set up your workflow action.
  • To ignore a workflow recommendation, click Dismiss. The workflow recommendation will disappear from the editor.
  • To provide feedback about a recommendation:
    • If a recommended action was helpful, click the thumbs up icon.
    • If a recommended action wasn’t helpful, click the thumbs down icon.

Use AI actions to manage data in workflows

Use AI actions to manage data in your workflows. For example, you can use the Data Agent: Custom prompt or Data Agent: Research workflow actions to analyze, summarize, and categorize data from enrolled records. You can also use the Data Agent: Fill Smart Property workflow action to use AI to populate your smart properties.

After, use outputs from the action with other workflow actions, such as the Edit record action or branches. For example, within the action, you can enter a prompt to analyze enrolled records and then use a branch to categorize these records.

If your account has a Marketing Hub Enterprise subscription, you can also use this action to generate personalized content to use in automated marketing emails.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Understand limitations and requirements

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to create workflows.

Before using the Data Agent: Custom prompt or Data Agent: Research workflow actions to analyze your records’ data, please note the following:

  • The Give users access to generative AI tools and features and CRM data settings must be turned on. Learn more about managing your AI settings.
  • The LLM model used in the Data Agent: Custom prompt is not connected to the internet.
  • If your account does not have sufficient credits, the Data Agent: Custom prompt action will fail and result in null values being populated as the output. Learn how to troubleshoot and resolve this issue.

Use the Data Agent: Custom prompt workflow action

To use the Data Agent: Custom prompt action:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow or create a new workflow.
  • Set your enrollment triggers.
  • Click the + plus icon to add an action.
  • In the left panel, click to expand the AI section. Then, click Data Agent: Custom prompt.
  • In the Message section, enter your prompt. You can use the data panel to add properties from the enrolled or any associated records to the prompt.
    • It is recommended to include all the information that you’d like to use in the prompt. The prompt will not include any extra context or information beyond the data added to the prompt. Any context that should be considered must be included in the prompt.

      • For example, it will not have access to the enrolled record’s other properties, timeline activity, contents of recently sent or received emails, and more, unless added to the prompt.

      • To create a personalized and dynamic response for each enrolled record, you must add personalization tokens such as contact properties. You can also add information from associated records or activities by adding data variables to the action.

    • When entering your prompt, it is recommended to limit the response to fit your subsequent action. For example, in your prompt, you can add: The response should be limited to a one-word answer with a value of either “manufacturer” or “importer”.
    • Prompts messages are limited to 3,000 characters in length.

.

  • To define your outputs, click to expand the Action outputs section. This is optional.
  • Click + Add output to define your action outputs.
  • Click the first dropdown menu and select your output type. Then, enter your output value. To select from a list of values:
    • Select Enumeration as your output type.
    • Enter your output value.
    • To add additional options, click + Add value.
    • To remove an option, click the deletedelete icon.
  • To remove an output, click the deletedelete icon next to the output.
  • At the top, click Save.
