Example use cases

The following examples outline the different ways you can use the Summarize record action in workflows to automate more complex processes:

  • Send lead data efficiently: after assigning a contact to a sales rep, you can use the output from the Summarize record action to send a summary of the contact to the rep.
  • Simplify research for sales reps: review a summary of a contact’s company before setting up the first meeting or calling the contact. You can also copy this data to a custom property on the record.

Use journey automation

Use journeys to build engaging and personalized marketing automation experiences all within the same view, instead of building across a handful of workflows. Marketers can build out marketing strategies, including lead generation, lead nurturing, or customer re-engagement campaigns.

After creating your journey, you can analyze your journey’s performance and report on your marketing automation efforts.

Please note: on November 30th, 2026, journeys will be sunset. After that date, you’ll no longer be able to create and use the journeys tool. Instead, it is recommended to use campaign automation in Marketing Studio. To use automation and other features in Marketing Studio, you must opt into the Marketing Studio beta.

Permissions required Super Admin or Journey permissions are required to use journey automation.

Create journeys

When creating journeys, enroll contacts using an enumeration property and selected lists. You can assign each journey stage to a different property value. Each stage will work as an automated flow. Contacts will move through the journey on different paths depending on their progress through each stage.

In each journey, you can set one goal exit end based on your goals, corresponding to the journey property value selected. However, you can have multiple unsuccessful ends based on different property values.

For example, you can set up a journey with the new default Journey stage property. Then, create stages for each of the Journey stage property values and add actions to automatically execute at each stage. Finally, set Journey stage property values for your goal exit and other exits.

Create a new journey

Each user can create up to 10 journeys. To create a new journey:

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Marketing > Journeys.
  • In the top right, click Create journey.
  • To create a journey from scratch:
    • In the right panel, select Start from scratch.
    • In the bottom right, click Next. You’ll be directed to the journey editor. Then, continue setting up your journey.
  • To create a journey from a template:
    • In the right panel, select Use a template.
    • In the bottom right, click Next.
    • Select your template. Then, click Next. You’ll be directed to the journey editor. Then, continue setting up your journey.
  • If you’re creating a journey for the first time, to learn how to create a journey from scratch:
    • In the right panel, select Guided setup.
    • In the bottom right, click Next. Then, follow the guided tour to create a new journey.
  • In the journey editor, you can review your journey as different engagement paths, or as a single journey tree. To select your view, in the top right, click the engagement path icon or the tree icon.
Set up journey enrollment

When building a new journey, select your lists for enrollment and center your journey around a property such as Journey stage or lifecycle stage. You can use any enumeration property such as a dropdown select, multiple checkboxes, or radio select type property.

When setting up a journey, you can assign specific property values to different journey stages. When a contact is updated with a specific property value, they will enroll in the corresponding stage. After setting up your journey, it is still possible to change the journey’s enrollment property and property values used for each stage.

Please note: you cannot select the same eligibility lists and property as another journey. To set up a new journey, you must select different lists or a different property for enrollment.

To set up your enrollment criteria:

  • In the top left, click Enrollment.
  • Click the They’re in any of the selected lists dropdown menu and select the contact lists with contacts eligible to enroll in the journey.
    • This doesn’t mean that contacts will automatically enroll. Contacts will still need to meet either the journey’s starting criteria or any of the stage values to enroll.
    • Contacts will still continue on the journey even if removed from lists after enrolling.
    • You can select up to 5 lists. Learn more about using lists.
  • Click the Contact property equals value dropdown menu and select a property.
Set up journey unenrollment

To set up unenrollment criteria in the journey editor:

  • In the top left, click Enrollment.
  • In the left panel, click the Unenrollment tab.
  • Select the checkboxes next to the unenrollment criteria that you’d like to apply:
    • Are on or join a suppression list: unenroll contacts from the journey when they’re added to any of the selected suppression lists.
    • Are removed from enrollment lists: unenroll contacts from the journey if they’re no longer in the enrollment lists.
    • Match an end stage early: unenroll contacts from the journey if they match an end stage in the journey. When selecting this, contacts will skip any final actions associated with the end stage.
Change the journey enrollment criteria

If you’ve previously set up your journey with a different property, to update the property used:

  • In the top left, click Enrollment.
  • In the left panel, click the Contact property equals value dropdown menu and select a new property.
  • At the top, click Save.
  • In the dialog box, select a corresponding stage value based on the new property.
  • At the bottom, click Save updates. To select the stages’ property values later, click Skip.
Select a journey’s starting stage

Select a property value from the enrollment property to begin enrolling contacts into your journey:

  • In the journey editor, from the starting stage, click Details. In the left panel, set up your journey starting stage:

    • Click the first dropdown menu and select a property. If you’ve previously selected a property when setting up enrollment, the property will appear by default.
    • Click the second dropdown menu and select a property value to set as your enrollment stage value.
    • To enroll new contacts with no property value for the selected property, select the Enroll contacts with blank value in this stage checkbox.
    • In the top, click Save.
Configure your journey stages and actions

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

To add more stages and actions to each of your journey stages:

  • In the journey editor, hover over the line and click the + icon. Then, select Add new stage. When adding a new stage to an unsuccessful path:
    • If you’re in the tree view, this’ll create a new branch.
    • If you’re in the engagement path view, this’ll create a new alternative path section in the editor. You can click the collapse icon to collapse and expand each section.
    • You can add up 10 stages per journey.

.

  • After adding a stage you can add actions to your newly added stages. In the stage, click the menu icon and select Edit flow.
    • You must add at least one action for each stage.
    • You can add up to 50 actions per stage.
  • To add an action in your stage, click the + plus icon. Then, you can use Breeze Assistant (beta) or manually add actions to your stages.
  • To use Breeze Assistant to add actions (beta), click Build with Assistant. Then, enter your prompt and click the send icon. Actions will be suggested based on the request.
  • When manually adding an action, you can select from the following action types:
    • Marketing actions: select from the following marketing actions.
      • Send Assets: send an automated marketing email, SMS, or WhatsApp message to the contact. When setting up this action, you can trigger all three asset types to send at once.
      • Wait: add a delay for a specified amount of time.
      • Wait until activity: delay until a specific user activity occurs. For example, delay until the user submits a form, visits a specific page on a website, replies to an email, or more.
    • Process actions: select from the following process actions.
      • Create task: create and add a task to the enrolled contact. This task will also appear on the tasks page. Learn more about using tasks.
      • Set property: set a specific property value for the enrolled contact. You can configure the stage used for the journey automation.
      • Send notification: send an in-app or internal email notification. You can send the notification to specific users, teams, or the enrolled contact’s existing owners.
    • Go to: associate the stage with a successful or unsuccessful end.
  • After setting up your actions, in the top left click Exit to journey.

.

  • In the main journey editor:
    • To route a contact back to an earlier stage, hover over the line and click the + icon. Then, select Go to stage. This option can only be selected for stages, go to paths cannot be added between stages.
    • To end a journey, hover over the line and click the + icon. Then, select End journey. This will automatically add a Goal exit or Exit.
Determine the success of your journey

Select a property value to determine the success or failure of your journey. To set up your Goal exit or Exit:

  • In the Goal exit or Exit box, click Set up. If you’re using a template or editing an existing journey, click the stage name.
  • In the right panel, click the Set [property name] to dropdown menu and select a property value.
  • For each end, you can also click the Add to static list dropdown menu and select a static list. This will add all contacts who have finished the journey to the selected static list. This is an optional step.

Please note: you can only select one Goal exit end per journey.

Turn on your journey
  • After setting up your journey automation, in the top right, click Review and publish.
  • In the right panel, you can review the number of contacts eligible for the journey. You can also configure the following:
    • Do you want to enroll contacts that currently meet the enrollment criteria when the workflow turns on: choose to enroll records that currently meet the enrollment criteria or only enroll records that meet the criteria in the future.
      • Yes, enroll existing contacts who meet the enrollment criteria immediately when the journey is turned on: enroll all existing records that meet the enrollment criteria.
      • No, only enroll contacts who meet the enrollment criteria after the journey is turned on: only enroll records that meet the enrollment criteria after the workflow is turned on.
  • At the bottom, click Turn on journey.

Manage your journeys

From the journey index page, you can edit, delete, and manage your journeys. When editing a journey, please note the following:

  • You can edit both published journeys or journeys in a draft state. When editing a journey, updates will not be published automatically. You can make changes to the journey before manually publishing.
  • If you delete a stage, any contacts in the deleted stage will be removed from the stage and will be inactive. These contacts will not enroll in another stage unless their tracking property is updated to a stage value.
  • If you delete a single action or add an action within a flow:
    • Contacts will automatically move to the next available action.
    • For example, you have a send notification, create task, and set property action in sequence. If you delete the create task action, any contacts will move from directly from the send notification action to the set property action.
  • If you delete multiple actions in sequence:
    • Contacts in the previous action will become inactive and will not enroll in another stage or action unless their tracking property is updated to a stage value.
    • For example, you have a send notification, send assets, create task, and set property action in sequence. If you delete both the send assets and the create task actions, then contacts currently in the send notification action will become inactive.

To manage your journey:

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Marketing > Journeys.

  • To see which assets were used in a journey, such as emails or SMS messages, click More and select See assets used. The assets will appear in the right panel.

  • To review the performance of a journey, click More and select View details.

  • To delete a journey, click More and select Delete.

  • To edit a journey:

    • Hover over the journey and click Edit. You will be directed to the journey editor.
    • Edit your journey.
    • After editing your journey, in the top right, click Update and select Review and publish draft.

.

Review the version history of a journey

To review the version history of a journey:

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Marketing > Journeys.
  • Click the name of an existing journey.
  • To view the version history of the overall journey, in the top right, click View and select Version history.
  • To view the revision history of a specific journey stage, click Edit flow on the stage that you’d like to review. Then, click View and select Version history in the top right.
  • In the right panel, you can review all previous versions of your journey or journey stage, sorted by date. At the top, you can filter your version history by the Date range for the version or the User that edited that version.
  • To view more details about the changes made in each version, click the right dropdown icon to expand the section for the version.
  • To view a specific version, hover over the version and click View version.
  • To restore a specific version, hover over the version and click Restore. Then, click Restore version.
    • This feature will only apply when reviewing overall journeys. It will not appear when reviewing individual journey stages.
    • The restored version of the journey will be saved as the current draft and any previous changes in your draft will be erased.
    • After restoring your journey, you’ll still need to publish your journey to take the updates live.

Review your journey’s performance

After turning on your journey, you can analyze the enrollment history and individual performance of each journey. This includes the journey’s metrics, reporting, and details such as conversion metrics.

Review journey reports

You can review your journey reports while reviewing your overall performance in your journey details or from the journey report editor.

  • To review your journey reports from your journey details:
    • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Marketing > Journeys.
    • Hover over a journey. Then, click More and select View details.
    • At the top, click the Reports tab.
  • To review your journey reports from the journey report editor:

    • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Marketing > Journeys.

    • Click the name of an existing journey.

    • In the top right of the journey editor, click View and select Report.

    • To review the overall journey dashboard, click View all reports.

    • In the Stage reports section, click Preview report for the stage you want to preview.

    • To review the report in the reports editor, click Go to report.

Please note: you cannot edit journey reports.

Review a journey’s conversion metrics

From the journey editor, you can review your journey’s conversion metrics for each stage of the journey.

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Marketing > Journeys.
  • Click the name of an existing journey.
  • To review your journey metrics, in the top right, click View and select Metrics. From the metrics page, you can review the following:
    • The total enrollment count for the journey.
    • The percentage and count of enrollments that reached each endpoint.
    • For each stage, the percentage of enrollments that continued along each path.
Review a journey’s performance

To review a journey’s overall performance metrics:

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Marketing > Journeys.
  • Hover over the journey. Then, click More and select View details.
  • From the Performance tab, you can review the following performance reports. The reports will only show data from when the journey was turned on.

    • Top metrics: this report displays the total number of enrolled contacts out of all eligible contacts, the number of successful contacts, and unsuccessful contacts.

    • More contact metrics: this report displays the number of eligible contacts and contacts that have exited early from the journey.

    • Successful conversions: the percentage of successful conversions with the count of eligible contacts, enrolled contacts, and contacts that reached the journey with a successful end.

    • Unsuccessful conversions: the percentage of successful conversions with the count of eligible contacts, enrolled contacts, and contacts that reached the journey with an unsuccessful end.

Review journey enrollments

To review a list of contacts that have enrolled in your journey:

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Marketing > Journeys.
  • Hover over a journey. Then, click More and select View details.
  • At the top, click the Action and enrollment logs tab.

Please note: each contact can only enroll in a journey once. Contacts cannot re-enroll in a journey.

Use records created earlier in the same workflow

Use records created in a workflow, later in the same workflow. For example, in a company-based workflow, you create a new contact record. Within that same workflow, you can add actions to set the marketing contact status of that contact and use the properties from it when creating a task or a note for your team.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.

  • Click the name of an existing workflow, or create a new workflow.

  • Add a Create record or a Create task action to create a new record in your workflow.

  • In the workflow editor, click the + add icon.

  • In the left panel, select your action. Learn more about the different workflow actions available.

  • To take action on the newly created record, you can click the [object-type] dropdown menu and select The created object. This may not be available on all actions.

  • To use properties from the newly created record:

    • After selecting your action, in the left panel, click on the field that you’d like to use the data with.
    • In the Action data section, click Create record.
    • In the The created object section, you can select properties from your newly created record. Learn more about adding data variables in workflows.

  • Continue setting up your workflow action.

  • At the top, click Save.

Use the workflow navigation bar

Use the workflow navigation bar when creating and editing your workflows. Below, review an overview of how the navigation is organized in the workflow editor. When using the new navigation bar in the workflow editor, you can also use keyboard shortcuts.

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to use the workflows tool.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow or create a new workflow. The new workflow navigation bar will appear in the top left of the workflow editor.

File

  • New: create a new workflow. The workflow editor will launch in a new tab.
  • Clone: create a duplicate of the existing workflow.
  • Export as .PNG: export the workflow as displayed in the workflow editor, as a PNG file. You may encounter issues when exporting larger or more complex workflows. It is recommended to simplify your workflow before trying again.
  • Organize: manage your workflow’s details, associations, and organization within the workflow tool.
    • About this workflow: review and update the workflow’s name and description. You can use AI assistant to generate a workflow description.
    • Assign workflow access: assign the workflow to a specific team. Only teams with access will be able to edit the workflow. Learn more about managing access to your HubSpot assets.
    • Add business unit label: if you have the Business units add on, you can associate your workflow with a specific business unit.
    • Add campaign label: if you have a Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription, you can add your workflow to a campaign as a campaign asset.
    • Move to folder: add the workflow to an existing workflow folder. Learn more about organizing your workflow with folders.
  • Delete: delete the workflow. After deleting a workflow, you can still clone the workflow for up to 90 days. Learn more about deleting workflows.

Edit

  • Edit enrollment trigger: change the enrollment triggers or event enrollment triggers for the workflow.
  • Add action: add a new action to the workflow. This action will be added to the end of your workflow.
  • Edit available records: edit the records can be used to trigger actions or have associated data used in fields as data variables.
  • Edit goal: set a goal and keep track of your progress in contact-based workflows. Contacts that meet the workflow goal will be automatically unenrolled. Learn more about using goals.
  • Clean up workflow: automatically streamline your workflow. If there are no opportunities to clean up your workflow, this option will be greyed out.
  • Undo: revert the most recent change to your workflow in the workflow editor.
  • Redo: if you’ve previously selected the Undo option, use this to make the same change again.

View

  • Comments: review and add comments to the workflow in the collaboration sidebar. Learn more about adding and managing comments in workflows.
  • Zoom: zoom in to get a closer view of your workflow, zoom out to get a further view of your workflow. You can also view a simplified minimap of the workflow.
  • Test: preview how a record will proceed through your workflow if enrolled.
  • Connections: review the workflow’s associated assets. For example, if a workflow uses a form submission as an enrollment criteria, the form will appear in this list. Learn more about reviewing your workflow’s connections.
  • Revision history: review historical changes to the workflow. Learn more about reviewing your workflow history.
  • Performance: review your workflow’s performance. The workflow’s performance page will open in a new tab.
  • Enrollment history: review your workflow’s enrollments, including enrollments from more than 90 days ago.
  • Metrics: review and use your workflow actions’ conversion and performance data to analyze the effectiveness of each section of the workflow. Learn more about managing your workflow’s conversion and performance data.
  • Action logs: review your workflow’s action logs. The workflow’s Action logs will open in a new tab.

Settings

  • Settings: access the workflow’s settings page. Learn more about managing workflow settings.

Help

  • Knowledge base: access workflow how-to guides, reference docs, and troubleshooting steps in HubSpot’s Knowledge Base. The workflow Knowledge Base page will open in a new tab.
  • Troubleshoot issues: diagnose and troubleshoot workflow execution issues. Learn more about troubleshooting workflows.
  • Troubleshoot enrollment: diagnose why a record didn’t enroll in a workflow. Learn how to troubleshoot enrollment issues.

Use workflow action outputs

In the data panel, select action outputs from other workflow actions to use in your workflow action. For example, you’ve added a Format data action in your workflow. To use the formatted data, you’ll still need to configure seperate workflow action to use the action output, such as the Edit record action or Send to Google Sheets action.

Workflow actions with outputs

The following workflow actions produce action outputs that you can use with other workflow actions.

  • Format data
  • Validate and format phone number
  • Ask Anthropic
  • Ask OpenAI Assistant
  • Data Agent: Custom prompt (BETA)
  • Data Agent: Research (BETA)
  • Data Agent: Fill Smart Property (BETA)
  • Summarize record (BETA)
  • Infer company value proposition and ICP (BETA)
  • Use a custom LLM (BETA)

Examples

When using an action that produces an output, you’ll need to use the action ouput with another, seperate workflow action. In general, you can use action outputs with workflow actions that accept inputs, such as the Edit record action, the Create Google Sheet row action, the Create task action, and more.

The following are some examples of how you can use workflow action outputs:

  • Format your record data: use the Data Agent: Custom prompt action to format data in your account. If the data has been filled or submitted in different formats, you can use the action to standardize the values into specific formats. For example, you can format different values in a state property to two-letter state abbreviations. Then, you can use a One property or action output branch to create branches for lead assignment based on each state.
  • Simplify research for sales reps: use the output from the Summarize record action review a summary of a contact’s company before setting up the first meeting or calling the contact. You can add this information to the Notes of a Create task action. You can also copy this data to a custom property with the Edit Record action.
  • Send lead data efficiently: after assigning a contact to a sales rep, you can use the output from the Summarize record action to send a summary of the contact to the rep with the Send internal email notification action.
  • Update google sheet: after formatting phone numbers with the Validate and format phone number action, you can use the Create Google Sheet row action or Update data in a Google Sheet action to send formatted data to a Google sheet. For example, as part of an outreach list.

Use workflow action outputs

When setting up the workflow action to use your action output with, you can select the action ouput from the data panel.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow, or create a new workflow.
  • In the workflow editor, click the + plus icon to add a workflow action.
  • In the actions panel, select the Action that you’d like to use your output with.
  • In the left panel, click the field that you’d like to use the action output.
  • For checkbox and other select-type fields:
    • Click the dropdown menu and select choose data variable.
    • In the Choose a data variable panel, click on the Enrolled [object] dropdown menu and select Action outputs. When copying a value to a different property, the properties must be compatible. Learn more about compatible property types.
    • Click to expand the previous action name and select an action output.
  • For text input properties:
    • Click the Choose a value text box.
    • In the Choose a data variable panel, click on the Enrolled [object] dropdown menu and select Action outputs.
    • Click to expand the previous action name and select an action output.
  • Click Save.

View and revert changes to your workflow

From a workflow’s revision history, review a history of changes made to the workflow. This includes what changes were made, when each change was made, and the user who made the change. You can also revert to that specific revision of the workflow.

If you would like to view your workflow’s Enrollment history and Action logs instead, learn more about the workflow details page. You can also review and revert CRM property changes from a specific workflow. Learn how to restore workflow CRM property changes.

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to use the workflows tool.

To review and revert a workflow’s change history:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.

  • Click the name of a workflow you’d like to review.

  • At the top left, click View > Revision History.

  • In the right panel, all changes will be listed chronologically, with the most recent change at the top. To filter events, at the top, select from the following:

    • Date Range: filter by the time period when the change was made.
    • Event: filter by the specific type of change, such as changed enrollment triggers or changed timing settings.
    • User: filter by the user who made the change. When reviewing your workflow change history, you may notice changes made by an Unknown user. Generally, these changes are made from the HubSpot system.

  • To review what the workflow looked like at a specific revision, hover over the revision, then click View.

  • On the workflow revision screen, review your selected version of the workflow. The workflow cannot be edited from the workflow revision screen.

    • To review additional details about the workflow, you can click the enrollment triggers and action boxes.
    • To review the workflow’s settings at the time of the revision, in the top left, click Settings. The workflow settings at the time of the revision will appear in the right panel.

  • To revert to a specific version of the workflow, hover over the revision, then click Revert.

    • The selected revision will appear in the editor, and can be further updated.
    • If your workflow is currently turned on, the reverted version will automatically begin executing. To prevent this, you can turn off your workflow, revert to the desired workflow version, then turn your workflow on again.

Please note: reverts are not supported for webhook and custom code actions. If a workflow’s revision contains a webhook or a custom code action, you will not be able to revert your workflow’s changes. In this instance, it is recommended to use the read-only revision as a reference to manually update the current workflow.

View workflow connections

When you reference a workflow in another HubSpot asset, such as a list or another workflow, you can view those connections from the workflows dashboard and the workflow review page. You can also view any assets that the workflow uses, such as lists and properties.

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to use the workflows tool.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Hover over a workflow, then click Actions and select Edit workflow.
  • At the top of the workflow editor, click the Connections tab.
  • In the right panel, review the asset types that the workflow is using. To review the specific asset, click to expand the [asset type] section.

Workflows | Frequently Asked Questions

Find answers and general information about the workflows tool in HubSpot.

Permissions required Super Admin or Workflows permissions are required to use the workflows tool.

General

How do I troubleshoot workflow errors?

If you’re encountering errors when reviewing your workflow history, or if your workflow isn’t working as expected, learn more about common workflow errors and the steps you can take to resolve these issues.

Can I set a workflow to automatically turn off?

Yes, you can schedule a workflow to turn off automatically after a specified date and time in your workflow settings. Learn more about automatically turning off a workflow.

Can I pause my workflow?

While there isn’t a general pause button for your workflow, you can set up pause dates so that actions don’t execute on specific days. On pause dates, actions will reschedule to the next available day. This is especially useful for managing campaigns that overlap with holidays and other sensitive dates.

Learn more about setting up pause dates.

What happens when a record is deleted?

Deleted records are automatically unenrolled from workflows. Even if the record is deleted then restored while in a delay, the restored record will not resume and continue the workflow.

To add previously deleted records back to a workflow, ensure that re-enrollment is enabled, then manually enroll the record.

Why was my action skipped because of an “infinite loop”?

When reviewing your workflow history, you may see that an action was skipped to prevent an infinite loop: The enrolled deal was created by this workflow, so this action was skipped to prevent an infinite loop.

This indicates that your workflow has an action to create a record that also meets the enrollment criteria for the same workflow:

  • If the record was created, it would enroll into the same workflow.
  • This would lead to the same Create record action that creates a new record.
  • The new record would enroll into the same workflow as well.
  • This would result in an “infinite loop” and the workflow continuously and endlessly creating records.

HubSpot prevents this action from occurring so that the workflow will not create records indefinitely. When you encounter such an error, review your workflow to ensure that new records created do not meet the enrollment criteria of the workflow.

How many workflows can I create?

The number of workflows you can create depend on your HubSpot subscriptions:

  • If you have a Marketing, Sales, or Service Hub Professional subscription, you can create up to 300 workflows.
  • If you have a Marketing, Sales, or Service Hub Enterprise subscription, you can create up to 1000 workflows.
  • If you have an Data Hub Professional subscription, you can create up to 400 workflows.
  • If you have an Data Hub Enterprise subscription, you can create up to 1100 workflows.
  • If you have the Brands add-on, you can create an additional 100 workflows.

If you have multiple subscriptions, your limit will be determined by the subscription with the highest workflow limit. For example, if your account has a Marketing Hub Professional and a Sales Hub Enterprise subscription, you’d be able to create up to 1000 workflows.

Which workflows count towards my HubSpot account limits?

Only customized workflows created from the workflows tool will count toward your account limits. Embedded workflow tools with preset triggers do not count toward your workflow limits. This includes the following:

  • Simple workflows created from the ads tool, marketing email tool, and forms tool.
  • Automation from CRM settings such as deal pipeline settings or ticket pipeline settings.
  • Automation from other tools such as sequences, forecasts, quotes, surveys, etc.
How long is workflow data stored?

HubSpot will store workflow data within the below time periods:

  • 90 days: all workflow action log data will be stored. This includes high-level action log data such as object ID (which contact, company, deal, etc.), event type (enrollment, unenrollment, etc.), and action type will be stored.
  • 6 months: historical data of enrollments will be retained in our system to enable workflow-based filters.
What are the limits for workflow action and enrollment logs?

When reviewing your workflow history, there is a 100,000 log limit for successful workflow executions per day.

  • This is calculated from midnight in the account’s time zone.
  • Once the limit is exceeded, success and info logs will not be stored for the rest of the day, but error logs will continue to appear.

Credits

Which workflow features use credits?

The following workflow enrollment triggers and actions will use HubSpot credits. Learn how to understand HubSpot credits and billing.

  • Currently all AI-related actions and triggers in workflows will consume credits. Please refer to the table below. Learn more about using AI actions in workflows.
  • Any workflows that include AI-related actions, if triggered from the workflows CRM card, will still consume credits
  • Automated enrollment from the Prospecting agent will consume credits.

Triggers

Actions

  • Enrolling companies from saved views in buyer intent.

  • Enrolling companies from a dataset on a schedule.

  • AI actions including:

    • Summarize record (BETA)
    • Infer company value proposition and ICP (BETA)
    • Use a custom LLM (BETA)

  • Data Agent actions including:

    • Data Agent: Custom prompt (BETA)
    • Data Agent: Research (BETA)
    • Data Agent: Fill Smart Property (BETA)

  • Enroll in Prospecting agent from Ruleset.

  • Prospecting agent actions (Sales Hub Professional and Enterprise only):

    • Enroll in prospecting agent (BETA)
    • Unenroll in prospecting agent (BETA)

  • Intent signal actions including:

    • Track intent signals
    • Stop tracking intent signals
How to control permissions for credit use in workflows

To determine which users have access to manage credit use from certain workflow actions or triggers, you’ll need to manage access to the associated feature:

  • Enrollment triggers and actions associated with Prospecting agent require Prospecting Agent admin permissions.
  • Workflow actions associated with Data agent require Data Agent access permissions.
  • Enrollment triggers and actions associated buyer intent and intent signals require Data Enrichment access permissions and edit Buyer Intent permission.

Enrollment triggers

Why didn’t my record enroll in the workflow?

There are a number of reasons why a record may meet the workflow’s enrollment criteria, but not enroll into the workflow. For example, if a contact record is included in the workflow’s suppression list, if the record was previously enrolled in the workflow but re-enrollment isn’t turned on, and more.

Learn more about troubleshooting your workflow enrollment.

What are the different workflow enrollment trigger types?

There are three types of enrollment triggers that you can use for different scenarios:

  • When an event occurs: records will enroll when an event has happened. For example, when a form has been submitted. When using event enrollment triggers, the record must be created before the event occurs. It is not possible to enroll existing records that meet the event criteria, only records that meet the event criteria after the workflow is turned on will be enrolled. Learn more about event triggers.
  • When filter criteria is met: records will enroll when a criteria is true. For example, when a contact’s whose city is equal to Dublin, do [X] action. When using filter criteria, you can choose to enroll only new contacts that meet the criteria after the workflow has been turned on, or both new and existing contacts that meet the filter criteria.
  • Based on a schedule: records will enroll based on on a specified calendar date or by using a date property. To enroll automatically, you must add additional filter criteria. Learn more about using Based on a schedule enrollment triggers.
Why aren’t previously enrolled records that meet a workflow’s enrollment triggers again being re-enrolled in the workflow?

By default, records are only enrolled in a workflow the first time they meet the workflow’s enrollment triggers or are enrolled manually. Learn how to add re-enrollment triggers to allow records to be re-enrolled in a workflow.

If a record is already active in a workflow, it cannot be enrolled again in the same workflow until it completes the workflow. Attempts to re-enroll the record will fail with an Already enrolled error. Records will only re-enroll only after completing the workflow and meeting the re-enrollment trigger again.

What happens when I edit an active segment used in a workflow’s enrollment triggers? (Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise only)

When you edit the filters in an active segment used in an active workflow’s enrollment triggers, then try to save the segment, a dialog box will appear for you to choose if existing contacts that meet the newly updated criteria should be enrolled in the workflow.

How many enrollment triggers can I add to a workflow?

You can add up to 250 enrollment triggers to a workflow. If your workflow requires more enrollment triggers, create multiple workflows instead.

Why do I receive an error when saving my number property as an enrollment trigger?

If you’re using a number property for your enrollment trigger in a contact-based workflow, you can only use whole numbers.

If a value with a decimal is used, an error will display and the enrollment trigger will not be saved. This applies to both formatted and unformatted number properties. For example, you cannot set Employees is any of 0.98.

Why is the number of contacts shown when I review my workflow different to the number of contacts in my segment?

If you have a Marketing Hub Starter, Professional, or Enterprise account, in contact-based workflows, the number of contacts displayed on the review page is an estimate and not an exact measure of the number of contacts.

To view the exact number of records, when publishing your workflow, click See all contacts in lists (segments).

Why has an [object] enrolled in my workflow even though I selected No, only enroll objects which meet the trigger criteria after turning the workflow on?

When this option is turned on, objects will be enrolled if they did not meet the enrollment criteria before and change to meet the enrollment triggers for the first time after the workflow is turned on or if they change to meet the enrollment criteria again and re-enrollment is turned on. Objects that already met the criteria at that time are excluded. Newly created contacts are still checked and can enroll if they meet the criteria. Learn more about re-enrollment triggers.

Actions

Why are my workflow actions not executing at the expected time?

When a large number of records enroll in a workflow or execute an action at the same time, the workflow may be throttled. When a workflow is throttled, actions will not execute immediately, but in a queue as records are processed. Heavy simultaneous processing can cause actions or property changes to take time to process.

In Specific date or Contact date property contact-based workflows, this may cause contacts to miss the first action if it’s scheduled shortly after they’re enrolled in the workflow. To avoid this, you can enroll your contacts in advance, or schedule the first action at a later time relative to the date or date property.

Large bulk enrollments can also delay pending actions in other workflows in the same account as well. To reduce these delays, split bulk enrollments into different batches and stagger each batch by 10 minutes.

What happens to enrolled records when I add more workflow actions?

Adding actions to an active workflow can impact records that are enrolled and active in the workflow:

  • Any records that haven’t yet made it to the new action will be scheduled for it when they reach that action.
  • Any records that have already proceeded past that point will not complete the new action.

For example, in a workflow with two actions, when a new action is added between the first action and second action:

  • The contact Pablo the Cat is currently scheduled for the first action. Because the new action comes after the action they’re scheduled for, they’ll then be scheduled for the new action after they execute the first action.
  • The contact Tito the Cat is scheduled for the original second action (now third action). Because the contact has already proceeded past the point where the new action was added, they will not be scheduled for the new action.
What happens to enrolled records when I remove workflow actions?

Removing actions from an active workflow will affect records currently scheduled for that action. When you remove an action that has scheduled records, the records will not execute that action. The records will proceed to the next step of the workflow and continue in the workflow.

For example, if the action is scheduled to only execute on weekdays, the record will not move to the next stage until it is a weekday or until the scheduled time has passed. An error will also appear for that action in the workflow history.

When records are scheduled for an action, the action will show a count of those records, such as 1 contact in action.

Why is the rotate leads action in my workflow delayed for 10 minutes for new contacts?

If the Assign company owner to contact by default setting is enabled, the following error will display when you add a Rotate leads action to a contact-based workflow: New contacts will take about 10 minutes to be processed because the contact and company owner sync is enabled.

When a new HubSpot contact is created, and ownership is synced between contacts and companies, it may take some time for the contact to be associated with a company, and then for the company’s owner to sync to the contact. As a result, new contacts will be delayed for 10 minutes before executing the Rotate leads action, to allow sufficient time for the contact-company association to take place and ownership to sync.

Why can’t I send my marketing email in a workflow? (Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise only)

Only marketing emails that have been saved for automation can be sent in workflows. If a marketing email is a draft or has been previously sent to a segment of recipients, it will not appear for selection in the Send email action.

What happens if multiple workflows update the same property?

If multiple workflows update the same property for a specific CRM record, a later workflow action can overwrite, remove, or clear a value set by an earlier workflow.

To troubleshoot overwritten property values, you can review the record’s property history. Then, turn off or update any workflow that is overwriting or clearing the value.

Delays

What happens to records waiting in a workflow delay when the delay is deleted?

When you delete a delay, records waiting in the delay will immediately skip the delay, then proceed through the rest of the workflow.

Learn more about editing workflow delays.

What happens to records waiting in a workflow delay when the delay timing is changed?

When you change the length of a delay, the records waiting at the delay will immediately be rescheduled. Rescheduling accounts for the time that has already passed in the original delay. Learn more about editing workflow delays.

  • If you make a delay longer:
    • Delayed records will be rescheduled to complete the remainder of the new delay length.
    • For example, if you adjust a delay from one hour to two hours, records that have already waited 30 minutes will wait for an additional hour and 30 minutes.
  • If you make a delay shorter:
    • Records will either be rescheduled to the new length or exit the delay.
    • For example, if you adjust a delay from two hours to one hour, a record that’s waited for 30 minutes will wait for an additional 30 minutes. A record that’s waited an hour and 30 minutes will exit the delay immediately.

Data: Data Management

Access your HubSpot data from Amazon Redshift

Use Data Out for Amazon Redshift to export selected HubSpot CRM data to tables in an Amazon Redshift database that you own. Each sync run writes a full snapshot of the selected data and replaces the previous snapshot. After the sync, you can query the tables with SQL or with your preferred BI and analytics tools to combine HubSpot data with other business data.

Please note: if you’re a Super Admin, opt your account into the Data Studio beta to use this feature.

HubSpot Credits required for certain features syncing data directly from a single warehouse source in Data Studio to the HubSpot CRM doesn’t consume HubSpot Credits. If you prepare the data in Data Studio before syncing (for example, by creating calculated fields or joining it with other data sources), those actions consume HubSpot Credits.

Understand limitations & considerations

Before you begin working with this feature, make sure to fully understand what steps should be taken ahead of time, as well as the limitations of the feature and potential consequences of using it.

  • Each sync replaces the destination tables with the latest snapshot. HubSpot doesn’t keep previous snapshots in Redshift.
  • HubSpot doesn’t delete the Parquet files it stages in your S3 bucket. To remove them automatically, set up an S3 lifecycle policy on the bucket or prefix.
  • Each object, event type, or association pair can be included in one recurring Redshift Data Out sync per HubSpot account.
  • Sensitive data isn’t supported yet. Sensitive properties may be excluded from exports.
  • Object-specific tables, such as OBJECTS_CONTACTS, aren’t supported yet.

Understand the data you can export

You can sync the following data from HubSpot to Amazon Redshift:

  • Objects: standard and custom objects, such as contacts, companies, deals, tickets, and products.
  • Records: individual records for the selected objects.
  • Properties: selected property values and property history on records.
  • Associations: selected relationships between records, including association definitions.
  • Events: selected standard HubSpot events and custom behavioral events, including selected event properties.

Data for different objects is combined in the object tables. When you read an object table, use OBJECTTYPEID to filter to a specific object. For example, contacts use 0-1. Custom objects are assigned an ID when they’re created and are identified as 2-{unique_id}, such as 2-12345.

Understand the export format

During setup, you choose:

  • The Redshift database and the cluster or Serverless workgroup where HubSpot will create tables.
  • The S3 bucket HubSpot uses to stage data before loading it into Redshift.
  • The data sources to sync: objects, events, associations, or a combination of these sources.
  • The sync schedule.

HubSpot exports the data as Parquet files, stages the files in your S3 bucket, and loads them into Redshift tables.

Please note: HubSpot doesn’t delete data from the staging bucket. It’s recommended to set a bucket lifecycle policy to automatically clean up the bucket.

Find your data in Redshift

HubSpot creates one table per data source in a HubSpot-managed schema named after your destination:

&lt;database>.hubspot_data_out_&lt;destination-id>.&lt;table-name>

You can find the schema name on the configuration page of your Redshift sync. For example:

  • your_database.hubspot_data_out_456.OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES
  • your_database.hubspot_data_out_456.EVENTS_VISITED_PAGE
  • your_database.hubspot_data_out_456.ASSOCIATIONS_CONTACTS_TO_COMPANIES

Each sync replaces the table with the latest snapshot. If a table fails during a sync, its previous data stays in place until the next successful sync.

HubSpot stages Parquet files in your S3 bucket under a HubSpot-managed prefix, then loads them into Redshift:

s3://&lt;bucket>/&lt;prefix>/hubspot-dataout/&lt;portal-id>/&lt;destination-id>/&lt;run-id>/&lt;table-name>/

These staging files stay in your bucket until you remove them. To remove them automatically, configure an S3 lifecycle policy on the bucket or prefix.

Please note: table and column names come from the exported data. They may be shortened to meet Redshift’s 127-character identifier limit. Column types follow the exported data.

Manage the sync schedule

You configure the sync schedule during setup in HubSpot. You can also manually trigger a re-sync from HubSpot. Each sync run produces a full snapshot of the selected data. To control data volume, choose which objects, events, associations, and properties to include.

Please note: during the beta, only a limited set of sync frequencies may be available, such as once, every 6 hours, every 12 hours, daily, weekly, and monthly. Additional frequency options may be added in future releases.

Monitor syncs and handle errors

You can monitor Amazon Redshift syncs in HubSpot. A sync can have one of the following states:

State

Meaning

Syncing

A sync run is currently in progress.

Synced

The last sync completed successfully.

Failed

The last sync run encountered an error.

Archived

The sync configuration was archived or removed.

When a sync fails:

  • HubSpot shows a Failed status with per-table details showing which tables succeeded or failed.
  • A table is updated only after HubSpot finishes loading all of its data, so you never see a partially loaded table.
  • If a table fails, its previous data stays in place until the next successful sync.
  • The next scheduled sync automatically reattempts a full sync.
  • You can manually trigger a re-sync at any time in HubSpot.

Tables that succeeded in a previous run aren’t modified when a later run fails.

FAQs

How do I query the data?

Query the tables in your destination schema with SQL. For example:

Read all contact records:

SELECT * FROM your_database.hubspot_data_out_456.OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES WHERE OBJECTTYPEID = '0-1';

Read a specific property from the PROPERTIES JSON column:

SELECT OBJECTID, JSON_EXTRACT_PATH_TEXT(PROPERTIES, 'email') AS email FROM your_database.hubspot_data_out_456.OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES WHERE OBJECTTYPEID = '0-1';
Can I export one data type in multiple Redshift syncs?

Each object, event type, or association pair can be included in one recurring Redshift Data Out sync per HubSpot account. For example, if contacts are already exported to one recurring Redshift destination, you can’t add contacts to another recurring Redshift sync until you archive the first sync.

Are object-specific tables supported?

No. Object-specific tables, such as OBJECTS_CONTACTS, aren’t supported yet. Use OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES and filter by OBJECTTYPEID to get records for a specific object.

Is sensitive data supported?

No. Sensitive data isn’t supported for Data Out to Redshift yet. Sensitive properties may be excluded from exports.

Does HubSpot keep previous snapshots?

No. Each sync replaces the destination table with the latest snapshot, so previous snapshots aren’t kept in Redshift. HubSpot also doesn’t delete the temporary Parquet files it stages in your S3 bucket. Configure an S3 lifecycle policy to expire them automatically.

Access your HubSpot data from Microsoft Azure Synapse Analytics

Use Data Out for Azure Synapse to export selected HubSpot CRM data to tables in an Azure Synapse dedicated SQL pool that you own. HubSpot refreshes each output table from a full export of the selected data. After the sync, you can query the tables with SQL or with your preferred BI and analytics tools to combine HubSpot data with other business data.

Please note: if you’re a Super Admin, opt your account into the Data Studio beta to use this feature.

HubSpot Credits required for certain features syncing data directly from a single warehouse source in Data Studio to the HubSpot CRM doesn’t consume HubSpot Credits. If you prepare the data in Data Studio before syncing (for example, by creating calculated fields or joining it with other data sources), those actions consume HubSpot Credits.

Understand limitations & considerations

Before you begin working with this feature, make sure to fully understand what steps should be taken ahead of time, as well as the limitations of the feature and potential consequences of using it.

  • HubSpot updates tables separately. If you query across multiple tables while a sync is running, some tables may update before others.
  • Data Out doesn’t provide historical snapshot retention. After a successful refresh, the destination table contains the latest snapshot.
  • Each object, event type, or association pair can be included in one recurring Azure Synapse sync per HubSpot account. This limit is independent of other Data Out providers.
  • Object-specific tables, such as OBJECTS_CONTACTS, aren’t supported yet.
  • If two table names collide after HubSpot normalizes them, the affected export fails. For more information, review the table and column name rules.

Understand the data you can export

You can sync the following data from HubSpot to Azure Synapse Analytics:

  • Objects and records: selected standard and custom objects and their records, such as contacts, companies, deals, tickets, and products.
  • Properties: selected property values and property history on records.
  • Associations: selected relationships between records, including association definitions.
  • Events: selected standard HubSpot events and custom behavioral events, including selected event properties.

Data for different objects is combined in the object tables. When you read an object table, use OBJECTTYPEID to filter to a specific object. For example, contacts use 0-1. Custom objects are assigned an ID when they’re created and are identified as 2-{unique_id}, such as 2-12345.

Understand the export format

During setup, you choose:

  • The destination Azure Synapse dedicated SQL endpoint and database.
  • The data sources to sync: objects, events, associations, or a combination of these sources.
  • The sync schedule.

HubSpot creates a temporary Parquet export in HubSpot-managed storage and writes the results to tables in your Azure Synapse dedicated SQL pool. You don’t need to provide or manage a staging bucket.

Find your data in Azure Synapse

HubSpot creates output tables in a HubSpot-managed schema for your destination. HubSpot exports object data to the three object tables described in this article. HubSpot also creates one table per selected event type and, when available, one pair-specific table per selected association pair.

&lt;database>.hubspot_data_out_&lt;destination-id>.&lt;table-name>

You can find the exact schema name on the configuration page of your sync. For example:

  • your_database.hubspot_data_out_456.OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES
  • your_database.hubspot_data_out_456.EVENTS_VISITED_PAGE
  • your_database.hubspot_data_out_456.ASSOCIATIONS_CONTACTS_TO_COMPANIES
Table and column names

HubSpot normalizes exported table and column names to uppercase letters, numbers, and underscores:

  • Spaces and hyphens become underscores.
  • Other non-alphanumeric characters are removed.
  • Names longer than 128 characters are shortened.
  • Colliding column names receive a suffix.
  • Colliding table names fail the affected export.

Use square brackets when you query identifiers, especially if you construct queries dynamically. Identifier case sensitivity depends on your Synapse database collation. For example:

SELECT *
FROM [your_database].[hubspot_data_out_456].[OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES]
WHERE [OBJECTTYPEID] = '0-1';

Query the tables in your destination schema with SQL. For example, read all contact records:

SELECT *
FROM [your_database].[hubspot_data_out_456].[OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES]
WHERE [OBJECTTYPEID] = '0-1';

Read a specific property from the PROPERTIES JSON string:

SELECT
  [OBJECTID],
  JSON_VALUE([PROPERTIES], '$.email') AS [email]
FROM [your_database].[hubspot_data_out_456].[OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES]
WHERE [OBJECTTYPEID] = '0-1';
Can I export one data type in multiple syncs?

Each object, event type, or association pair can be included in one recurring Azure Synapse sync per HubSpot account. This limit is independent of other Data Out providers.

For example, if contacts are already exported to a recurring Azure Synapse destination, you can’t add contacts to another recurring Azure Synapse sync until you archive the first sync. You can still export contacts to another supported Data Out provider at the same time.

Are object-specific tables supported?

No. Object-specific tables, such as OBJECTS_CONTACTS, aren’t supported yet. Use OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES and filter by OBJECTTYPEID to get records for a specific object.

Does HubSpot keep previous snapshots?

No. Data Out doesn’t provide historical snapshot retention. After a successful refresh, the destination table contains the latest snapshot. If a table can’t be updated, the previous successful data usually remains available.

Access your HubSpot data from Microsoft Fabric

Use Data Out to export selected HubSpot CRM data to native tables in a Microsoft Fabric Warehouse that you own. You can sync object, association, and event data to tables in your warehouse, then query that data with SQL or use it with your business intelligence and analytics tools. Each sync creates a full snapshot of the selected data. When a sync succeeds, it replaces the previous snapshot in the destination tables.

Please note: if you’re a Super Admin, opt your account into the Data Studio beta to use this feature.

HubSpot Credits required for certain features syncing data directly from a single warehouse source in Data Studio to the HubSpot CRM doesn’t consume HubSpot Credits. If you prepare the data in Data Studio before syncing (for example, by creating calculated fields or joining it with other data sources), those actions consume HubSpot Credits.

Understand the data you can export

You can sync the following data from HubSpot to Microsoft Fabric:

  • Objects and records: selected standard and custom objects and their records, such as contacts, companies, deals, tickets, and products.
  • Properties: selected property values and property history on records.
  • Associations: selected relationships between records, including association definitions.
  • Events: selected standard HubSpot events and custom behavioral events, including selected event properties.

Data for different objects is combined in the object tables. When you read an object table, use OBJECTTYPEID to filter to a specific object. For example, contacts use 0-1. Custom objects are assigned an ID when they’re created and are identified as 2-{unique_id}, such as 2-12345.

Understand the export format

During setup, you choose:

  • The destination Fabric workspace SQL connection string and database (Warehouse).
  • The data sources to sync: objects, events, associations, or a combination of these sources.
  • The sync schedule.

HubSpot creates a temporary Parquet export in HubSpot-managed storage and writes the results to tables in your Fabric Warehouse. You don’t need to provide or manage a staging bucket.

Find your data in Microsoft Fabric

HubSpot creates output tables in a HubSpot-managed schema for your destination. HubSpot exports object data to the three object tables described in this article. HubSpot also creates one table per selected event type and, when available, one pair-specific table per selected association pair.

<database>.hubspot_data_out_<destination-id>.<table-name>

For example:

your_database.hubspot_data_out_456.OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES

your_database.hubspot_data_out_456.EVENTS_VISITED_PAGE

your_database.hubspot_data_out_456.ASSOCIATIONS_CONTACTS_TO_COMPANIES

You can find the exact schema name on the sync configuration page.

Table and column names

HubSpot normalizes exported table and column names to uppercase letters, numbers, and underscores:

  • Spaces and hyphens become underscores.
  • Other non-alphanumeric characters are removed.
  • Names longer than 128 characters are shortened.
  • Colliding column names receive a suffix.
  • Colliding table names fail the affected export.

For example:

SELECT * FROM [your_database].[hubspot_data_out_456].[OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES] WHERE [OBJECTTYPEID] = '0-1';

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I query the exported data?

Query the tables in the destination schema with SQL.

-- Read all contact records
SELECT *
FROM [your_database].[hubspot_data_out_456].[OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES]
WHERE [OBJECTTYPEID] = '0-1'; -- Read a specific property from the PROPERTIES JSON string
SELECT
  [OBJECTID],
  JSON_VALUE([PROPERTIES], '$.email') AS [email]
FROM [your_database].[hubspot_data_out_456].[OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES]
WHERE [OBJECTTYPEID] = '0-1';
Can I export one data type in multiple syncs?

Each object type, event type, or association pair can be included in one recurring Microsoft Fabric sync per HubSpot account. This is independent of other Data Out providers.

For example, if contacts are already exported to a recurring Fabric destination, you can’t add contacts to another recurring Fabric configuration until you archive the first configuration. You can still export contacts to another supported Data Out provider at the same time.

Are object-specific tables supported?

Object-specific tables, such as OBJECTS_CONTACTS, aren’t currently supported. Use OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES and filter by OBJECTTYPEID to retrieve records for a specific object type.

Does HubSpot keep previous snapshots?

No. Each successful sync replaces the destination table with the latest snapshot. HubSpot doesn’t retain previous snapshots. If a table fails during a sync, its previous data remains in place until that table is successfully updated.

Access your HubSpot data from PostgreSQL or MySQL

Use Data Out for PostgreSQL and MySQL to export selected HubSpot CRM data to tables in a database that you own. Each sync run writes a full snapshot of the selected data and replaces the previous snapshot. After the sync, you can query the tables with SQL or with your preferred BI and analytics tools to combine HubSpot data with other business data.

Please note: if you’re a Super Admin, opt your account into the Data Studio beta to use this feature.

HubSpot Credits required for certain features syncing data directly from a single warehouse source in Data Studio to the HubSpot CRM doesn’t consume HubSpot Credits. If you prepare the data in Data Studio before syncing (for example, by creating calculated fields or joining it with other data sources), those actions consume HubSpot Credits.

Understand limitations & considerations

Before you begin working with this feature, make sure to fully understand what steps should be taken ahead of time, as well as the limitations of the feature and potential consequences of using it.

  • Each sync replaces the destination tables with the latest snapshot. HubSpot doesn’t keep previous snapshots.
  • Each object, event type, or association pair can be included in one recurring PostgreSQL sync and one recurring MySQL sync per HubSpot account. These syncs are independent of each other and of other Data Out providers.
  • Sensitive data isn’t supported yet. Sensitive properties may be excluded from exports.
  • Object-specific tables, such as OBJECTS_CONTACTS, aren’t supported yet.
  • Table and column names are case-sensitive in PostgreSQL and may be case-sensitive in MySQL. Review the query syntax before you write queries.

Understand the data you can export

You can sync the following data from HubSpot to PostgreSQL or MySQL:

  • Objects: standard and custom objects, such as contacts, companies, deals, tickets, and products.
  • Records: individual records for the selected objects.
  • Properties: selected property values and property history on records.
  • Associations: selected relationships between records, including association definitions.
  • Events: selected standard HubSpot events and custom behavioral events, including selected event properties.

Data for different objects is combined in the object tables. When you read an object table, use OBJECTTYPEID to filter to a specific object. For example, contacts use 0-1. Custom objects are assigned an ID when they’re created and are identified as 2-{unique_id}, such as 2-12345.

Understand the export format

During setup, you choose:

  • The destination database. This applies to PostgreSQL only. For MySQL, HubSpot creates the database.
  • The data sources to sync: objects, events, associations, or a combination of these sources.
  • The sync schedule.

HubSpot exports the data as Parquet files and loads it directly into tables in your database. PostgreSQL and MySQL don’t use a customer-owned staging bucket. HubSpot manages staging internally.

Find your data in your database

HubSpot creates one table per data source in a HubSpot-managed schema named after your destination. You can find the exact schema name on the configuration page of your sync.

  • PostgreSQL: &lt;database>.hubspot_data_out_&lt;destination-id>.&lt;table-name>
  • MySQL: hubspot_data_out_&lt;destination-id>.&lt;table-name>. In MySQL, schema and database are the same concept, and HubSpot creates it. There’s no separate database level to choose.

For example, in PostgreSQL:

  • your_database.hubspot_data_out_456.OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES
  • your_database.hubspot_data_out_456.EVENTS_VISITED_PAGE
  • your_database.hubspot_data_out_456.ASSOCIATIONS_CONTACTS_TO_COMPANIES

For example, in MySQL:

  • hubspot_data_out_456.OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES
  • hubspot_data_out_456.EVENTS_VISITED_PAGE
  • hubspot_data_out_456.ASSOCIATIONS_CONTACTS_TO_COMPANIES

Each sync replaces the table with the latest snapshot. HubSpot doesn’t keep previous snapshots. If a table fails during a sync, its previous data stays in place until the next successful sync.

Table and column names

Table and column names come from the exported data. PostgreSQL identifiers are limited to 63 characters, and MySQL identifiers are limited to 64 characters. HubSpot shortens longer names to fit.

Identifier case

Identifier case matters. HubSpot creates all tables and columns with quoted, case-preserved names in uppercase, matching the tables in this article.

  • PostgreSQL: wrap names in double quotes exactly as shown. PostgreSQL folds unquoted names to lowercase, so they won’t match.
  • MySQL: use backticks and match the case shown. Table name case sensitivity depends on your server configuration.

PostgreSQL example:

SELECT * FROM your_database.hubspot_data_out_456."OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES" WHERE "OBJECTTYPEID" = '0-1';

MySQL example:

SELECT * FROM `hubspot_data_out_456`.`OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES` WHERE `OBJECTTYPEID` = '0-1';
