Manage the sync schedule

You configure the sync schedule during setup in HubSpot. You can also manually trigger a re-sync from HubSpot. Each sync run produces a full snapshot of the selected data. To control data volume, choose which objects, events, associations, and properties to include.

Please note: during the beta, only a limited set of sync frequencies may be available, such as once, every 6 hours, every 12 hours, daily, weekly, and monthly. Additional frequency options may be added in future releases.

Monitor syncs and handle errors

You can monitor PostgreSQL and MySQL syncs in HubSpot. A sync can have one of the following states:

State

Meaning

Syncing

A sync run is currently in progress.

Synced

The last sync completed successfully.

Failed

The last sync run encountered an error.

Archived

The sync configuration was archived or removed.

When a sync fails:

  • HubSpot shows a Failed status with per-table details showing which tables succeeded or failed.
  • A table is updated only after HubSpot finishes loading all of its data, so you never see a partially loaded table.
  • If a table fails, its previous data stays in place until the next successful sync.
  • The next scheduled sync automatically reattempts a full sync.
  • You can manually trigger a re-sync at any time in HubSpot.

Tables that succeeded in a previous run aren’t modified when a later run fails.

FAQs

How do I query the data?

Query the tables in your destination schema with SQL.

PostgreSQL

Read all contact records:

SELECT * FROM your_database.hubspot_data_out_456."OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES" WHERE "OBJECTTYPEID" = '0-1';

Read a specific property from the PROPERTIES JSON column. Cast the column to JSON first, because it’s stored as text:

SELECT "OBJECTID", json_extract_path_text("PROPERTIES"::json, 'email') AS email FROM your_database.hubspot_data_out_456."OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES" WHERE "OBJECTTYPEID" = '0-1';

MySQL

Read all contact records:

SELECT * FROM `hubspot_data_out_456`.`OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES` WHERE `OBJECTTYPEID` = '0-1';

Read a specific property from the PROPERTIES JSON column:

SELECT `OBJECTID`, JSON_EXTRACT(`PROPERTIES`, '$.email') AS email FROM `hubspot_data_out_456`.`OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES` WHERE `OBJECTTYPEID` = '0-1';
Can I export one data type in multiple syncs?

Each object, event type, or association pair can be included in one recurring PostgreSQL sync and one recurring MySQL sync per HubSpot account. These syncs are independent of each other and of other Data Out providers. For example, if contacts are already exported to a recurring PostgreSQL destination, you can’t add contacts to another recurring PostgreSQL sync until you archive the first sync. You can still export contacts to a recurring MySQL sync at the same time.

Are object-specific tables supported?

No. Object-specific tables, such as OBJECTS_CONTACTS, aren’t supported yet. Use OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES and filter by OBJECTTYPEID to get records for a specific object.

Is sensitive data supported?

No. Sensitive data isn’t supported for Data Out yet. Sensitive properties may be excluded from exports.

Does HubSpot keep previous snapshots?

No. Each sync replaces the destination table with the latest snapshot, so previous snapshots aren’t kept.

Build and activate datasets in Data Studio

Please note: if you’re a Super Admin, learn how to opt your account into the beta.

Summary

HubSpot Data Studio consolidates external customer data to provide a unified platform for synchronization, integration, and activation across your technology stack. Users can build datasets from external sources like Google Sheets, Snowflake, and data sync apps, then integrate them into lists, workflows, and reports for efficient, data-driven decision-making.

Before you get started

  • In order to view, edit, and use datasets, you must have Data Studio permissions.
  • View and Edit permissions are turned on by default. Super Admin must turn on Use permissions for dataset users to let them use HubSpot Credits for Data Studio.
  • Use permissions are only required when using a dataset in a workflow, segment, syncing to the CRM, or exporting.
  • You can receive Data Studio sync notifications to stay updated on their status, allowing you to quickly take action if errors or unexpected failures occur, and ensuring the continued quality of data being updated in the CRM on a recurring schedule. Learn how to set up notifications.
  • Learn more about subscription limitations in HubSpot’s Product & Services catalog.

What is a dataset?

A dataset is a collection of data from across your HubSpot account that can consist of HubSpot and/or external data sources. A dataset can include properties for CRM objects and HubSpot assets, fields from external data sources, and formulas to calculate your data.

Learn more about dataset definitions in the Glossary.

Use cases for Data Studio

Below are key use cases demonstrating how you can leverage external datasets to enhance CRM records, optimize workflows, create dynamic customer lists, and use datasets to build reports.

Sync data from third-party applications

You can sync datasets from third-party applications directly to your HubSpot CRM. This allows you to:

  • Update CRM records using external datasets
  • Generate new properties from calculated formula fields
  • Instantly write data to your CRM with one click

For example, you could blend data from a product usage platform (e.g. Mixpanel) with company datasets to create a powerful Product engagement score property in HubSpot.

Learn how to sync data from third-party applications.

Sync data to HubSpot’s CRM

You can sync data to HubSpot’s CRM to:

  • Improve your audience segmentation
  • Send more personalized marketing emails
  • Improve your sales outreach based on learnings derived from data

For example, you could create a dataset that tracks customer behavior across different channels. By syncing this data back to the CRM, you can refine audience segmentation to identify high-intent leads. Using these insights, you can send personalized email campaigns tailored to customer preferences, boosting engagement and conversion rates.

Learn how to sync data to HubSpot’s CRM.

Use your dataset in a workflow

You can use your datasets in a workflow to:

  • Build one-time or recurring workflows for primary dataset records
  • Incorporate dataset fields into workflow actions

For example, leverage the engagement score dataset to build a workflow that automates customer alerts for potential upgrades or churn risks. This workflow can also proactively reach out to customers who may be a strong fit for an upgrade.

Learn how to use datasets in a workflow.

Use your dataset to create segments

You can use your datasets to create segments to:

  • Import and merge product usage, lead scores, and customer data into Data Studio
  • Combine HubSpot contact data with external sources, refining insights with filters
  • Generate a filtered list of dataset contacts that meet specific criteria

For example, leverage a targeted customer data dataset to generate a dynamic segment that drives an automated marketing campaign, delivering personalized customer experiences at scale.

Learn how to use your datasets to create segments.

Use your dataset in a report

You can use your datasets in a report to:

  • Combine multiple data sources to create unified reports with information from your CRM, external applications, and analytics platforms
  • Segment data dynamically by applying filters to focus on specific groups, behaviors, or trends
  • Build custom metrics and calculations using formula fields to generate unique performance indicators.

For example, you could create a field to calculate annual recurring revenue based on the deal amount property, and then use this data from the dataset in a report to track revenue trends, forecast future earnings, and analyze customer retention over time.

Please note: if your dataset uses HubSpot objects and includes summarized measures and custom formulas, any filters you apply to those measures will affect only the summarized view of the data, not the underlying report.

Learn how to use your datasets in a report.

Export datasets to Google Sheets and Office 365 Excel

You can export datasets to Google Sheets and Office 365 Excel to:

  • Maintain external copies for archival purposes or additional security.
  • Work with your data even without an internet connection.
  • Share datasets easily with team members for real-time edits and feedback.

For example, exporting HubSpot datasets to Google Sheets or Office 365 Excel allows businesses to refine data for clear insights into revenue trends and customer acquisition, then securely share it with external stakeholders without granting HubSpot access.

Learn how to export datasets.

Create a dataset

To create a dataset:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Data Management > Data Studio. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Data Management > Data Studio directly.
  • Click Create dataset in the top right.
  • Click Bring in data.
Data sources

Data sources are the basis of your dataset. Learn more about different data sources in the Glossary.

  • On the Sources left side panel:

    • To add a HubSpot data source already in your CRM: select a data source from the list or click Help me choose to use HubSpot’s AI, to suggest objects. Upon selection, the Choose your columns left side panel will appear. To add additional data sources, click + Add source.
    • To add external data: click + Connect a new source. In the Add a data source panel, select the File option or an external application.

  • After selecting your data sources, in the list of properties, click the checkboxes next to the properties you want to appear in your dataset. Then, click Done.

  • To join additional data sources to construct a more complex dataset, click Sources at the top. In the left side panel, click Use advanced source configuration.

Advanced source configuration

To join another data source:

  • Click Join another data source, or the + icon in the data source viewer.

  • On the HubSpot data sources or External data sources tab, select a data source.

  • Click Continue.

  • On the Preview your join screen, configure the following:

    • In the Left table box, it will display the primary source you selected.
    • In the Right table box, it will display the additional source you selected.
    • Click the Left dropdown menu to select Left join or Inner join.
      • Left join: returns all rows from [primary data source] and any matching rows from [secondary data source].
      • Inner join: returns rows that have matching values in both [primary data source] and [secondary data source].
    • Click Use association labels or Use match key.
      • Use association labels: select an association label for the join.
      • Use match key: select a match key for the left table and right table.
    • Under Match behavior, specify the relationship between the selected data sources:
      • Multiple matches: one row in the left table can match multiple rows in the right table.
      • Only one match: one row in the left table can match at most one row in the right table. Additional rows won’t be included.
    • Click Add custom join.
Columns
  • To customize columns:
    • Drag and drop the columns to customize their order.
    • To see aggregate summaries at the bottom of the table for numeric columns, click the footer to toggle between summary functions.
  • To create new columns, click one of the following:
    • Add columns from a source
    • Add a Data Agent column
    • Add a formula column
Data Agent

When selecting the Add a Data Agent column option, you can use data agent to conduct research and generate new data in a smart column:

  • Click Add a Data Agent column.
  • In the Describe what you want to know textbox, write a description of the data you want to generate and extract from the smart column. Additionally, you can use suggested prompts. Then, click Preview.
  • In the Smart column name textbox, type the column name.
  • Review the description, and modify the text as needed.
  • Click + Insert column token to reference other properties within the dataset.
  • Click the Where should this data come from? dropdown menu to select a source for your data.
    • Web research: data from searching the internet.
    • Company research: data from the company’s primary website.
    • Dataset columns: data from another column in the dataset.
  • Click the What kind of data should this prompt return dropdown menu to specify the kind of information in the cell (e.g., number, text, or date).
    • String
    • Number
    • Boolean
  • Click Preview.
  • The smart column will now appear in the table.
Enrichment

Use Enrichment to fill gaps or validate data:

  • At the top, click Enrich. Then, click the checkboxes next to data you want to add to columns.
  • Click + Add selected columns.
  • After reviewing your enrichment selections, click Add enrichment column(s).
Formulas

Use Formulas to create calculations based on other columns:

  • At the top, click Formulas. Then, click one of the available options.

  • In the bottom panel, fill in the formula fields.

  • Then, click Save.

Modifiers

Use Modifiers to apply formatting changes and normalizations:

  • At the top, click Formulas.
  • Click Fix capitalization or Trim whitespace, then do the following:

    • Type a name in the column name textbox.

    • Click the Choose column dropdown menu to select a column.

    • Click the Transformation dropdown menu, and select Title case, Lower case, or Trim whitespace.

    • Click Save.

Summarized and unsummarized views

There are two types of views that are used to view your datasets:

  • Summarized view: the view for a dataset that’s created when it has more than one data source and there are multiple matches possible between the primary and secondary data sources. This view will show data grouped by primary data source and will be used in CRM sync, workflows, and lists. Only columns available in the summarized view will be available in CRM sync, workflows, and lists.
  • Unsummarized view: the view for a dataset that displays ungrouped data.

Please note: in cases where there’s only one source or there’s a one-to-one relationship between different sources (e.g., example@hubspot.com appears once in Snowflake and once in your HubSpot CRM), you will not be presented with a summarized or unsummarized view of your dataset, and the dataset can be used for reporting, CRM syncs, workflows, and lists. Learn how to configure your data join settings.

You can select between the two by clicking Expandable view in the top left, and then selecting Summarized view or Unsummarized view.

Filters

You can apply filters to your dataset.

  • At the top, click Filter. Click + Add filter or Advanced filter view.
  • If you selected Advanced filter view, click between the following advanced filters:
    • Row level filters: filter row before any grouping or summarization
    • Aggregate filters: filter rows based on fixed aggregate values
    • Summarized view filters: filter rows in the summarized view after summarization of one-to-many sources
  • If you selected + Add filter, click a filter from the pop-up box. Continue adding filters as needed.

Review dataset

Once you have completed customizing your dataset, you can do the following:

  • Review the table to make sure your dataset is appearing correctly.

  • After changes are made or saved, you should see the status update in the top right corner.

  • If your dataset has activations, the number of activations will appear.

  • Click to open the panel to review and edit them as needed.

  • If you are satisfied with your dataset, click Save. Click Use in to create a report, workflow, list, do a CRM sync, or export your dataset.

Glossary

Data sources

Data sources include CRM objects (e.g., contacts, custom objects), assets (e.g., website pages, emails), and activities (e.g., conversations, sales) you want to report on. You can select up to five per dataset.

The primary data source anchors the dataset, with all other sources linking to it. HubSpot connects them using the shortest path, automatically joining related data like contacts and deals without extra steps.

Other data sources require intermediary connections for integration. For example, if Deals is the primary source and blog post data is needed, HubSpot links them via Contacts and Web activities, automatically selecting the necessary sources.

Additional data sources

You can add secondary data sources to your dataset to consolidate information into a single view. Some sources will integrate automatically, while others may require additional input to establish a connection.

Automatic joins

Automatic joins are available for common HubSpot data combinations (e.g., Companies + Deals) and integrations with sync apps (e.g., Contacts + Stripe Invoices).

When selecting these source pairs, rows are automatically matched using a default column, typically Email Address or Company Domain.

To customize the matching column, you can manage the join in the source panel.

Custom joins

When integrating data from sources with flexible column structures—such as Google Sheets, AirTable, CSVs, and warehouses—you must provide additional details to enable data merging.

If a custom join is required, you’ll need to select matching columns from each source. This ensures that data aligns correctly, using common identifiers such as email addresses, IDs, or company domains.

Syntax

Within a function, you can use data from properties and fields or literal data. Property and field data will be dynamic based on the individual data sources, while literal data is constant. For example:

  • 2021-03-05 is a literal date, which is constant.
  • [CONTACT.createdate] is a property-based date, which is dynamic for each contact record.

Functions can include both literal and property/field data, as long as the data types are compatible with the function’s required arguments. For example:

DATEDIFF("MONTH", "2021-01-01", “[CONTACT.createdate]”)

Below, learn about the syntax for literals and property/field data, and how to incorporate them into formulas.

Literal syntax

Use literals to add specific, static strings of text, numbers, true or false values, and dates in your calculations.

  • String literal: text surrounded by quotation marks. For example, “My cool string”.

  • Number literal: numbers without quotation marks. For example, 42.

  • Boolean literal: true or false.

  • Date literal: a string formatted as "YYY-MM-DD" , or a date timestamp number (e.g, 1635715904).

Property syntax

Property references allow you to directly include values from the properties of your selected data sources. You don’t need to add the property as a dataset field to reference it.

Use the following syntax when referencing properties:

  • Reference expressions are always surrounded by square brackets ( [ and ] ).
  • Property references specify the object or event name, followed by a period and the internal property name. For example:
    • [CONTACT.lifecyclestage]
    • [COMPANY.name]
    • [e_hs_scheduled_email_v2.__hs_event_native_timestamp]
Field reference syntax

You can reference fields in a formula by surrounding the field name with square brackets. For example:

- `[Field 1]`
- `[My awesome custom field]`

You can reference fields in formulas as long as the formula’s operators and functions accept the field’s data type. For example, if you create a new field that contains a string, you can reference the field in a function that accepts strings:

  • If Field 1 is [DEAL.name], it contains a string value (the deal’s name).
  • CONCAT([Field 1], "Q4") would be valid because it contains two string values.
  • CONCAT([DEAL.name], 2012) would not be valid because it contains both a string and a number value.
Operators

You can use operators with literal and property/field values, and operators are evaluated in the standard PEMDAS order of operations. This allows you to nest operators using parentheses. For example:

  • Adding a number with a property reference: 1 + [DEAL.amount]
  • Using parentheses to nest operations: (1 + 2) * (3 + 4)

Operator

Description

Example usage

+

Add numbers. Returns a number.

1 + 1

= 2

[DEAL.amount] + 100

-

Subtract numbers. Returns a number.

100 - 1

= 99

EXP(1) - EXP(1)

= 0

WEEKNUM([DEAL.closedate]) - WEEKNUM([DEAL.createdate])

*

Multiply numbers. Returns a number.

2 * 2

= 4

POW(10, 2) * -1

= -100

[DEAL.amount] * 0.5

/

Divide numbers. Returns a number.

10/ 2

= 5

[DEAL.amount] / DATEDIFF("DAY", [DEAL.createdate], [DEAL.closedate])

-

Negates a number.

-100

= -100

-[DEAL.amount]

AND or &&

Checks if both of two boolean values are true. Returns a boolean.

true AND false

= false

CONTAINS(“HubSpot”, “Hub”) && CONTAINS(“HubSpot”, “Spot”)

= true

OR or ||

Check if either of two boolean values are true. Returns a boolean.

true OR false

= true

CONTAINS(“HubSpot”, “Hub”) || CONTAINS(“HubSpot”, “CRM”)

= true

!

Negatives a boolean value. Returns another boolean value.

!true

= false

= or ==

Equality operator. Returns a boolean value.

=true

= true

IF

IF logic is a set of rules performed if a certain condition is met. You can use IF logic to differentiate data. For example, you can use IF logic to:

  • Calculate different commissions based on the size of a deal (i.e. give a higher % for a bigger deal).
  • Bucket deals into tiers for analysis and action in your reports.
  • Translate feedback responses into categories (e.g. label 1-6 is detractor).
  • Define contact priority based on how many days they’ve been marked as lead.
LABEL

The LABEL function converts enumeration property interval values into user-friendly values. Some HubSpot defined properties, such as Deal and Contact owner are represented as internal values. This make analysis difficult. When used with HubSpot’s defined properties that support translation, the LABEL function will provide the translation based on portal settings, not user settings. For example, you can use the LABEL function to:

  • Access contact or deal stage names directly in fields

LABEL([DEAL.dealstage]) = "Closed Won"(10)

  • Reference HubSpot owners by name directly in fields

LABEL([DEAL.hubspot_owner_id]) = "John Smith"

WIDTH_BUCKET

Bin numerical values into buckets of equal width. Returns the number of the bucket that the value falls into.

If returned value is below the minimum, returns zero. If returned value is above the maximum, returns the number of buckets +1.

WIDTH_BUCKET(value, minValue, maxValue, bucketCount)

value: the number to compute in the bin number.

maxValue: the maximum value to bin to.

Buyer Intent, Intent Signals, and Custom Signals | Frequently asked questions

Please note: Buyer Intent and signal-based actions that add or track companies consume HubSpot Credits. For current credit rates, see the HubSpot Product and Services Catalog.

Summary

Buyer Intent helps you see which companies are in-market and showing intent for what you sell, so your sales and marketing teams know which accounts to prioritize and how to engage them. Find answers to common questions about Buyer Intent, Intent Signals, and Custom Signals, including how they’re structured, what costs credits, how companies are identified, and how your data is handled.

Learn more about using Buyer Intent and using Intent Signals.

Introduction: Buyer Intent, Intent Signals, and Custom Signals

What is the relationship between Buyer Intent, Intent Signals, and Custom Signals?

Buyer Intent is the overall feature. Within it are three key capabilities, shown as tabs in the UI:

  • Visitors: see which companies — both those already in your CRM and those that aren’t — are visiting your website and landing on your highest-intent pages.
  • Research: see which companies, in your CRM or not, are researching topics you care about or topics related to what your business sells.
  • Signals: track the companies you care about for buying signals. Within Signals, you can track both Standard Signals (predefined by HubSpot) and Custom Signals (ones you create yourself). Custom Signals are bespoke — you define them yourself.

The Visitors and Research tabs can be used independently of Intent Signals. There’s also a relationship between them: a key part of setting up Buyer Intent is defining your Visitor Intent criteria and selecting your Research Intent topics in configuration. Doing this benefits all three capabilities — it lets Visitors filter for companies hitting your highest-intent pages, lets Research filter for companies researching the topics you care about, and lets Signals track, detect, and emit signals tied to those same criteria and topics.

What is Intent Signals and how does it differ from Buyer Intent?

Buyer Intent is the overall feature — a full suite of intent capabilities native to HubSpot. Intent Signals is one capability within it, alongside Visitors and Research.

Where do I find Buyer Intent in HubSpot?

In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Buyer Intent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Buyer Intent directly.

What is the Website Visits tool (formerly the Prospects tool), and how does it differ from Buyer Intent?

Website Visits (formerly called Prospects) is HubSpot’s legacy tool for listing companies that visited your site, identified by IP address. It isn’t currently receiving updates or improvements, and it’s powered by third-party reverse-IP technology.

The Visitors capability in Buyer Intent is what HubSpot recommends using instead. It offers richer functionality and higher data quality, because it uses HubSpot’s proprietary reverse-IP technology to identify visiting companies.

Please note: ongoing roadmap investment for Website Visits is paused. HubSpot encourages customers to use Visitors in Buyer Intent instead.

What is Conversational Enrichment, and how does it relate to Buyer Intent?

Conversational Enrichment is a separate HubSpot feature that uses AI to read your conversations — emails, call transcripts, and meetings — and extract structured facts to update your CRM records automatically. It’s a different feature from Buyer Intent, which is based on visitor, research, and signals activity.

The two are related through Buyer Intent’s CRM-based signals. Conversational Enrichment and CRM-based signals use the same agentic extraction methodology to produce structured data from the same unstructured sources. The difference is in the output: Conversational Enrichment produces enrichment values on your records, while Buyer Intent, through its intent signals capability, produces real-time signals. Both look at the same sources and use the same technology to turn unstructured data into structured output — the output is different.

Tracking companies for Standard Signal monitoring

How do I turn on Standard Signal monitoring for a specific company?

There are several ways to track a company for Standard Signals. You can start tracking from:

  • The company record’s Intelligence tab or Buyer Intent CRM card.
  • A segment of companies.
  • A company index page.
  • The Signals tab within Buyer Intent, where you can track an existing segment, track companies ad hoc, or track all companies at once.

You can also set up automated tracking so companies are tracked when they become a target account, enter a chosen lifecycle stage, become a member of a segment, or enter a saved view in the Visitors or Research tab.

For the full set of methods, see use Intent Signals.

Please note: tracking a company for Standard Signals consumes credits as a recurring monthly cost. For current credit rates, see the HubSpot Product and Services Catalog.

If I turn on Standard Signal tracking for a company, do I automatically get Visitor Intent, Research Intent, and Custom Signals?

Tracking a company for Standard Signals provides Visitor Intent and Research Level Change signals, provided your Visitor Intent criteria are configured and your Research Intent topics are selected.

HubSpot sets both of these up for you automatically through auto-configuration. When you first land in Buyer Intent, HubSpot pre-selects up to three Visitor Intent criteria (based on the visitor traffic it detects through your tracking code) and selects Research Intent topics (based on the content of your website). Both are done for you and remain editable. Both need to be in place for you to receive the related Visitor Intent and Research Intent signals.

Custom Signals are a separate capability that you create and track individually, so they aren’t provided automatically.

Custom Signals

What’s the difference between Standard Signals and Custom Signals?

Standard Signals are predefined by HubSpot. There are many of them, across categories such as web intent, news, CRM, and champion. When you track a company for Standard Signals, HubSpot automatically monitors for all signals across all signal categories, and you pay a single recurring standard-signal tracking charge per company. You can then choose which Standard Signals to listen for and which to ignore.

Custom Signals work differently. You define each Custom Signal yourself, and for each one you choose which companies to track. There’s a separate recurring monthly charge for each company you track for each Custom Signal.

Both Standard and Custom Signals fall under the Signals capability.

What is a Custom Signal, and how does it differ from a Standard Signal?

A Custom Signal is one you create yourself. You write a plain-language description of an in-market behavior or buying cue that matters to you, give it a name, and HubSpot uses data agent to regularly check your tracked companies for it, flagging matches with links to the sources it found.

A Custom Signal differs from a Standard Signal in four ways:

  • Who defines it: you write a Custom Signal in your own words; Standard Signals are built by HubSpot.
  • Scope: your Custom Signal exists only in your account; Standard Signals are the same for all accounts.
  • How it’s evaluated: a Custom Signal is evaluated by data agent reading public web content against your prompt; Standard Signals come from defined events HubSpot tracks, such as funding, layoffs, executive hires, website visits, and research activity.
  • Cost: Custom Signals are billed at a higher rate than standard monitoring.

A Custom Signal isn’t a separate product. Once you create it, it appears alongside your standard intent signals.

How do I preview and test a Custom Signal before I save it?

After you write your signal prompt, HubSpot provides two ways to test it on the Create Custom Signal page before you save:

  • Auto-generated preview: shows example companies that triggered your signal in the last 90 days, each with the matching event and links to the sources.
  • Choose a company to test: select a specific company to see whether it triggers. You’ll see the result and sources, or “No signal detected.” You can only choose companies that already exist in your CRM.

If a company you expected doesn’t trigger, edit your prompt and test again. Testing doesn’t save or turn on the signal, and it doesn’t consume credits.

What are Custom Signal recommendations, and how do I use them?

HubSpot suggests ready-made Custom Signals for you to create:

  • Go to the Signals tab and open My Signals.
  • Your recommended signals appear automatically at the top of the My Signals panel, showing three suggested signals at a time. Each includes a name, a short description, and a View Signal link to open and use it.
  • Click the refresh button to display three more suggestions, or dismiss an individual recommendation to replace it with a new one.

Recommendations also appear when you create a Custom Signal. In the second step of the create flow, HubSpot shows recommendations directly below the prompt input, so you can draw inspiration from them or start from a recommended signal.

Please note: these recommend new Custom Signals for you to create — they aren’t recommendations about which Standard Signals to turn on.

Can Custom Signals read information behind paywalls, login screens, or inside PDFs?

Custom Signals read only publicly available web content. They visit pages anonymously and can’t sign in, so anything behind a login is inaccessible. A public teaser or snippet can still be used, and some soft paywalls that deliver the full page text may be read, but this is site-dependent.

Whether the contents of a public PDF can be read depends on how the signal is evaluated, so PDF reading isn’t guaranteed. At minimum, a public snippet describing a PDF can be used.

In short: public web text can be read; logins and paywalls can’t; PDF reading isn’t guaranteed.

What happens if a website my Custom Signal is scanning blocks AI crawlers?

Custom Signals don’t scan a single website, and they don’t scan your CRM data. Data agent researches across public sources — web search results, news, and company websites — to evaluate your prompt. If a page blocks it or fails — whether blocked by robots.txt, marked noindex, served behind an anti-bot challenge, or returning an error — data agent looks to other public sources, such as search engine results, that may carry the same information.

Because Custom Signals aren’t charged per run, if data agent doesn’t find a result on its current run, it tries again on the next run at no additional charge.

Why is my Custom Signal not producing any results?

There are two common causes:

  • The signal isn’t running. The signal isn’t activated, it’s paused, you aren’t tracking any companies for it, or you’re out of credits or have hit your Custom Signal action-level credit limit.
  • The event isn’t visible on the public web. The behavior you’ve described may not appear publicly — for example, a company doing internal research about CRMs isn’t detectable on the public web, so a signal looking for it won’t return results.

To help with this, the Custom Signal creation flow includes automatic validations that try to catch these scenarios before a signal is created, and Custom Signal recommendations offer examples of signals that are detectable on the public web.

Credits and billing

How many credits does it cost to add a company to my CRM from Buyer Intent?

Adding a company that Buyer Intent has identified for you consumes credits as a one-time charge. For current rates, see the HubSpot Product and Services Catalog.

Please note: adding a company manually by searching for it yourself is free. The credit charge applies only to adding a company that Buyer Intent has identified for you.

How many credits does it cost to track a company for Standard Signal monitoring?

Tracking a company for Standard Signal monitoring is a recurring credit cost, charged per company. It re-bills each month while monitoring remains on. For current rates, see the HubSpot Product and Services Catalog.

Please note: adding and tracking the same company works as a two-for-one action when both happen in the same billing period — most commonly when you add and track a company in a single action, which you can do in the Buyer Intent app. If you add a company and track it within the same billing period, you aren’t billed twice; you’ve already been charged for that period, and tracking continues to re-bill in later periods. If you add a company in one billing period and track it in a later one, a separate tracking charge applies at that time.

How are Custom Signals billed?

Custom Signals are billed with HubSpot credits on a recurring monthly basis, charged per company per Custom Signal each month. This covers HubSpot regularly checking that signal for that company on an ongoing basis. You’re billed once per company per signal for the month, not each time HubSpot checks.

Please note: Custom Signals cost more per company than Standard Signal tracking. For current rates, see the HubSpot Product and Services Catalog.

Do Custom Signals use the same credits as Standard Signal tracking?

Yes. Adding companies, tracking companies for Standard Signals, and tracking companies for Custom Signals all spend HubSpot credits. They’re treated as separate actions with separate line items. For current rates, see the HubSpot Product and Services Catalog.

Please note: you can set separate action-level limits for different actions, but all actions draw from the same shared intent credit pool.

Does it cost credits to view the companies identified in Visitors or Research?

No. Viewing and filtering the companies that appear in the Visitors and Research tabs is free and doesn’t consume credits. You can browse identified companies, apply filters, and save views without spending anything.

Credits are consumed only when you take a credit-based action, such as adding a company that Buyer Intent identified to your CRM or tracking a company for signals.

What happens when I run out of HubSpot credits, or I’ve hit one of my intent-related limits? Can I still see intent data?

Running out of credits, or reaching an intent-related limit, blocks only the actions that consume credits — adding a company to your CRM and tracking a company for monitoring.

You can still view your existing intent data: Research Intent, Visitor Intent, and Buyer Intent all remain visible at no cost. Without tracking, you won’t receive new Intent Signals.

Why am I getting a “no capacity” or credit limit error when I try to track companies?

This error indicates credit-gating, which can have a few causes:

  • You’ve reached a Buyer Intent usage limit, which an admin needs to raise.
  • You’ve reached an action-level limit set on the relevant action.
  • You’ve reached a feature-level limit for intent.
  • You’re out of HubSpot credits.

Intent uses several types of limits. At the account level, usage and limits configuration governs HubSpot credits overall. Within that, you can set a feature-level limit for intent, and within intent you can set action-level limits — for example, a separate limit for Custom Signals. Learn more about setting credit limits.

You can also set Buyer Intent usage limits in Buyer Intent’s own configuration settings, which let you break out limits for adding companies from Buyer Intent versus tracking companies for Standard Signals. (Otherwise, adding and standard-signal tracking share a single combined action-level limit.)

Please note: untracking companies doesn’t free up capacity within the current period. Because the cause varies, review which limit you’ve reached before adding credits.

If I stop tracking a company for signals, does it stop right away, and when does my credit usage period reset?

Untracking a company stops future monitoring, but it doesn’t free up capacity within the current billing period — you’ve already been charged for that period. Tracking charges recur monthly while monitoring stays on. For details on your credit balance and billing cycle, see the HubSpot Product and Services Catalog and your account’s credit usage settings.

Which HubSpot plans include Buyer Intent?

Full Buyer Intent functionality is available on any plan that includes HubSpot credits. The only requirement is access to HubSpot credits.

Please note: free accounts have limited access to Buyer Intent. They can see a limited number of companies visiting their website through Visitors and a limited number of companies researching relevant topics through Research. Credit-spending actions — such as tracking companies for signals or adding companies to the CRM — aren’t available on free accounts or on accounts without access to HubSpot credits.

Visitor Intent and company identification

How does Buyer Intent identify which companies are visiting my website?

Buyer Intent identifies the company behind a visit — not the individual person — using an IP-address lookup. It takes the visitor’s IP address and determines which company it belongs to.

Learn more about how Visitors works.

How quickly do companies and Visitor Intent signals appear after a visit?

Identified companies appear on the Visitors tab, and Visitor Intent Standard signals are detected for tracked companies, on the same timeline. Both can happen close to real time, though there can be a delay of up to a few hours.

Please note: a Visitor Intent Standard signal fires when a tracked company meets, or stops meeting, the criteria of a configured Visitor Intent criterion. For example, if you set a criterion for companies that visited your pricing page in the last week with at least 10 visitors, a signal fires when a company meets that criterion, and another fires when the company no longer meets it.

Does bot traffic, scrapers, or spam crawlers consume my credits?

No. Visitor Intent doesn’t charge per visit, per page view, or per identified company, so bots, scrapers, and spam crawlers can’t consume your credits by visiting your site. You consume credits only when you add a company to your CRM or track a company for intent monitoring.

Please note: Buyer Intent filters out known bot and junk traffic to keep it from affecting your data quality. This filtering isn’t related to a per-visit charge, because there is no per-visit charge.

How many Visitor Intent criteria can I set up?

You can set up to 10 Visitor Intent criteria — the page and URL view patterns that indicate intent.

Please note: this limit is separate from Research Intent topics, which have their own limit.

Why am I not seeing any Visitor Intent signals for my account?

This is usually the result of a configuration issue. Check two things:

  • The HubSpot tracking code is installed and firing on your site.
  • Your Visitor Intent criteria are configured correctly. In configuration, each criterion needs a domain and the page path you’re targeting. Common issues include entering full URLs or malformed page paths, and selecting visits, visitors, or timeframe requirements that restrict the chance of criteria qualification.

Please note: whether signals are emitted depends on your traffic volume — how many people visit your site — and how narrow your Visitor Intent criteria are.

Why does a company show up in Website Visits but not in Buyer Intent, or vice versa?

Website Visits and Buyer Intent identify visiting companies differently, so some difference is expected. Website Visits uses legacy third-party reverse-IP technology and lists essentially every company it can match, unranked. The Visitors capability in Buyer Intent uses HubSpot’s own, higher-quality reverse-IP technology, honors visitor cookie opt-outs, and surfaces companies based on meaningful activity within your target market.

As a result, a company can appear in one tool and not the other. For the most accurate results, HubSpot recommends using Visitors in Buyer Intent.

Why do I see companies that don’t seem relevant, or visit numbers that look higher than expected?

Buyer Intent identifies visiting companies by IP address, which is probabilistic. Multiple unrelated visitors can share an IP address — for example, on a shared office network, VPN, internet service provider, or large organization — so a company may surface when the visit actually came from someone unrelated, and a single company can appear to have a high number of visits when many separate visitors resolve to the same IP.

You can reduce noise by tightening your target market, refining your Visitor Intent criteria, and adding exclusions.

Please note: if you compare Buyer Intent with another visitor resolution tool, expect some differences. Each tool uses its own IP-matching technology, so no two tools surface exactly the same companies.

Why does a company have Visitor Intent signals or page views within Buyer Intent but no page views on its record?

Buyer Intent-based visit data and page view data derived from associated contacts on a company record come from two different systems. Buyer Intent identifies the company behind a visit by IP address, at the company level. Page view data derived from associated contacts on a company record is based on cookied website analytics tied to opted-in contacts. Because they’re tracked differently, a company can show visitor intent in Buyer Intent without matching page views appearing on its record, and the reverse can also happen. This is expected.

Research Intent

How is Research Intent scored? What do High, Moderate, Mild, and Low mean?

Research Intent is shown on a four-level scale — Low, Mild, Moderate, and High — based on how much a company’s research activity on the topics you track has increased recently, comparing the last 30 days with the prior 30 days.

  • High: the company has significantly increased its research on your topics over the past 30 days compared with the previous 30.
  • Moderate: a moderate increase in research activity over the same period.
  • Mild: a mild increase in research activity over the same period.
  • Low: little to no increase in research activity.
How often is Research Intent data refreshed?

Research Intent data refreshes once a day.

How does Research Intent know what a company is researching?

Research Intent is powered by HubSpot’s intent ecosystem — a large network of websites that have the HubSpot tracking code installed and have opted into intent data sharing. When a company (identified by IP address) is active on topics you track anywhere across that ecosystem, HubSpot attributes that research to the company, even if the company has never visited your own site.

Please note: Research Intent isn’t search-engine tracking. HubSpot doesn’t see what a company types into a search engine. It categorizes the sites in its ecosystem by topic and detects research activity against those topics.

Can I track my own keywords or competitor names in Research Intent? Is there a topic limit?

Research Intent uses a pre-categorized topic library. You select up to 20 topics from the available topics rather than entering free-text keywords or competitor names, so a very specific or niche term may not be available. To see which topics HubSpot has associated with a company, enter their domain in the research topic selection UI and HubSpot returns the mapped topics.

Markets and detected signals

What is Total Addressable Market (TAM), and how is it calculated?

TAM is the total number of companies in HubSpot’s company enrichment dataset that match your market’s firmographic filters (industry, employee range, revenue, geography, web technologies, and company keywords), counting only active companies. It’s a company count, not a revenue figure.

TAM is shown next to Market Penetration — the percentage of your TAM already in your CRM (companies from the market that are in your CRM ÷ TAM × 100) — so you can see how much of your addressable market you’ve captured.

Please note: some views also show Market Opportunity, which shows the companies in your TAM that aren’t yet in your CRM.

What firmographic criteria can I filter on when creating a target market?

When you create a target market, you can filter companies on six firmographic categories: Industries, Company keywords, Employee range, Revenue, Web technologies, and Location. Location is made up of three separate fields: Company country, Company state/region, and Company city.

You can combine these categories — for example, company keywords alongside industries to narrow within an industry — or use them individually.

How do I create a target market?

You can create a target market in one of two places.

From Buyer Intent:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Buyer Intent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Buyer Intent directly.
  • Go to Configuration.
  • Click Manage markets.

From CRM settings:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar., In the left sidebar menu, click Data Management > Markets.
  • Click Create new market.

Give the target market a name and set your firmographic filters (industry, company keywords, employee range, revenue, web technologies, and location) to define which companies belong to it.

What types of company news events does HubSpot detect as signals?

HubSpot detects a wide range of company news events as signals — dozens of event types in total. These include funding rounds, geographic and physical expansion, technology investment, executive hiring and leadership changes, layoffs, growth metrics, mergers and acquisitions, strategic partnerships, product launches, regulatory approval, industry recognition and awards, office closures, and going public (IPO).

For a full, up-to-date list of the news signals HubSpot detects, see use Intent Signals.

How to use HubSpot intent data across HubSpot tools

Once a signal is detected, how can I access and use it?

When HubSpot detects a signal for a company you’re tracking, the signal surfaces in three ways:

  • As an event on the record. Each detected signal is emitted as an event associated with the company or contact record. Because it’s an event, the signal is available across HubSpot — as segment criteria, as a workflow trigger, as a lead scoring input, and as a data source in the custom report builder. The event’s metadata is available as additional filtering criteria in those tools.
  • As a value in the Recent Intent Signals company property. HubSpot writes the signals detected for a tracked company over the last 30 days to the Recent Intent Signals company property, including custom signal hits. Add Recent Intent Signals as a column on your company index or saved views to see hits at a glance. This is useful if you prefer to build segments, workflow triggers, index columns, and saved views from property values rather than from events.
  • On the record activity timeline. Detected signals appear as cards on the company or contact activity timeline, giving reps intent context directly on the record — what the company is doing and why it’s showing intent — without leaving where they work.

Use events when you want the full signal detail and metadata, and the Recent Intent Signals property when you want a simpler, value-based way to drive segments, workflows, and index views.

Can I see the evidence behind Standard and Custom Signals?

Yes. When you open a signal, HubSpot shows cited sources when applicable. News and Custom Signals include references or sources, so you can see where the information came from. Visitor intent ties back to the Visitor Intent criterion the company met, and you can see the company’s recent page views in Buyer Intent. Research Intent signals show the topic and research level.

What are common ways to use Intent Signals?

Most teams use Intent Signals in a few core ways:

  • Alert reps when a tracked company shows a signal, using a workflow notification or an email digest.
  • Build lists and segments of companies with specific signals to target with campaigns or hand to the prospecting agent.
  • Score leads by using signal events as criteria in HubSpot’s lead scoring.
  • Give reps context on the record, where signals appear on the activity timeline so reps can personalize their outreach.
How do I set up a notification when a target account shows Buyer Intent?

There are two ways to do this:

  • Set up an email digest from a Buyer Intent saved view of the accounts you want to monitor.
  • Build a workflow with a notification-based action that uses one of the following triggers:

The workflow can then notify the rep with an internal email, an in-app notification, or a task assigned to the company owner.

For step-by-step instructions, see use Intent Signals.

How do Buyer Intent Signals work with the prospecting agent?

Tracked companies that receive signals aren’t passed to the prospecting agent automatically, but you can configure them to enroll into the prospecting agent automatically via workflows or segment membership. Once enrolled, the prospecting agent researches the company, scores its fit and a “why now,” prioritizes it, and drafts outreach using signal-based context.

Can I use Buyer Intent Signals in Marketing Hub campaigns or lists?

Yes. Intent isn’t limited to Sales Hub; you can use it in Marketing Hub, where it works at the company level.

Detected signals appear as company-level events and as values for the Recent Intent Signals company property. Companies that enter your Buyer Intent saved views also emit a Buyer Intent Saved View Change event.

These are available for list segmentation and workflow triggers. You can build company lists and segments filtered on intent, trigger workflows from intent, and use Buyer Intent to auto-add companies to static lists that your campaigns then target. If you run company-based advertising campaigns — for example, on LinkedIn — intent-based segments work there too.

Can I report on Intent Signals over time?

Yes. Because detected signals are emitted as events, you can build reports on them in HubSpot’s custom report builder — for example, tracking how many companies fired a given signal over time, or breaking signals down by segment.

Does Buyer Intent give me contact-level information?

Buyer Intent works at the company level — it identifies the companies showing intent, not the individual people visiting. Some signals do fire at the contact level (for example, job change signals on associated contacts), but visitor and research intent identify the company, not the specific visitor.

Can I access Buyer Intent data through HubSpot’s public APIs?

There’s no dedicated public Buyer Intent API, but you can access certain data in two ways. Recent signals and certain visit data are written to company properties, which the public CRM API can read. All signals are also emitted as events, which you can retrieve through the Events API.

What happens to my Buyer Intent data when I delete my HubSpot account?

When you delete your account, your data — including your Buyer Intent and intent signals data — is handled according to HubSpot’s standard data retention and deletion practices. Deleting your account isn’t the same as an immediate wipe: data is retained for a period and then permanently removed as part of HubSpot’s deletion process.

For details on how HubSpot stores, retains, and deletes customer data, along with HubSpot’s security, privacy, and compliance commitments, visit the HubSpot Trust Center.

Connect HubSpot to Microsoft Azure Synapse Analytics

Please note: if you’re a Super Admin, opt your account into the Data Studio beta to use this feature.

HubSpot Credits required for certain features syncing data directly from a single warehouse source in Data Studio to the HubSpot CRM doesn’t consume HubSpot Credits. If you prepare the data in Data Studio before syncing (for example, by creating calculated fields or joining it with other data sources), those actions consume HubSpot Credits.

Summary

Connect HubSpot to Microsoft Azure Synapse Analytics to export selected HubSpot CRM data to native tables in an Azure Synapse dedicated SQL pool. You can select the objects, associations, events, and sync schedule for each destination.

Before you get started

Understand requirements

You need the following:

  • An Azure Synapse workspace with a running dedicated SQL pool.
  • A database in the dedicated SQL pool for HubSpot’s exported data.
  • A Microsoft Entra ID service principal.
  • A user for the service principal in the selected Synapse database.
  • The required permissions to create and manage HubSpot-owned schemas and tables.

The Microsoft Entra ID service principal must be able to:

  • Create schemas.
  • Create tables.
  • Insert rows.
  • Rename or alter HubSpot-owned tables.
  • Delete HubSpot-owned tables and schemas.

HubSpot creates and manages a separate schema for each destination. Don’t modify objects in this schema directly.

Please note: Azure Synapse Data Out supports dedicated SQL pools only. Serverless SQL pools aren’t supported.

Understand network requirements

The Azure Synapse dedicated SQL endpoint must be reachable from HubSpot over TCP port 1433. HubSpot uses TLS, and the server certificate is validated.

If your Synapse workspace uses firewall or network restrictions, allow inbound access from the HubSpot Synapse egress addresses for your account region.

Region

IP range

NA1

54.174.62.128/26

EU1

143.244.87.0/25

AP1

216.157.42.32/27

NA2

216.157.40.32/27

NA3

216.157.41.32/27

Install the Microsoft Azure Synapse Analytics app

It’s recommended to open your HubSpot and Azure consoles in separate browser tabs.

  • In the HubSpot App Marketplace, search for Microsoft Azure Synapse Analytics.
  • Click Install.
  • Click Next.
  • Enter the required Microsoft Entra ID information:
    • Tenant ID.
    • Client ID.
    • Client secret.
  • Click Connect to Microsoft Azure Synapse Analytics.

Connect HubSpot to your Synapse database

  • In the Permissions section, copy the displayed SQL template.
  • Replace the placeholder with the name of your Microsoft Entra ID service principal.
  • Run the SQL statements in your selected Synapse database.
  • In the Destination section, enter the following information:
    • Dedicated SQL endpoint.
    • Database name.

Use the dedicated SQL endpoint in the following format:

<workspace-name>.sql.azuresynapse.net

Don’t use the serverless SQL endpoint:

<workspace-name>-ondemand.sql.azuresynapse.net
  • Make sure the selected dedicated SQL pool is running.
  • Click Test connection.
  • If the connection test is successful, click Next.

Please note: a paused or unavailable dedicated SQL pool can cause the connection test or a sync to fail.

Configure the sync

  • Select the data sources to export.
  • Select the objects, associations, and events to include.
  • Select the sync frequency and start time.
  • Click Start sync.

Monitor the sync

To view sync details, including the sync status, last sync, errors, sync activity, and sync history:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Data Management > Data Integration. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Data Management > Data Integration directly.
  • Click App Syncs.
  • Search for Microsoft Azure Synapse Analytics.
  • Click the sync.

From the sync details page, you can:

  • Pause the sync.
  • Archive the sync.
  • Start a sync manually.

Connect HubSpot to Microsoft Fabric

Connect HubSpot to Microsoft Fabric to bring warehouse data into HubSpot or export selected HubSpot CRM data to Microsoft Fabric. Use Data Studio to access Microsoft Fabric data alongside your HubSpot data, or configure a data out sync to export selected objects, associations, and events to tables in a Microsoft Fabric warehouse.

Please note: if you’re a Super Admin, opt your account into the Data Studio beta to use this feature.

HubSpot Credits required for certain features syncing data directly from a single warehouse source in Data Studio to the HubSpot CRM doesn’t consume HubSpot Credits. If you prepare the data in Data Studio before syncing (for example, by creating calculated fields or joining it with other data sources), those actions consume HubSpot Credits.

Before you get started

Before you connect HubSpot to Microsoft Fabric, review the following requirements and considerations.

Understand requirements

To sync data with Microsoft Fabric, you’ll need:

  • A Microsoft Fabric workspace with a Fabric Warehouse.
  • A Warehouse in the workspace to store HubSpot’s exported data.
  • A Microsoft Entra ID service principal added to the Fabric workspace with the Contributor role.
  • The service principal’s tenant ID, client ID, and client secret.

The Microsoft Entra ID service principal must have permission to create and manage HubSpot-owned objects in the destination Fabric Warehouse. During connection validation and syncs, HubSpot creates schemas and tables, inserts data, renames staging tables, and removes temporary objects. Grant the service principal the Contributor role on the Fabric workspace to allow HubSpot to:

  • Create schemas
  • Create tables
  • Insert rows
  • Rename or alter HubSpot-owned tables
  • Drop HubSpot-owned tables and schemas

Your Fabric Warehouse SQL endpoint must be reachable by HubSpot on TCP port 1433. HubSpot uses TLS for all connections and validates the server certificate.

If your Fabric workspace restricts network access, add HubSpot’s egress IP addresses for your account region to the allowlist.

Region

IP range

NA1

54.174.62.128/26

EU1

143.244.87.0/25

AP1

216.157.42.32/27

NA2

216.157.40.32/27

NA3

216.157.41.32/27

Understand limitations and considerations
  • Microsoft Fabric Data Out supports Fabric Warehouses only. Lakehouses aren’t supported as export destinations.
  • Each sync creates a full snapshot of the selected HubSpot data. A successful sync replaces the previous snapshot in the destination tables. HubSpot doesn’t retain previous snapshots. If a table fails during a sync, its previous data remains available until the next successful sync.
  • Each object, event, or association pair can be included in one recurring Microsoft Fabric sync per HubSpot account.
  • Each sync replaces the destination table. Table-level grants or settings added in your Fabric Warehouse aren’t preserved between syncs.
  • Reconnecting with a different service principal requires adding that service principal to the Fabric workspace with the Contributor role before the connection test or sync can succeed.

Install the Microsoft Fabric app

To connect Microsoft Fabric to HubSpot, it’s recommended to open your HubSpot account and Microsoft Fabric workspace in separate browser tabs.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the Marketplace icon in the top navigation bar, then select HubSpot Marketplace.

  • Search for and select the Microsoft Fabric app.

  • Click Install.

  • Enter the required Microsoft Entra ID information:

    • Tenant ID
    • Client ID
    • Client secret

  • Click Connect to Microsoft Fabric.

Connect HubSpot to your Microsoft Fabric Warehouse

In your Microsoft Fabric workspace, confirm that the Microsoft Entra ID service principal has the Contributor role.

After installing the Microsoft Fabric app, you’ll be redirected to the Data integration tool in HubSpot, where a side pane will guide you through syncing data between HubSpot and Microsoft Fabric, based on the directions you want to sync:

  • Microsoft Fabric → HubSpot: configure syncing from Microsoft Fabric to HubSpot.
  • HubSpot → Microsoft Fabric: configure syncing from HubSpot to Microsoft Fabric.

Sync HubSpot data to your Microsoft Fabric account

  • Enter the following information in the Destination section:
    • SQL connection string: the server address for your Fabric Warehouse, without the port number.
    • Warehouse name: the name of the Fabric Warehouse where HubSpot data will be exported.
  • Click Test connection.
  • If the connection test is successful, click Next.

Please note: you don’t need to run SQL scripts to grant HubSpot access to the Fabric Warehouse. The Contributor role allows HubSpot to create and manage the required schemas and tables.

Configure the sync

  • Select the data sources to export:
    • Objects: HubSpot CRM object data.
    • Associations: relationships between HubSpot records.
    • Events: selected event data.
  • Select the objects, properties, associations, or events to include in the sync.
  • Select the sync frequency and when the sync should start.
  • Click Start sync.

Each sync creates a full snapshot of the selected data. A successful sync replaces the previous snapshot in the destination tables.

For more information about exported tables, column types, and querying your data, learn how to export HubSpot data to Microsoft Fabric.

Monitor the sync

After you’ve configured syncing between your accounts, you can review syncing status and history from the sync details page:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Data Management > Data Integration. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Data Management > Data Integration directly.
  • Click the App Syncs tab.
  • Search for or select the Microsoft Fabric sync.
  • Click the sync.
  • On the sync details page, review the sync status, last sync time, errors, sync activity, and sync history.You can also pause an existing sync or manually start a sync by clicking Sync now.

Sync statuses and error handling

The table below outlines possible syncing statuses:

Status

Description

Syncing

A sync attempt is currently in progress.

Synced

The last sync completed successfully.

Failed

The last sync encountered an error.

Archived

The sync configuration was manually removed, but can be reviewed for posterity.

If a sync fails:

  • A Failed status will appear on the sync details page, along with information about which tables succeeded or failed to sync.
  • The next scheduled sync will automatically re-attempt a full sync.
  • You can trigger a re-sync manually at any time from the sync details page.

Create and use summary functions in datasets

A dataset is a collection of data from across your HubSpot account that can then be used in custom reports. A dataset can include properties for CRM objects and HubSpot assets, along with formulas to calculate your data as needed.

Summary functions allow you to aggregate data across multiple rows within datasets. It also allows you to calculate rates and ratios.

Metrics that can be calculated using summary functions include:

  • Conversion rate
  • Average order size
  • Average margin
  • Close ratio
  • Lifetime value
  • Customer acquisition cost
  • Churn rate
  • SLA adherence
  • Custom NPS calculations

Row-level vs summary formulas

Row-level formulas: execute row-level operations and make calculations across a single record. The formula result displays one value per row, and all context for the calculation exists at a row level. Find more information in the syntax section of the datasets knowledge base.

Summary formulas: execute multi-row data operations and calculate metrics across multiple records. The formula result displays one value per row, but the context for the calculation may contain more than one row of data.

Use summary functions

When creating a Formula field, you can use the below summary functions to create functions:

List of summary functions

Function

Definition

Input/Output

Syntax

Adds values in a given column and returns an aggregate value.

Input: Number/Null

Output: Number/Null

SUM([Value])

`SUM([DEAL.Amount])
