`

DISTINCT_COUNT

Returns the number of rows in a given column.

Input: Number/Null

Output: Number/Null

COUNT([Value])

`DISTINCT_COUNT([DEAL.hs_object_id])

DISTINCT_COUNT([DEAL.dealname])

`

AVERAGE

Calculates the average value of a column of numbers. The average value of a column is equal to the sum of the values divided by the number of values.

Input: Number/Null

Output: Number/Null

AVERAGE([Value])

`AVERAGE ([Deal.Amount])

AVERAGE(DATEDIFF(“DAY”,[DEAL.createdate], NOW()))

`

MIN

Returns the lowest value in a given column or the lowest value between two values on the same row.

Input: Number/Date/Datetime/Null

Output: Number/Date/Datetime/Null

MIN([Value])

`MIN([Ticket.Create_Date])

MIN([DEAL.AMOUNT)

`

MAX

Returns the highest value in a given column or the highest value between two values on the same row.

Input: Number/Date/Datetime/Null

Output: Number/Date/Datetime/Null

MAX([Value])

`MAX([Ticket.Create_Date])

MAX([DEAL.AMOUNT)

`

Create a summary function

Columns calculated with summary functions can be used in the custom report builder as a measure. Measures are numerical or quantitative values that can be broken down using dimensions.

Within the dataset builder, summary measures will repeat results on each row. The calculation defaults to a table calculation until used in the custom report builder where the report configuration defines the summary level of the measure.

Learn more about summary formulas in datasets and view examples.

Create row level summary results

You can also use summary functions to create row level results that will ignore any reporting dimensions. This requires using a FIXED() function.

Function

Input/Output

Syntax

Example

FIXED

Input: Summary expression

Output: Row-level result

SUM([Value])

`FIXED (SUM([DEAL.Amount]), [DEAL.pipeline])

SUM(IF([Is Closed Won] = true, 1,0), [DEAL.hubspot_owner_id])

`

Please note: if no optional value is defined in the FIXED() function, the calculation will be computed at the table level and will ignore all dimensions in the report view.

Example

Track conversion or win rate

Win rate refers to the proportion of successful deals out of the total number of opportunities. By tracking win rates based on product, market, target audience, and other factors, you can pinpoint the chances of success for each opportunity. This will allow you to strategically direct your resources toward those with the highest conversion potential.

  • Data source needed: Deals
  • Type of metric: Flexible measure
  • Formula:

DISTINCT_COUNT(IF(LABEL([DEAL.dealstage]) = "Invoiced", [DEAL.hs_object_id], NULL)) / DISTINCT_COUNT(IF([DEAL.hs_is_closed] = true, [DEAL.hs_object_id], NULL))

View this example below in the datasets editor:

This conversion rate formula will now appear in the dataset, which can be used in reports.

Create custom events

Use custom events in HubSpot to define and track events that are unique to your business. Custom events can be tied to event properties, which you can then use across HubSpot’s tools. For example, you may want to track offline events such as attendance at an in-person product launch.

Learn the three different methods to create custom events. You can send custom events via an API, upload a spreadsheet of event data, or use webhooks (Data Hub Professional and Enterprise only).

After setting up a custom event, you can review custom event data across different tools. You can create reports with custom event data, review custom event occurrences on contacts’ timelines, and use custom events in workflows.

Finally, track your custom event performance in the custom event management tool. You may also need resolve unknown property errors in the custom event management tool.

Different methods to create custom events

The event creation process involves two parts:

  • Defining the event in HubSpot, including any custom event properties.
  • Creating a Javascript Code Snippet or Defining the API call that will trigger the event.

There are different ways to create custom events:

  • Send via API: use the Custom event definition endpoint to create your event. From there, use your event ID with the send Custom event endpoint to send event occurrences to HubSpot.
  • Capture data from your website without the API:
    • Code Javascript: using Custom Javascript, you can insert custom code into your HubSpot tracking script by using the code editor.
    • Use event visualizer: track page views or clicked elements by selecting them on your website. Learn more about creating custom events with the Event visualizer.
  • Import spreadsheet: upload a spreadsheet of event data to capture offline activity, backfill data, or manually integrate any tool with HubSpot.
  • Setup webhooks (Data Hub Professional and Enterprise only): customize the conditions that trigger a webhook to be fired and the data that’ll be sent.

Please note: any events created in the legacy Custom Events tool will no longer work after August 1st, 2025.

Create custom events using the API

If you’re sending data to HubSpot via API, you can use the Send via API option or use the Custom event definition endpoint to create your event. Learn more about defining your API call in HubSpot’s developer documentation.

You’ll need a few pieces of information for your API call, which you can get from inside HubSpot:

  • Event name: the internal name for the event.
  • Property names: the internal names for the properties you’ll be sending data to.

To finish creating your event to send data via API:

  • Select Send data to HubSpot and copy the Tracking ID.
  • Click Create.

To find the internal event name for an existing event and property names:

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Data Management > Event Management.
  • Click the name of the event. You’ll then be taken to the event details page.
  • At the top, locate the event name under Internal name. To copy the internal name, click the copy icon next to the name.
  • To find the internal names for the properties you’ll be updating, click the name of a property.
  • In the right panel, click the code icon, then view the name under Internal name.

Please note:

When sending data to your event, the below limits apply:

  • The property names are limited to 50 characters.
  • URL and referrer properties can receive up to 1024 characters, while all other properties can receive up to 256 characters.
  • Each event occurrence can contain data for up to 50 properties.
  • Property internal names must start with a letter and contain only lowercase letters a-z, numbers 0-9, and underscores. Properties with the same internal name after lowercasing are considered duplicates, and only one of the properties will be used after the occurrence.

If these limits are exceeded when making an HTTP API request, the request will fail. If these limits are exceeded when making a JS API request, HubSpot will truncate any property name values to the allowed length and/or update only 50 properties per event occurrence.

Create custom events with JavaScript code

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Data Management > Event Management.

  • In the top right, click Create an event, then select Create custom event.

  • Select Code Javascript.

  • Enter an Event name and optionally provide your event description.

  • Select an Associated object. This allows you to associate your event occurrences with different objects in HubSpot, including Contacts, Companies, Deals, and Tickets.

  • Click Next.

Add properties to the event

When an event is created, default event properties will be available. You can also create your own custom properties. Event properties are stored separately from other CRM properties, and are unique to the event (i.e. you can’t edit these properties from your account settings).

  • To turn off the creation of default event properties, toggle the Default event properties to off.

  • To create custom properties, select the property type by clicking the Field type for your property. Options include:

    • Custom string property: create a property that is a plain text string.
    • Custom number property: create a property that is a number value.
    • Custom timestamp property: create a property that’s a date value. You must send your data in the form of epoch milliseconds or ISO8601.
    • Custom date property: create a property that’s a date value.
    • Custom boolean property: create a property that’s a boolean value.
    • Custom enumeration property: create a property with a set of predefined values.

  • When you have selected your property, configure the property in the right panel:

  • Enter a name for the property and enter a Description for the property.

    • For Enumeration properties, click Next and enter your property Labels and Values.

      • Enumeration properties can be single or multi-select. To enable multi-select values, toggle the Support multi-value toggle on.

      • You must set your values and labels before sending data to them. If this step isn’t completed before sending data that’s not in the list, the data won’t be available to use. To send multiple values via API, separate them with a semicolon.

Please note: it’s not possible to import multi-select enumeration properties.

  • Click Next.
  • After setting up the event and its properties, you can add this event to your website’s tracking code by selecting Javascript code snippet.
  • Click Done.

Creating events with a Javascript code snippet allows you to add Javascript to your HubSpot tracking code automatically. This can be used for capturing more complex event data which the tracking code does not capture by default.

  • Select Javascript code snippet. Use the snippet in the right panel to track the event in HubSpot. Any custom properties created will be predefined within the code snippet.
  • Modify the snippet as needed by entering text within the right panel. Any code you add will automatically be included as part of your HubSpot tracking code.
  • When you’re finished, click Create to finish your event and automatically start tracking.

Import custom event data from spreadsheets

Upload your attendance data from in person events, timestamped data coming from apps you don’t integrate with HubSpot, one off lead or campaign data from a vendor, or any other event data in spreadsheet form. Events allow you to capture behavior and then use the behavior across HubSpot.

Imports can create and update the following records:

  • Contacts
  • Companies
  • Deals
  • Tickets
  • Services
  • Projects
  • Appointments
  • Courses
  • Listings
  • Orders
  • Custom objects

The required properties vary based on the object type.

Event imports can only be used for events which have already occurred. The following must be included in a custom event import file:

  • Contact email address.
  • Occurred at timestamp. Learn more about formatting date properties in import files.

Example file

To import custom events:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Data Management > Event Management. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Data Management > Event Management directly.
  • In the top right, click Create an event, then select Create custom event.
  • Select Import spreadsheet.
  • Click either Create a new event or Import to an existing event.
    • If you select Import to an existing event, use the dropdown menu to choose the existing event, then continue with the steps to upload your spreadsheet.
    • If you select Create a new event, continue with the steps below.
  • Enter an Event name and optionally provide your event description.
  • Select an Associated object. At this time, events created via import can only be associated with contacts.
  • Upload your spreadsheet or paste directly from your spreadsheet. Select how to import the objects and the file language, then click Next.
  • Map columns to event and contact properties, then click Next.
  • Confirm the name of your import file.
  • click the checkbox to agree that contacts expect to hear from you and that your import file does not include a purchased list. Learn more about HubSpot’s acceptable use policy.
  • Select the date format of the Occurred at property.
  • Click Finish import.

Send custom events via the API endpoint

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Data Management > Event Management.

  • In the top right, click Create an event, then select Create custom event.

  • Select Send via API.

  • Enter an Event name, and optionally, provide your event description.

  • To add custom event properties:

    • Type a property name. This name will be applied to the internal name as well.
    • Click the Field type dropdown menu, and select a field type.
    • Optionally, add a description.
    • If you want to add more custom properties, click + Add custom property.
    • Click Next.

  • To link objects:

    • Click the Select a primary object dropdown menu, then select an associated object. This allows you to associate your event occurrences with different objects, including contacts, companies, deals, and tickets.
    • Click Customize the match and selecting your matching ID between your event and object records. The event will only link to the object record when their matching IDs are identical. If you use a custom matching ID, the object property you select must require unique values.

  • To create an objectless event:

    • Click the Select a primary object dropdown menu, then select No Object. This creates an event without associating event occurrences with CRM records. You can use the event to trigger workflows in the Agentic automation builder.

  • Click Next.

  • To track the event in HubSpot, click Copy next to the tracking ID.

  • Click Create event.

Please note:

  • You can only match event properties and object properties of the same data type.
  • If needed, you can edit the custom match later, but you can’t change the primary object selected.
  • If you create an objectless event, you can’t associate it with a CRM object later.

Create custom events using webhooks

Set the conditions that will trigger a webhook.

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Data Management > Event Management.
  • In the top right, click Create an event, then select Create custom event.
  • Select Setup webhooks.
  • Enter an Event name and select an Associated object.
  • Click Next.
  • Set up a test event:
    • Copy the Webhook URL.
    • Navigate to the webhook settings page in the third-party app you want to integrate with.
    • Paste in the copied URL.
    • Click Send a test event.
  • Click Next.
  • To link objects:
    • Review the properties for your webhook. Click the Property type dropdown menu to select a property type.
    • Click Next.
    • Select a property from your third-party webhook that’s an exact match for a HubSpot object property.
  • To create an objectless event:
    • Click the Select a primary object dropdown menu, then select No Object. This creates an event without associating event occurrences with CRM records. You can use the event to trigger workflows in the Agentic automation builder.
  • In the upper right, click Create event.

Review and use custom event data in HubSpot

Custom event data can be viewed and used across HubSpot’s tools. Below, learn where to view event occurrences and the ways that you can incorporate that data into other tools.

You can open your selected events directly in select HubSpot tools with the actions dropdown in your event list, the single event view, or the top right corner of charts in the analyze tab.

Create reports with custom event data

Custom event occurrences can be analyzed from the custom events tool, and event data will also be available in the custom report builder and attribution reports.

Learn more about analyzing your custom events.

Review event occurrences on contact timelines

Event occurrences will appear on the contact record timeline, along with any properties that were populated.

To view event details on the contact timeline:

  • Navigate to a contact record where a custom event has occurred.
  • To filter a contact timeline by event occurrences, click Filter activity, then select Custom event.
  • In the contact timeline, click to expand the event to display the event details.

Please note: you cannot view timeline activity on custom events created using webhooks.

Use custom events in workflows

In a workflow, you can delay based on custom event occurrences using a Delay until event happens action or an event enrollment trigger.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of a workflow. Or, learn how to create a new workflow.
  • To add a trigger:
    • In the workflow editor, click Set up triggers.
    • In the left panel, select When an event occurs. Set up the trigger, then click Apply filter.
    • To further refine your trigger, click Add refinement filters. You can select additional properties to refine the objects that you’d like to enroll in the workflow.
    • By default, records will only enroll in a workflow the first time they meet the enrollment triggers. To enable re-enrollment, under the Should [object] be re-enrolled in this workflow? section, select Yes, re-enroll every time the trigger occurs.
  • To add a delay:
    • In the workflow editor, click the + plus icon to add a workflow action.
    • In the right panel, select Delay until event happens.
    • Configure the delay:
      • Click the Event dropdown menu, then select a custom event.
      • Then, select the event property that you want to delay on.
      • Select the filter for the event property.
      • Click Apply filter.
      • Select the maximum wait time, or select the Delay as long as possible checkbox.
  • Click Save.

Please note: all event enrollment triggers will be separated using the OR operator. This means that only one of the event enrollment triggers must occur for the record to enroll in the workflow.

The workflow will then delay enrolled records until they meet the specified custom event criteria or will be triggered when the event occurs.

Track my custom event health and monitor delivery errors

To ensure your data remains accurate and your integrations are functioning as expected, you can use the Monitor tab within the Event Management tool.

Track performance in the custom event management tool
  • Completion trends: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Data Management > Event Management. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Data Management > Event Management directly. Click the Monitor tab to compare event completion volumes across different time periods.
  • Troubleshooting delivery errors: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Data Management > Event Management. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Data Management > Event Management directly. In the left sidebar of the Monitor tab, select Delivery errors. This table identifies events that failed to sync and provides the specific reason for the failure (e.g., mismatched data types or schema violations).
Resolve “Unknown Property” errors in the custom event management tool

If data is sent via API for a property that was never defined in HubSpot, it will appear in the error log. You can resolve this quickly:

  • Hover over the event in the Error logs table.
  • Click Actions, then select Add properties to event.
  • Confirm the suggested field types to allow HubSpot to begin accepting that data immediately.

Create custom events codelessly with the event visualizer

Custom events allow you to track information unique to your business. Clicked element and Visited URL events can be created without code.

A clicked element event tracks when an anonymous visitor or HubSpot contact clicks a specific element on your website. For example, track when a free demo CTA or PDF download link is clicked. Clicked element events can only be created and tracked on pages that have the HubSpot tracking code installed. Visited URL events record when an anonymous visitor or HubSpot contact visits a specific URL on your website.

A single Visited URL event can be set to track up to 30 different URLs, and a single Clicked Element event can be set up to track up to 30 different clicked elements.

Please note:

  • The instructions in this article are for the new custom events tool, which replaces the previous events tool. Any events created in the legacy tool will continue to work, and you can still manage and analyze those events in the legacy tool.
  • Legacy events cannot be migrated to the new events tool. Instead, it’s recommended to recreate your legacy events in the new tool, as new custom events provide more flexibility with event properties. For example, with legacy events you’d need to create multiple events to track separate campaigns, but now a single custom event can track multiple campaigns.

Once you’ve created your events, learn how to analyze events in the analytics and reporting tools. You can also create and manually track custom events.

Create codeless events

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Data Management > Event Management.

  • In the top right, click Create an event, and select Create custom event.

  • Select Use visualizer.

  • Click Next.

  • Enter your website URL then, click Done.

  • In the pop-up box, enter an Event name.

  • Select what type of event you want to create:

    • Visited URL: track visits to a web page.
    • Clicked element: track a page element that receives clicks.

  • If you selected Visited URL, enter a Tracking name, then click Next.

  • Tracking for that page is now set up. Click + Track another view to track another URL or click Done.

  • If you selected Clicked element:

    • Click the audienceTargeting target icon to choose a selector.
    • In the I’d like to track this on section, select where to track the clicked element; All websites with the tracking script, This domain, or This page.
    • Enter a Tracking name.

  • Click Next.

  • Tracking for that element is now set up. Click +Track another click to track another element or click Done.

HubSpot will then begin to track the element. Learn how to analyze the event in HubSpot.

Create custom signals

Summary

Custom signals allow you to define buyer intent triggers in plain language and identify companies that match those criteria — from hiring updates and RFP postings to product announcements.

You can automatically start or stop tracking custom signals based on buyer intent saved views, Target Account status, lifecycle stages, segments, and workflow actions. Automated tracking helps you apply custom signals to companies that meet your criteria while controlling custom signal credit usage with an account-level monthly limit.

Before you get started

Understand requirements

Please note the following:

  • To create or track custom signals, you need HubSpot Credits.
  • To track companies, you need Data Enrichment permissions.
  • To create, edit, or delete custom signals, you need Edit access within Buyer Intent permissions.
Understand limitations & considerations

Please note the following:

  • The company you want to track doesn’t require a domain. However, a domain can improve the accuracy and quality of the signals HubSpot detects.
  • HubSpot backfills matches from the last 90 days for companies you select to track.
  • Automated tracking for custom signals uses HubSpot Credits.
  • To control monthly usage, set an Action-level Limit for custom signal tracking.

Understand custom signals

A custom signal is a buyer cue that you define in plain language. HubSpot agentically researches the public web, such as company websites, articles, transcripts, posts, and filings, for matches against the companies you’re tracking. Each match is emitted as an event for the associated company.

Each detected signal includes:

  • The signal name you defined.
  • A summary of what was found, including why the signal was triggered.
  • Source citations, including the URLs that triggered the signal.
  • The signal date.

Tracking is configured per custom signal. When you create a custom signal, you select which companies it should monitor. This is independent of the companies you’re tracking for standard intent signals. HubSpot will backfill matches from the last 90 days for the companies you select.

Create a custom signal

To create a custom signal:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Buyer Intent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Buyer Intent directly.
  • Click the Signals tab, then click My signals.
  • Click Create custom signal.
  • Describe the signal in plain language. For example:
    • CISO hire: when a company hires a Chief Information Security Officer with a background in cybersecurity.
    • Agency growth: when an agency wins a large enterprise contract with a Fortune 1000 brand.
    • Data breach: when a company discloses a third-party data breach or supply chain vulnerability in the news.
    • Missed targets: when a company announces a missed earnings report that specifically cites sales execution or long sales cycles as the cause.
  • Review the prompt validation results. HubSpot indicates whether the prompt is likely to produce results.
  • Review the auto-preview, which shows sample matches against companies you already track. The auto-preview runs in the background and uses no credits.
  • Click Create signal.
  • Select the companies that the signal should monitor. Learn more about tracking companies for a custom signal.

Please note: HubSpot determines how often each signal refreshes based on the signal type. Signals refresh at least weekly. HubSpot also runs an initial scan when you track a new company for a custom signal.

Get portal-specific signal recommendations

If you’re not sure what to track, HubSpot can recommend custom signals based on your ideal customer profile and company information.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Buyer Intent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Buyer Intent directly.
  • Click the Signals tab.
  • Click My signals.
  • Under Recommended, review the suggested prompts.
  • Click View signal to review and edit a recommendation before creating it.

Track companies for a custom signal

Each custom signal has its own tracked-company list. After you create a custom signal, HubSpot prompts you to select which companies it should monitor. You can change the tracked-company list for any custom signal at any time.

Choose a source

In the tracking confirmation dialog box, select a source:

  • All companies in CRM: select specific company records or every company record in your CRM for this signal.
  • All tracked companies: select companies that are already monitored for standard intent signals or custom signals.
  • Companies in segments: select one or more existing company segments. Then, select specific companies from those segments or the entire segment.

Tip: check the TRACKING STATUS column in the modal table to see if a company is currently monitored and hover over the status to view which specific signals are actively tracking it.

After you select the companies to track, the signal begins scanning and HubSpot backfills matches from the last 90 days for the selected companies.

Automatically track custom signals

You can automatically start or stop tracking custom signals when companies meet specific criteria. In addition to manually selecting companies, you can automatically track custom signals from buyer intent saved views, Buyer Intent settings, and workflows.

Automatically track companies from a buyer intent saved view

When a company enters a saved view in the Visitors or Research tab, you can automatically track it for all active custom signals.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Buyer Intent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Buyer Intent directly.
  • On the Visitors or Research tab, create or select a saved view.
  • In the left sidebar menu, click a saved view from the dropdown menu, then select Add new companies.
  • If applicable, select the option to backfill companies that are already in the saved view.

Companies that enter the saved view will be tracked for active custom signals in addition to standard intent signals.

Automatically track companies from Buyer Intent settings

Use account-level rules to start or stop custom signal tracking based on company criteria.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Buyer Intent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Buyer Intent directly.
  • Click the Signals tab.
  • Click Automated Tracking.
  • Configure the rules for starting or stopping custom signal tracking.

You can start tracking when a company:

  • Is marked as a Target Account.
  • Enters a selected lifecycle stage, such as Lead or SQL.
  • Gains membership in one or more selected segments.

You can stop tracking when a company:

  • Enters a selected lifecycle stage, such as Customer.
  • Exits one or more selected segments.
Automatically track companies from workflows

Use workflow actions to start or stop tracking specific custom signals for enrolled companies.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Create or edit a company-based workflow.
  • Add the Track custom signals or Stop tracking custom signals action.
  • Select the custom signal or signals to track or stop tracking.
  • Configure the remaining workflow settings, then turn on the workflow.
Set a credit limit for custom signal tracking

Set a monthly credit limit to help control credit usage from automated custom signal tracking.

  • In your HubSpot account, click your account name in the top right corner, then click Account & Billing. Then, under Usage & Limits, select HubSpot Credits.
  • In the Manage usage by feature section, click Intent.
  • Set the limit for custom signal tracking.

The limit acts as a monthly account-level cap, regardless of how many custom signal automations are active.

Track companies for a custom signal

Each custom signal has its own tracked-company list. After you create a custom signal, HubSpot prompts you to select which companies it should monitor. You can change the tracked-company list for any custom signal at any time.

Choose a source

In the tracking confirmation modal, select a source:

  • All companies in CRM: pick some company records or every company record in your CRM for this signal.
  • All tracked companies: pick companies that are already monitored for standard intent signals or custom signals. This assists in applying a new custom signal across all existing tracked accounts.
  • Companies in segments: pick one or more existing company segments. Then, opt to track some companies from those segments, or the entire segment.

Tip: check the TRACKING STATUS column in the modal table to see if a company is currently monitored and hover over the status to view which specific signals are actively tracking it.

Once you select your companies to track, the signal begins scanning and HubSpot backfills matches from the last 90 days for the selected companies.

Track companies for a custom signal from other places in HubSpot

You can also start or stop tracking companies for a custom signal from the same locations you already track from for intent signal tracking:

  • From buyer intent, select companies on the Research or Visitors tab and click Track intent signals.
  • From the Intelligence tab or buyer intent CRM card of a company record, click Track signals on this company.
  • From a company segment or index, use the More dropdown menu and select Activate intent signals or use the row.
  • From a company import, select the Track for intent signals option in the post-import summary.

In any of these flows, the tracking confirmation modal includes a Signals dropdown menu that lists every signal type available for the selected companies. This includes standard signal categories alongside each of your active custom signals. Select which signals (including any custom signals) the companies should be tracked for, then confirm.

You can also start or stop tracking companies from the same locations where you track companies for intent signals:

  • From Buyer Intent, select companies on the Research or Visitors tab, then click Set up autotrack.
  • From the Intelligence tab or the Buyer Intent CRM card on a company record, click Track signals on this company.
  • From a company segment or index, use the More dropdown menu and select Activate intent signals, or use the row.
  • From a company import, select the Track for intent signals option in the post-import summary.

In these flows, the tracking confirmation dialog box includes a Signals dropdown menu that lists every signal type available for the selected companies. This includes standard signal categories and active custom signals.

View companies with custom signals

You can view custom signals from the Signals tab within Buyer Intent:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Buyer Intent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Buyer Intent directly.
  • To view detected custom signals across tracked companies, on the Signals tab, select one or more custom signals using the Signal type filter.
  • To track more companies with the same custom signal, find the signal in the table, click the three vertical dots icon, then click Track more companies in the pop-up box.
  • Select the companies to track.

To view details for a specific company, click the company name. The signal appears on the activity timeline of the company record alongside standard intent signals.

To view source citations, click to expand the signal event. Each cited URL is clickable.

Understand custom signal types and categories

All custom signals appear under the Custom signals category in Buyer Intent and downstream apps, including workflows, scoring, and segments.

When you use custom signals as workflow triggers or segment filters, they appear under the Custom signals category alongside standard intent signals.

Complete actions with custom signals

You can use custom signals anywhere standard intent signals are supported.

Use custom signals in segments

When creating a company segment, select a custom signal under the Event filter category to dynamically include companies that match the signal.

Use custom signals in workflows

You can trigger a workflow when a custom signal fires for a tracked company. You can also use workflows to start or stop tracking custom signals for enrolled companies.

Automatically set up a workflow
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Buyer Intent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Buyer Intent directly.
  • Click the Signals tab.
  • Click My signals.
  • Click the bell icon next to a signal.

This automatically opens a preconfigured workflow with internal email notifications populated with key signal metadata, including the company name, signal name, summary, and source URL.

Manually set up a workflow
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click Create workflow, then select From scratch.
  • Choose Company-based.
  • Select the Custom Signals trigger group.
  • Set your desired custom signal or signals as a trigger.
  • Add actions, such as assigning an owner, sending a notification, enrolling a company in a sequence, or updating properties.
Use custom signals in lead scoring

You can add custom signal events to a score group so that detected signals raise or lower a company’s score.

  • Open the score group that you want to edit.
  • Click + Add criteria, then select Event.
  • Select Custom signals, then choose the specific signal.
  • Assign a point value.
  • Click Save.

Manage custom signals

You can manage custom signals by editing, pausing, or deleting them.

Rename a custom signal
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Buyer Intent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Buyer Intent directly.
  • Click the Signals tab, then click My signals.
  • Find the signal, then click Edit.
  • Rename the signal.
  • Click Save.
Pause a custom signal

You can pause a custom signal for all tracked companies. HubSpot will stop scanning for that signal on those companies.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Buyer Intent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Buyer Intent directly.
  • Click the Signals tab, then click My signals.
  • Find the signal, then click the three vertical dots icon.
  • In the pop-up box, click Pause signal.

To resume a paused signal, repeat the steps above, then click Resume signal. In the dialog box, click Resume tracking.

Please note: resuming a signal consumes HubSpot Credits.

Delete a custom signal

Deleting a custom signal stops future scans for that signal. Historical signal events that were previously recorded remain on company record activity timelines and in the table on the Signals tab. These events can still be referenced in segments, workflows, and lead scoring.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Buyer Intent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Buyer Intent directly.
  • Click the Signals tab, then click My signals.
  • Click the edit icon, then click Delete.

Untrack companies for custom signals

You can review which companies are tracked for specific custom signals and stop tracking them from the Billing tab.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Buyer Intent. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Buyer Intent directly.
  • Click the Signals tab, then click My signals.
  • Click the Billing tab.
  • Click the Tracked for dropdown menu to filter companies by specific standard or custom signals.

To stop tracking companies:

  • Bulk untrack: select the checkboxes next to the companies, then click Untrack at the top of the table.
  • Individual untrack: next to a company, click the Signals dropdown in the row, such as 3 signals >, then click Untrack next to the signal you want to remove.

In the Stop tracking intent signals? dialog box, confirm which signals to remove, then click Update tracking.

Filter records with custom signals

When creating filter criteria for workflow triggers or segments, the following event is available for each active custom signal:

  • [Custom signal name] detected: the company matched the criteria defined in the signal prompt.

Each custom signal event includes the following filterable properties:

  • Signal date: when the match was detected.
  • Source URL: the citation or citations that triggered the signal.
  • Source summary: the text snippet that triggered the signal.

Define your data model with recommendations

You can apply data model recommendations that automatically create objects, properties, pipelines, and associations relevant to your industry. Using a recommendation, you can skip the manual work of setting up your data model and more efficiently and reliably track data in your CRM database. You can also generate data model recommendations with HubSpot’s AI.

If you don’t want to apply all elements of a recommendation, you can save them as a template, and apply the changes later.

Apply a recommendation with HubSpot’s AI

You can generate data model recommendations using HubSpot’s AI. This allows you to view object, association, pipeline, and property recommendations specific to your business needs. This means recommended relationships between records (e.g., contacts, services), custom properties to track desired data points (e.g., service offerings), and pipeline stages relevant to your business will be generated. If you need to make changes to the recommendations (e.g., rename a property or its values) or not include some elements, you can do so.

For example, you run a landscaping business. You may see the following recommendations: contacts and services as associations, custom pipeline stages for deals (e.g., negotiation, contract sent), or custom properties (e.g., a dropdown property displaying your service packages).

To generate a recommendation with HubSpot’s AI:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Data Management > Data Model. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Data Management > Data Model directly.
  • In the Build your data model with AI section:
    • Enter a prompt, then click Get data model recommendations now. (e.g., I own a coffee roastery that operates in the U.S. and am onboarding my sales and marketing teams to HubSpot.)
    • Generated recommendations will appear in Breeze Assistant.
    • You can review them, and apply or ask Breeze to save the template as a draft. The saved templates will be available on the same page for future use.
    • A banner will appear when the recommendation is applied successfully. To view more information about an object created or impacted by the recommendation, click the Settings link.
    • Once you’re finished, click Done.

Export HubSpot data to Amazon Redshift

Summary

Export HubSpot CRM objects, associations, and events to Amazon Redshift using the Amazon Redshift app in the HubSpot Marketplace. You can choose the data to export, configure a sync schedule, and monitor sync activity from HubSpot.

This article covers how to install and connect the app, configure a data export sync, and monitor or manage the sync.

Please note: if you’re a Super Admin, you can opt your account into the Improved Amazon Redshift Integration beta.

Before you get started

Understand requirements

Make sure you have the following:

  • An AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role connected to your HubSpot account and configured to access your AWS account.
  • An Amazon Redshift provisioned cluster or serverless workgroup that HubSpot can reach.
  • An Amazon S3 bucket for staging temporary Parquet files. The bucket must be in the same AWS Region as your Redshift cluster or serverless workgroup.
  • HubSpot copies temporary Parquet files to the configured Amazon S3 staging bucket and doesn’t delete them. To remove older files and manage storage costs, create an S3 lifecycle rule in your AWS account.
  • A Redshift administrator who can run a one-time SQL grant on the destination database.
  • Access to the HubSpot and AWS consoles. It’s recommended to open them in separate tabs.
Understand limitations and considerations
  • Each sync produces a full snapshot of the selected data.
  • Each sync replaces the destination table. Any table-level grants or settings added in Redshift aren’t preserved between syncs.
  • You control the amount of data exported by selecting which objects, associations, and events to include.
  • If a sync fails, the next scheduled sync automatically attempts the full sync again.

Install and connect the Amazon Redshift app

  • In the HubSpot App Marketplace, open the Amazon Redshift app listing.
  • Select the AWS role connected to your HubSpot account.
  • Click Install.
  • Click Next.
  • Create an AWS IAM role that’s connected to your HubSpot account and configured to access your AWS account.
  • Enter the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the role.
  • Click Connect to Amazon Redshift.

Configure your AWS role

HubSpot uses the connected AWS role to write temporary Parquet files to your S3 staging bucket and load the files into Redshift.

  • In the S3 bucket URL field, enter the URL of the S3 bucket that HubSpot will use to stage temporary Parquet files.

You can include a prefix in the URL to limit access to a specific path within the bucket. The bucket must be in the same AWS Region as your Redshift cluster or serverless workgroup.

Please note: HubSpot copies Parquet files to the configured S3 staging bucket by design and doesn’t delete them. Create an S3 lifecycle rule in AWS to automatically remove older files.

  • Select your Redshift deployment type from the dropdown menu:

    • Redshift Serverless
    • Provisioned cluster

  • Update the connected AWS role with the permissions policy for your deployment type:

    • Redshift Serverless: enter your workgroup ARN. HubSpot will generate a policy containing the ARN. Copy the policy and attach it to the connected AWS role.
    • Provisioned cluster: copy the policy template. Replace YOUR_REGION, YOUR_ACCOUNT_ID, YOUR_CLUSTER_ID, and YOUR_DATABASE with values from your AWS account, then attach the policy to the connected AWS role.

  • In AWS IAM, open the role connected to HubSpot.

  • Attach the generated permissions policy to the role, or create an inline policy with the policy content.

  • In the same AWS IAM role, update the trust policy with the statement generated by HubSpot.

HubSpot generates a different trust policy statement based on the Redshift deployment type you selected.

Associate the AWS role with Redshift

In Amazon Redshift, associate the same AWS role that you updated in the previous section with your Redshift setup.

  • Redshift Serverless: open the namespace configuration page for the namespace that you use with HubSpot. On the Security and encryption tab, click Manage IAM roles, then select Associate IAM roles.
  • Provisioned cluster: open your cluster, click Actions, and select Manage IAM roles > Associate IAM roles.

Grant Redshift permissions

  • In HubSpot, select the destination database.
  • Ask a Redshift administrator to run the SQL script in the selected database.

HubSpot uses this permission to create a schema for the destination during the sync.

  • Click Test connection.
  • If the connection test is successful, click Next.

Configure the data export sync

  • Select the data sources to export.
  • Select the objects, associations, and events tables to include.
  • Configure the sync frequency and start time.
  • Click Start sync.

Each sync run exports a full snapshot of the selected data to Amazon Redshift.

Monitor and manage the sync

From the sync details page, you can review the following information:

  • Sync status.
  • Last sync time.
  • Errors.
  • Sync activity.
  • Sync history.

To open the sync details page:

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Data Management > Data Integration.
  • On the App Syncs tab, search for Amazon Redshift app syncs.
  • Click the Amazon Redshift sync you want to review.

From the sync details page, you can also perform the following actions:

  • Click Pause to pause the sync.
  • Click Archive to archive the sync.
  • Click Sync now to manually start a sync.

Sync statuses

Status

Description

Syncing

A sync run is in progress.

Synced

The most recent sync run completed successfully.

Failed

The most recent sync run encountered an error.

Archived

The sync configuration was archived or removed.

Resolve sync failures

When a sync fails:

  • The sync displays a Failed status in HubSpot.
  • Per-table details show which tables succeeded or failed.
  • The next scheduled sync automatically attempts the full sync again.
  • You can click Sync now to manually start another sync.

Export HubSpot data to PostgreSQL or MySQL

Please note: if you’re a Super Admin, opt your account into the Data Studio beta to use this feature.

HubSpot Credits required for certain features syncing data directly from a single warehouse source in Data Studio to the HubSpot CRM doesn’t consume HubSpot Credits. If you prepare the data in Data Studio before syncing (for example, by creating calculated fields or joining it with other data sources), those actions consume HubSpot Credits.

Summary

Use Data Out to export selected HubSpot CRM data to a PostgreSQL or MySQL database that you manage. You can sync object, association, and event data to tables in your database, then query the data with SQL or use it with your business intelligence and analytics tools.

Each sync creates a full snapshot of the selected data. When a sync succeeds, it replaces the previous snapshot in the destination tables.

Before you get started

Understand requirements
  • Your PostgreSQL or MySQL database must be reachable from the HubSpot IP ranges for your account region.
  • Your database server must support SSL connections.
  • You must have a database user with the required permissions:
    • PostgreSQL: CREATE permission and write access to the target schema.
    • MySQL: CREATE permission on the database and write access.
  • Make sure your database user can create tables and write data.
  • Keep your HubSpot account and database consoles open in separate tabs.
Allow HubSpot IP addresses

Add the HubSpot IP range for your account region to your database server’s allowlist.

Region

IP range

NA1

54.174.62.128/26

EU1

143.244.87.0/25

AP1

216.157.42.32/27

NA2

216.157.40.32/27

NA3

216.157.41.32/27

Understand limitations and considerations
  • Each sync run creates a full snapshot of the selected data.
  • A successful sync replaces the previous snapshot in the destination tables.
  • HubSpot doesn’t retain previous snapshots.
  • If a table fails during a sync, its previous data remains available until the next successful sync.
  • Each object type, event type, or association pair can be included in one recurring PostgreSQL sync and one recurring MySQL sync per account.
  • Each sync replaces the destination table. Table-level grants or settings added in your database provider aren’t preserved between syncs.
  • If you reconnect using a different database user, you must grant that user access to existing HubSpot-managed schemas, databases, or tables.

Connect HubSpot to PostgreSQL or MySQL

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Data Management > Data Studio. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Data Management > Data Studio directly.
  • In the top right, click Connect external data source.
  • In the Add a data source panel, search for or browse to the database provider.
  • Click PostgreSQL or MySQL.
  • Enter the database connection details:
    • Host
    • Port
    • SSL
    • Username
    • Password
  • For PostgreSQL, enter the name of the database where HubSpot should create the schema.
  • Click Connect to PostgreSQL or Connect to MySQL.

HubSpot uses the connected database user to create tables and load data into your database.

Configure the sync

  • Select the data sources to export:
    • Objects
    • Associations
    • Events
  • Select the objects, properties, associations, or events to include.
  • Choose how often to run the sync and when to start it.
  • Click Start sync.

The available sync frequencies may vary during the beta. Options can include once, every 6 hours, every 12 hours, daily, weekly, or monthly.

Access your exported data

HubSpot creates a HubSpot-managed schema or database for each destination.

PostgreSQL

PostgreSQL tables use the following format:

<database>.hubspot_data_out_<destination-id>.<table-name>

For example:

your_database.hubspot_data_out_456."OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES"
your_database.hubspot_data_out_456."EVENTS_VISITED_PAGE"
your_database.hubspot_data_out_456."ASSOCIATIONS_CONTACTS_TO_COMPANIES"
MySQL

MySQL tables use the following format:

hubspot_data_out_<destination-id>.<table-name>

For example:

hubspot_data_out_456.OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES
hubspot_data_out_456.EVENTS_VISITED_PAGE
hubspot_data_out_456.ASSOCIATIONS_CONTACTS_TO_COMPANIES

You can find the exact schema or database name on the sync configuration page.

Table and column names

Table and column names are based on the exported data. PostgreSQL identifiers can contain up to 63 characters. MySQL identifiers can contain up to 64 characters. Longer names are shortened to fit the applicable limit.

HubSpot creates PostgreSQL tables and columns with quoted, case-preserved names. When querying PostgreSQL, use double quotation marks and match the capitalization shown in the table name and column name.

For MySQL, use backticks and match the capitalization shown. Table-name case sensitivity can vary depending on your MySQL server configuration.

Column types

Exported type

PostgreSQL

MySQL

String

Number, 64-bit

BIGINT

DATETIME(6)

Boolean

BOOLEAN

TINYINT(1)

Decimal

NUMERIC

DECIMAL

The PROPERTIES column in the OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES table is stored as a JSON-formatted string. It’s stored as TEXT in PostgreSQL and LONGTEXT in MySQL, not as a native JSON column type.

Monitor your sync

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Data Management > Data Integration. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Data Management > Data Integration directly.
  • On the left, click App Syncs.
  • Search for or select the PostgreSQL or MySQL sync.

From the sync details page, you can view the sync status, last sync time, errors, sync activity, and sync history. You can also pause, archive, or manually run the sync.

Sync statuses

Status

Description

Syncing

A sync run is currently in progress.

Synced

The last sync run completed successfully.

Failed

The last sync run encountered an error.

Archived

The sync configuration was archived or removed.

Resolve sync failures

When a sync fails:

  • The HubSpot UI shows a Failed status and table-level details indicating which tables succeeded or failed.
  • A table is updated only after HubSpot finishes loading all of its data.
  • If a table fails, its previous data remains in place until the next successful sync.
  • The next scheduled sync automatically attempts the full sync again.
  • You can manually run a sync from the sync details page.

Tables that succeeded during an earlier run aren’t modified when a later run fails.

FAQs

How do I query the exported data?

Query the tables in the destination schema or database with SQL.

PostgreSQL
-- Read all contact records
SELECT *
FROM your_database.hubspot_data_out_456."OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES"
WHERE "OBJECTTYPEID" = '0-1';

-- Read a property from the PROPERTIES column
SELECT
  "OBJECTID",
  json_extract_path_text("PROPERTIES"::json, 'email') AS email
FROM your_database.hubspot_data_out_456."OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES"
WHERE "OBJECTTYPEID" = '0-1';
MySQL
-- Read all contact records
SELECT *
FROM `hubspot_data_out_456`.`OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES`
WHERE `OBJECTTYPEID` = '0-1';

-- Read a property from the PROPERTIES column
SELECT
  `OBJECTID`,
  JSON_EXTRACT(`PROPERTIES`, '$.email') AS email
FROM `hubspot_data_out_456`.`OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES`
WHERE `OBJECTTYPEID` = '0-1';
Can I export one data type in multiple syncs?

Each object type, event type, or association pair can be included in one recurring PostgreSQL sync and one recurring MySQL sync per HubSpot account.

For example, if contacts are already exported to a recurring PostgreSQL destination, you can’t add contacts to another recurring PostgreSQL configuration until you archive the first configuration. You can still export contacts to a recurring MySQL configuration at the same time.

Are object-specific tables supported?

Object-specific tables, such as OBJECTS_CONTACTS, aren’t currently supported. Use OBJECT_WITH_OBJECT_PROPERTIES and filter by OBJECTTYPEID to retrieve records for a specific object type.

Is Sensitive Data supported?

Sensitive Data isn’t currently supported for Data Out. Sensitive properties may be excluded from exports.

Does HubSpot keep previous snapshots?

No. Each successful sync replaces the destination table with the latest snapshot. HubSpot doesn’t retain previous snapshots.

If a table fails during a sync, its previous data remains in place until that table is successfully updated.

Does HubSpot use a staging bucket that I manage?

No. HubSpot exports the data as Parquet and manages staging internally. You don’t need to provide a customer-owned staging bucket for PostgreSQL or MySQL.

What happens if I change the database user?

If you reconnect using a different database user, you must grant the new user access to existing HubSpot-managed schemas, databases, or tables.

Maintain a trusted source of customer data

To grow your business, your teams need one central place where customer data is accurate and reliable. By establishing proactive data cleanup strategies, enforcing solid governance, and ensuring team-level ownership visibility, you can maintain clean data and drive seamless collaboration across your entire organization.

The steps below outline processes and suggested best practices for admins governing CRM data in HubSpot, from setting up schema permissions and automated ingestion to monitoring data health and aligning team ownership.

Permissions required Super Admin permissions or Data quality tools access are required to use these features.

Subscription required An assigned seat is required for specific advanced pipeline and team settings.

Define a clear data model and governance strategy

Maintaining a single trusted source of data begins with a strong data foundation and strict guardrails surrounding data creation and modification.

  • Map your data schema: use the data model builder to map standard objects, custom objects, properties, and direct association logic to reflect exactly how your business operates.
  • Govern with field-level permissions: set view and edit permissions for critical CRM properties, protecting essential fields from unauthorized edits.
  • Enforce strict validation rules: configure properties with strict formatting rules, enumeration fields, and unique IDs to maintain standardization.
  • Secure Sensitive Data: group and secure sensitive property fields using application-layer encryption and restricted view access to stay compliant.

For example, Sprocket Supply Co. wants to make sure support agents don’t accidentally override customer industry categories. They use field-level editing permissions to restrict property edits to CRM administrators and operations teams, while keeping it view-only for general staff.

Consolidate and automate data ingestion

To keep a database clean, you must control the data that enters it. Set up automated pathways that continuously add and enrich information without adding user friction like duplicate information or manual data entry.

  • Use data sync and REST APIs: keep your external billing, go-to-market (GTM), and back-office applications connected with HubSpot via native two-way sync integrations.
  • Activate data enrichment: automatically enrich incomplete contact and company records using verified third-party source data and conversational insights.
  • Filter spam and form submissions: protect incoming form data by turning on invisible CAPTCHAs and gibberish detection settings to filter spam out of the CRM.
  • Integrate personal and team channels: connect phone call integrations, shared inboxes, and scheduling tools so records stay automatically updated with historical touchpoints.

For example, Sprocket Supply Co. wants to stop fake email addresses and spam form submissions from cluttering up their contact list. They turn on invisible CAPTCHAs and strict spam-filtering on their website forms, while using data enrichment to automatically fill in legitimate details (like company size and country) without asking users to type it in.

Monitor and resolve data quality issues

Data decay is inevitable, but monitoring it should not be manual. Use the HubSpot data quality overview page to track, report, and fix data health issues automatically.

  • Audit the data quality overview page: regularly check the data quality overview page to locate duplicate records, formatting issues, and integration failures.
  • Deduplicate and format with AI: detect and merge duplicate contacts and companies, and apply rules to resolve formatting issues automatically.
  • Archive unused properties and workflows: track property fill rates and unused workflows to archive and deprecate outdated CRM data.
  • Set up a weekly data quality digest: configure notification settings to receive a weekly email summary of new record creation, formatting issues, and duplicate alerts on Monday mornings.

For example, Sprocket Supply Co. wants to stop typos, incorrect capitalizations, and duplicate contacts from skewing their analytics. They use the data quality overview page to automatically fix capitalization issues in contact names, then schedule a digest email at the beginning of each week so their lead database administrator can see which duplicate profiles were merged over the weekends.

Align team ownership and visibility

A clean database is only valuable if your team knows how to use it together. Establish clear alignment, automated assignment, and ownership transparency.

  • Establish account basics and organization structure: set up your multi-account management, brand settings, and system defaults to match your company’s hierarchy.
  • Configure teams and permission sets: group users into standard teams and assign tool permissions so everyone only has access to the tools they need to do their jobs.
  • Automate ownership and SLA routing: use workflows to auto-assign and route incoming records to the correct teams, and set SLA guidelines for “at risk” work visibility.
  • Log shared context and cross-record associations: standardize your CRM activity feeds, comment threads, and explicit object-to-object associations to keep relevant data connected and preserve historical context.
  • Implement conditional pipeline stages: enforce stage transitions by learning how to set up and customize pipelines with conditional stage properties, and ensure seamless handoffs by setting up pipeline rules.

For example, Sprocket Supply Co. wants to ensure a seamless handoff when a prospective lead buys a plan and moves from sales to onboarding. They set up conditional pipeline rules so sales reps are required to fill out a “Customer Setup Notes” property before a deal can be moved to “Closed Won.” This triggers an automated workflow that reassigns the record to the onboarding team and creates a task with a clear 48-hour SLA deadline.

Measure data quality and team alignment

Use these key metrics to continuously measure the quality of your CRM database and the effectiveness of your team alignment.

Metric

Definition

Actions to improve performance

CRM record fill rate

Percentage of required properties populated on standard CRM objects.

Review custom property names, simplify layouts, and require fields on pipeline stage transitions.

Deduplication rate

Percentage of duplicate contact and company records successfully resolved.

Turn on automated duplicate matching inside the data quality overview page and apply deduplication rules.

Formatting issue resolution

Speed and volume of fixing misformatted names, phone numbers, or emails.

Set up automated formatting validation workflows and turn on standard formatting rules in the data quality overview page.

Unused workflow and property ratio

The proportion of total workflows or properties that are flagged as inactive or unused.

Use the data quality overview page Property Insights to identify low-impact properties and archive or deprecate them.

SLA miss rate

Percentage of escalated records or customer handoffs that miss the established team SLA.

Build workflows with auto-escalation alerts and construct real-time dashboards to track “at-risk” records.

Glossary and resources

  • Data quality overview page: a centralized dashboard displaying metrics on property health, record duplicates, integrations, and workflow issues.
  • Field-level permissions: a security setting allowing Super Admins to manage who can edit or view specific data fields.
  • Sensitive Data properties: specialized property types with application-layer encryption to safely store permitted regulated information.
  • Handoff rules: process requirements embedded into pipeline settings to ensure standardized information is gathered before a deal or ticket is passed to another team.
